In several products, free membership covers community participation (public events, groups, feeds) while paid tiers unlock one-to-one depth — browsing more profiles, initiating more conversations, accessing private spaces. The community is the open layer; intimate contact is the monetized layer.

### Commercial use may be restricted

Some products prohibit commercial use of community surfaces and refuse advertising outright, on the argument that advertiser interests conflict with member safety; third-party organizations may be admitted only when acting in members' interests. Postures differ across the type.

### Moderation is two-layered

Published community guidelines govern content and conduct; report/block machinery routes violations to moderation teams; escalation processes handle harassment and safety issues. In products with member organizers, moderation extends to reviewing new activities and collecting attendee feedback.
leaves.rules_zh:
### 联系门槛是可选的——这正是重点所在

与约会应用不同，在约会应用中，产品中介的门槛是定义性的，而在这里，门槛是一种设计选择。抽样产品涵盖了整个范围：聊天前的双向同意匹配；强制验证后的开放消息；订阅门槛消息。一致的是，信任由社区背景——验证、可见参与、审核——产生，而非仅由门槛产生。

### 验证通常先于通信

一些产品要求身份或资格验证，社区优先的产品可能在验证完成前锁定通信。这同时充当资格门槛（例如，特定年龄段的社区）和反欺诈层，通常被呈现为社区的核心安全机制。

### 可见参与充当声誉

在社区密集型产品中，会员的历史——参加的活动、加入的群组、贡献的讨论——可被他人阅读，并作为信任信号发挥作用。一些产品明确陈述这一点：在社区中的行为构成会员地位的一部分，这使得社区成为诈骗者和虚假档案的敌对领域。

### 会员创建的活动通常是非官方的

当会员组织聚会时，平台通常声明不承担运营责任：活动属于组织者，出席规则属于组织者，平台提供推广、回复邀请工具和安全指南，而非监管。针对组织者和参与者的责任指南是这一规则的书面配套文件。

### 会员等级限制深度，而非归属感

在一些产品中，免费会员涵盖社区参与（公共活动、群组、动态流），而付费等级解锁一对一

leaves.name: Daycare / Preschool Management
leaves.overview:
A **Daycare / Preschool Management** application is operator-side software for running a daycare center or preschool — a licensed early-childhood business that holds other people's children in care for a substantial part of the day. It keeps the operator's system of record: which children are enrolled and under whose authority, which children are present right now and with whom they may leave, what happened during each child's day, what the staff covered, and what the family (or a subsidy payer) owes.

The defining core is small:

```text
Guardian/family account
└── Enrolled child (ongoing care enrollment)
    ├── Daily attendance recorded as custody events (check-in / check-out by authorized adults)
    └── Care-day documentation shared with guardians
```

Everything else commonly bundled with these products — classrooms with ratio monitoring, tuition autopay, subsidy billing, waitlists, parent apps, curriculum and progress reporting — is standard capability layered onto that loop to make it workable in a licensed, revenue-collecting business.

When the software instead matches families with individual caregivers, it is a Babysitting Marketplace; when the programs it manages are scheduled part-day sessions around the school day, it is After-school Program Management; when those sessions become seasonal and consecutive-day, it is a Camp Management System.
leaves.overview_zh:
一个**日托/幼儿园管理**应用程序是运营方软件，用于运行日托中心或幼儿园——一个持牌的早期儿童业务，在一天中大部分时间照顾他人的孩子。它维护运营方的记录系统：哪些孩子已注册并受谁监护、哪些孩子当前在场以及他们可以与谁离开、每个孩子的一天中发生了什么、工作人员覆盖了什么、以及家庭（或补贴支付方）欠款。

定义的核心很小：

```text
监护人/家庭账户
└── 已注册的孩子（持续护理注册）
    ├── 每日出勤记录为监护事件（由授权成人签入/签出）
    └── 护理日文档与监护人共享
```

与这些产品通常捆绑的其他一切——具有比例监控的教室、学费自动支付、补贴账单、候补名单、家长应用、课程和进度报告——都是标准功能，叠加到该循环上，使其在持牌、收费业务中可行。

当软件改为将家庭与个人护理人员匹配时，它是一个保姆市场；当它管理的项目是围绕学日的预定半天课程时，它是课后项目管理；当这些课程变为季节性和连续日时，它是一个营地管理系统。
leaves.dc:
```text
Guardian/family account
  └── Enrolled child (ongoing care enrollment)
        ├── Daily attendance: check-in / check-out (custody events by authorized adults)
        ├── Care-day documentation (meals · naps · toileting · activities · photos · notes · incidents)
        └── Tuition ledger (charges · payments · subsidies)
Rooms / classrooms (children + staff assigned; capacity + ratio)   [center settings]
Staff records & schedules ──┘
```
leaves.dc_zh:
监护人/家庭账户
  └── 入托儿童（持续护理登记）
        ├── 每日考勤：签到/签出（授权成人的监护事件）
        ├── 护理日文档（餐食·午睡·如厕·活动·照片·笔记·事件）
        └── 学费账本（费用·支付·补贴）
房间/教室（儿童+员工分配；容量+比例）   [中心设置]
员工记录与日程 ──┘
leaves.rules:
- **Custody is the gate.** A child leaves only with an authorized adult. Products maintain per-child authorized-pickup lists and can block check-in attempts by anyone else; some capture signatures because licensing authorities may treat the event as the custody record.
- **Attendance is the load-bearing record.** The same event feeds live ratios, attendance-based tuition, subsidy reporting, and the licensing attendance history, so errors propagate — which is why batch corrections and audit views exist.
- **Enrollment is ongoing, and history is retained.** Children move through statuses rather than re-registering per term; departed children's records are archived, not deleted, because licensing requires historical attendance and enrollment records.
- **Rooms bound capacity and ratio.** Room assignment is what makes ratio monitoring possible; going out of ratio is an alertable compliance event, and staffing plans are checked against child schedules room by room.
- **Money has multiple parties.** Tuition may be split between the family and a subsidy payer; the ledger must track who owes what, post agency payments separately, and handle co-pays and adjustments without disturbing the family balance.
- **Documentation has visibility classes.** Not every logged entry is family-visible: internal entries are staff-only, and some products route family-visible posts through administrator approval.
- **Roles are stratified.** Administrators see money and compliance; teachers see their room's children and feeds; guardians see only their own children; approved pickups and emergency contacts see custody functions but not the child's feed.
- **The day is logged in the moment.** Documentation and custody events are captured as care happens; the record is meant to reflect the day, not be reconstructed later.
- **Learning records are documentation, not academic records.** Observations and progress reports describe development; they are not grades, transcripts, or promotion decisions — the care operator is not the child's school of record.
leaves.rules_zh:
- **监护是门槛。** 孩子只能与授权成人一起离开。产品维护每个孩子的授权接人列表，并可以阻止任何其他人的签入尝试；有些捕获签名，因为许可机构可能将该事件视为监护记录。
- **出勤是承载记录。** 同一事件为实时比例、基于出勤的学费、补贴报告和许可出勤历史提供数据，因此错误会传播——这就是为什么存在批量更正和审计视图。
- **注册是持续的，历史被保留。** 孩子通过状态移动，而不是每个学期重新注册；已离开孩子的记录被归档，而不是删除，因为许可要求历史出勤和注册记录。
- **房间绑定容量和比例。** 房间分配使比例监控成为可能；超出比例是一个可警报的合规事件，人员配备计划根据孩子时间表逐个房间检查。
- **资金涉及多方。** 学费可能在家庭和补贴支付方之间分摊；账簿必须跟踪谁欠什么，单独记录机构付款，并处理共付额和调整，而不影响家庭余额。
- **文档有可见性类别。** 并非每个记录的条目都对家庭可见：内部条目仅工作人员可见，有些产品将家庭可见的帖子路由到管理员批准。
- **角色是分层的。** 管理员查看资金和合规性；教师查看他们房间的孩子和动态；监护人只看到他们自己的孩子；批准的接人和紧急联系人具有监护功能，但看不到孩子的动态。
- **一天实时记录。** 文档和监护事件在护理发生时被捕捉；记录旨在反映当天，而不是事后的

leaves.name: DDoS Protection Platform
leaves.overview:
A **DDoS Protection Platform** is an availability-defense application for internet-facing services. It binds itself to a defined set of protected assets — network prefixes, IP addresses, applications, or DNS infrastructure — continuously evaluates the traffic arriving at those assets for signs of a distributed denial-of-service attack, and executes countermeasures in the traffic path (absorbing, filtering, dropping, rate-limiting, challenging, or diverting attack traffic) so that the protected service remains available to legitimate users.

The defining core is deliberately small and is the same regardless of where the product is deployed:

```text
Protected traffic surface (identified assets the platform takes responsibility for)
└── Standing attack detection (continuous evaluation → identified attack events)
    └── Traffic-path mitigation execution (absorb / filter / drop / rate-limit / divert)
        └── Availability objective (keep the service up under volumetric, protocol, and application-layer flooding)
```

Everything else commonly associated with these products — machine-learned traffic profiles, managed rule catalogs, dashboards and reports, human response teams, tiered pricing, WAF integration — makes the protection practical but does not define what the product is. Detection without mitigation is network monitoring; enforcement without standing detection is just a firewall; the same machinery pointed at request content rather than traffic volume is a WAF.
leaves.overview_zh:
一个**DDoS防护平台**是面向互联网服务的可用性防御应用。它将自身绑定到一组定义好的受保护资产——网络前缀、IP地址、应用程序或DNS基础设施——持续评估到达这些资产的流量中是否存在分布式拒绝服务攻击的迹象，并在流量路径中执行缓解措施（吸收、过滤、丢弃、速率限制、挑战或重定向攻击流量），以确保受保护的服务对合法用户保持可用。

其定义的核心是刻意精简的，并且无论产品部署在何处都保持一致：

```text
受保护流量面（平台负责的已识别资产）
└── 持续攻击检测（持续评估 → 已识别攻击事件）
    └── 流量路径缓解执行（吸收 / 过滤 / 丢弃 / 速率限制 / 重定向）
        └── 可用性目标（在容量型、协议型和应用层洪泛攻击下保持服务运行）
```

与这些产品通常关联的所有其他方面——基于机器学习的流量画像、托管规则集、仪表板和报告、人工响应团队、分级定价、WAF集成——使防护变得实用，但并未定义产品本身。没有缓解的检测只是网络监控；没有持续检测的执行仅仅是一个防火墙；针对请求内容而非流量容量的相同机制则是一个WAF。
leaves.dc:
Four structures, held together. Remove any one and the product stops being this Type.

**Protected traffic surface.** The platform starts with an explicit statement of what it protects: specific IP ranges, public IPs, application endpoints, DNS infrastructure, or whole networks. This binding is what turns generic traffic machinery into *someone's* protection — the platform takes responsibility for those assets, reports on them individually, and applies per-asset policies. Without it, the product is generic network tooling.

**Standing attack detection.** The platform continuously evaluates arriving traffic against a body of detection knowledge: known attack signatures and vectors (floods of SYN, ACK, UDP, ICMP; reflection and amplification techniques; DNS query floods and water torture; HTTP floods; slow-read attacks; protocol abuse), volume thresholds, and learned baselines of what normal traffic looks like for each protected asset. When traffic crosses into attack territory, the platform records an identified **attack event** — with the affected asset, the attack vector(s), and its progress over time. Without standing detection, a device that merely forwards or absorbs traffic (a load balancer, a CDN) is not a protection platform.

**Traffic-path mitigation execution.** The platform does not stop at alerting: it executes — or automatically orchestrates — countermeasures on the path the attack traffic takes. The action spectrum includes dropping or filtering malicious packets, absorbing floods in high-capacity infrastructure, rate-limiting aggressive sources, issuing challenges to suspected bot clients at the application layer, closing abusive connections, and diverting traffic that exceeds local capacity to cloud scrubbing systems. Without execution, the product is a monitoring or alerting tool.

**Availability objective.** The success criterion is that the legitimate user can still reach the service while the attack runs. This is what separates the Type from content-security products: the adversary being countered is *volume and state exhaustion* — traffic that may be individually valid-looking but is collectively destructive — not exploit payloads or policy violations. The platform's rules are judged by availability outcomes (did the service stay up; were legitimate users spared), not by whether a policy matched.
leaves.dc_zh:
四种结构，相互依存，移除任一则产品不再是此类型。

**受保护流量面。** 平台首先明确声明其保护的对象：特定IP范围、公网IP、应用程序端点、DNS基础设施或整个网络。这种绑定关系将通用流量处理设备转化为对特定主体的保护——平台对这些资产负责，进行单独报告，并实施资产级策略。若无此特性，该产品仅为通用网络工具。

**持续攻击检测。** 平台持续依据检测知识库评估入站流量：已知攻击签名与向量（SYN、ACK、UDP、ICMP洪泛；反射与放大技术；DNS查询洪泛与水刑攻击；HTTP洪泛；慢速读取攻击；协议滥用）、流量阈值，以及对各受保护资产正常流量模式的自学习基线。当流量进入攻击范畴时，平台记录已识别的**攻击事件**——包含受影响资产、攻击向量及其随时间推移的演变过程。若无持续检测功能，仅转发或吸收流量的设备（如负载均衡器、CDN）并非防护平台。

**流量路径缓解执行。** 平台不止于警报：它执行——或自动编排——流量路径上的反制措施...
leaves.rules:
### Mitigation is threshold-gated

Mitigation actions fire when detection knowledge decides traffic has crossed into attack territory — a threshold, a signature match, or a baseline deviation. Below the threshold, attack-shaped traffic may pass. This is deliberate: over-blocking harms availability, so products err toward documented, adjustable trigger points rather than unconditional filtering. Users who need different behavior adjust sensitivity or thresholds per rule — and inherit the false-positive risk they create.

### Baselines require observation time

Detection is strongest for assets the platform has observed under normal conditions. Several products state minimum observation periods before events are reported with full accuracy, and behavioral profiling improves with history. A newly enrolled asset gets signature- and threshold-based protection immediately, but its behavioral layer matures over time.

### The protection provider's own survival comes first

Enforcement points are shared infrastructure. When attack traffic is large enough to threaten the protection system itself, mitigation happens regardless of customer preferences — customers who set rules to "off" or "log-only" still see extreme traffic mitigated. This is a structural behavior of any shared enforcement point, not a policy nicety.

### Coverage follows where the platform sits

A protection platform covers the layers at which it operates. Network-layer-native products protect L3/4 and reach L7 through a bundled engine or through explicit WAF integration; edge reverse-proxy products protect their own protocol surface downward. L7 availability defense frequently requires the customer to attach a WAF to the protected resource — the DDoS platform either enforces it or manages it on the customer's behalf.

### The appliance complements upstream protection

On-premises enforcement is positioned to catch what upstream defenses pass through — small or short attacks below upstream thresholds, attacks that bypass a CDN by targeting the origin directly, state-exhaustion attacks aimed at the customer's own middleboxes — rather than to replace ISP, CDN, or cloud protection. Cloud-scrubbing arrangements integrate the two: local enforcement detects a volumetric attack it cannot absorb and signals the cloud layer to divert and scrub.

### Validate before enforcing

Because a misfiring protection rule is itself an availability incident, the mature posture is log-first: observe what a rule flags before letting it block, lower sensitivity until legitimate traffic is spared, and use the application's own health signals to confirm real impact. Some vendors add their own pre-enforcement checks to catch misfiring new rules before customers are affected.
leaves.rules_zh:
### 缓解受阈值门控

缓解措施在检测知识判定流量已跨入攻击领域时触发——一个阈值、一个签名匹配或一个基线偏差。低于阈值时，具有攻击形态的流量可能会被放行。这是有意为之：过度阻塞会损害可用性，因此产品倾向于采用有记录的、可调整的触发点，而非无条件过滤。需要不同行为的用户根据规则调整灵敏度或阈值——并承担其产生的误报风险。

### 基线需要观察时间

对于平台在正常条件下观察过的资产，检测能力最强。多个产品声明了在事件以完全准确度报告前所需的最短观察期，并且行为画像会随历史数据积累而改善。新注册的资产会立即获得基于签名和阈值的防护，但其行为层会随时间成熟。

### 防护提供方的自身生存优先

执行点是共享基础设施。当攻击流量大到足以威胁防护系统本身时，无论客户偏好如何，缓解都会发生——即使客户将规则设置为“关闭”或“仅记录日志”，仍然会看到极端流量被缓解。这是任何共享执行点的结构性行为，而非策略上的考量。

### 覆盖范围跟随平台位置

防护平台覆盖其操作的层级。网络层原生产品保护L3/4，并通过内置引擎或明确的WAF集成达到L7；边缘反向代理产品保护其自身的协议表面向下。L7可用性防御通常要求客户将WAF附加到受保护资源——DDoS平台要么执行它，要么在客户的边界管理它。

leaves.name: Deal Desk / Commercial Approval Platform
leaves.name_zh: 交易管理平台/商业审批平台
leaves.overview:
A **Deal Desk / Commercial Approval Platform** is the selling organization's cross-functional commercial approval center: the system of record where deals that depart from the organization's standing commercial terms are reviewed, decided, and authorized.

Most deals in a selling organization follow standard terms — standard prices, standard discounts, standard contract language. A defined minority do not: an unusually large discount, a custom payment structure, a non-standard clause, an atypical bundle. These exceptions carry real margin, legal, and compliance risk, and no single function can judge them alone. The deal desk exists to close that gap: it holds the organization's commercial policy, receives the deals that depart from it, convenes the functions whose judgment is needed, records the decision, and authorizes the deal to proceed on the excepted terms.

The defining core is small:

```text
Deal exception of record
  └── judged against
Standing commercial policy (guardrails / thresholds / pre-approved terms)
  └── decided by
Cross-functional review with recorded, attributable decisions
  └── retained as the
Authorization record that lets the deal proceed downstream
```

Everything else commonly associated with deal desk software — dashboards, parallel approval chains, delegation, in-app collaboration, AI summaries, quote building, clause libraries — is standard capability that mature products add, not what makes the product a deal desk. The same is true of packaging: in today's market the deal desk most often ships as a capability inside a CPQ or revenue suite rather than as a standalone product; standalone deal-desk platforms exist but are fewer.

Two boundary clarifications follow from the research. First, the deal desk is not the quote: CPQ computes and holds the quote, and may embed simple discount-approval gates; the deal desk is the policy and review layer above it. Second, "deal desk" is also used in the market for the *buying* organization's software-procurement negotiation support — that is a different kind of product serving a different operator, and it is not covered by this Type.
leaves.overview_zh:
一个**交易台/商业审批平台**是销售组织的跨职能商业审批中心：它是记录那些偏离组织标准商业条款的交易并进行审查、决策和授权的记录系统。

销售组织中的大多数交易都遵循标准条款——标准价格、标准折扣、标准合同语言。少数交易则不然：异常大的折扣、定制化的付款结构、非标准条款、非典型捆绑包。这些例外情况带来了真实的利润、法律和合规风险，且没有任何单一职能能够独自判断。交易台的存在就是为了弥合这一差距：它持有组织的商业政策，接收偏离该政策的交易，召集需要其判断的职能，记录决策，并授权交易以例外条款继续推进。

其定义性核心很小：

```text
交易例外记录
   └── 对照
标准商业政策（护栏/阈值/预批准条款）
   └── 由
跨职能审查决定，具有记录在案且可追溯的决策
   └── 保留为
允许交易向下游推进的授权记录
```

通常与交易台软件相关联的其他所有内容——仪表盘、并行审批链、授权委托、应用内协作、AI摘要、报价构建、条款库——都是成熟产品添加的标准功能，而非使该产品成为交易台的原因。包装方式也是如此：在当今市场，交易台通常作为CPQ或收入套件内的功能发布，而非作为独立产品；独立交易台平台存在，但数量较少。

研究得出了两个边界澄清。首先，交易台不是报价：CPQ计算并持有报价，并可能嵌入简单的折扣审批门；交易台是其上方的政策和审查层。其次，“交易台”在市场上也用于*采购*组织的软件采购谈判支持——那是服务于不同操作者的另一类产品，本类型不涵盖此类产品。
leaves.dc:
- **Deal desk dashboard / queue** — real-time visibility into quote progress, approval status, and deal momentum across the desk's caseload.
- **Approval chain machinery** — parallel and sequential workflows, approver groups, and routing driven by the organization's structure; some products add advance-notice previews for pending approvers.
- **Delegation and reassignment** — ways to keep reviews moving when a designated reviewer is unavailable, such as reassignment to a teammate or team-based approver groups.
- **Light-touch approval participation** — one-click approvals and notifications delivered where reviewers already work (email, chat).
- **Exception intake inside the selling flow** — the seller requests the exception from within the quote, rather than through a separate form.
- **Collaboration on the deal record** — mentions, comments, and internal discussion attached to the deal, replacing scattered email threads.
- **Automatic propagation of approved terms** — an approved discount or term updates the quote or agreement without manual re-entry.
- **Desk metrics** — approval cycle time, deal cycle time, deal size, win rate, and margin, used to find bottlenecks and tune policy.
- **CRM integration** — the deal's context (account, opportunity, history) flows in from the CRM, and outcomes sync back.
- **AI assistance** (era-current) — summaries that highlight critical deal terms for approvers, clause scanning on attachments, and conversational deal guidance for sellers.
leaves.dc_zh:
1. 交易桌面仪表板/队列——实时查看报价进度、审批状态和整个桌面案件负载中的交易动态。
2. 审批链机制——基于组织结构的并行和顺序工作流、审批者组和路由；一些产品为待审批者添加预先通知预览。
3. 委托和重新分配——当指定审查者不可用时保持审查继续的方法，例如重新分配给团队成员或基于团队的审批者组。
4. 轻触式审批参与——一键审批和通知发送到审查者已工作的位置（电子邮件、聊天）。
5. 销售流程内的异常接入——卖方从报价内部请求异常，而不是通过单独的表单。
6. 交易记录协作——提及、评论和内部讨论附加到交易上，替代分散的电子邮件线程。
7. 已批准条款的自动传播——批准的折扣或条款更新报价或协议，无需手动重新输入。
8. 桌面指标——审批周期时间、交易周期时间、交易规模、成功率和利润率，用于发现瓶颈和调整政策。
9. CRM集成——交易的上下文（账户、机会、历史记录）从CRM流入，结果同步回。
10. AI辅助（当前时代）——摘要突出关键交易。
leaves.rules:
### In-policy deals bypass the desk

The policy layer's most important behavior: deals within guardrails proceed without any review. The desk is for exceptions. A deployment where every deal requires approval has either misconfigured policy or no policy.

### Decisions are attributable and retained

Every approve/reject/counter is recorded against a named reviewer, with the deal's terms and the decision's basis retained. This is the audit trail that makes non-standard selling governable — and it is why the desk is a system of record rather than a meeting.

### Approval changes the deal record

When an exception is approved, the authorized terms propagate into the quote or agreement automatically. Sellers do not re-key approved discounts; the deal that goes to the customer is the deal that was authorized.

### Authority is layered

Policy typically grants sellers a band of commercial freedom (discounts up to a threshold, pre-approved clauses only) and routes everything beyond it upward. The thresholds, and who must approve above them, are organizational policy expressed in the system — they vary substantially between organizations and products.

### The desk authorizes; it does not own the quote

The quote or agreement remains the selling system's object (CPQ's or the CRM's). The desk's object is the review and its authorization. Products blur this by bundling quote-building into the desk platform, but the division of labor — compute the offer vs. authorize its exceptions — is the structural seam.

### Reviews must not stall

Delegation, reassignment, team-based approvers, reminders, and light-touch approval surfaces all exist for one reason: a stalled exception is a stalled deal. Cycle-time pressure is the desk's defining operational constraint.
leaves.rules_zh:
### 符合政策的交易绕过交易台

政策层最重要的行为：在护栏范围内的交易无需任何审查即可推进。交易台是为例外情况设立的。如果部署中每笔交易都需要审批，则要么政策配置错误，要么根本没有政策。

### 决策可追溯且被保留

每个批准/拒绝/反提议都记录在具名审查者名下，并保留交易的条款和决策依据。这是使非标准销售可治理的审计轨迹——这也是交易台是记录系统而非会议的原因。

### 审批改变交易记录

当例外被批准时，授权条款自动传播到报价或协议中。销售人员无需重新录入已批准的折扣；发送给客户的交易即为已授权的交易。

### 权限是分层的

政策通常赋予销售人员一定范围的商业自由（折扣不超过阈值、仅限预批准条款），并将超出部分向上路由。阈值以及谁必须批准超出部分，是系统中表达的组织政策——它们在不同组织和产品之间差异巨大。

### 交易台授权；但不拥有报价

报价或协议仍是销售系统的对象（CPQ或CRM的）。交易台的对象是审查及其授权。产品通过将报价构建捆绑到交易台平台中来模糊这一界限，但分工——计算报价 vs. 授权其例外——是结构性接缝。

### 审查不得停滞

授权委托、重新分配、基于团队的审批者、提醒和轻量级审批界面都存在，原因只有一个：停滞的例外即停滞的交易。周期时间压力是交易台定义性的运营约束。

leaves.name: Deal Discovery Platform
leaves.overview:
A **Deal Discovery Platform** is a consumer application whose unit of record is the **deal** — a time-limited saving opportunity (a price drop, coupon code, cash back rate, sale, or freebie) at an external merchant. It collects deals from many independent merchants into one place, surfaces them through discovery surfaces (feeds, categories, store pages, alerts), and hands the shopper off to the merchant to redeem the offer.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Deal (time-limited saving opportunity at an external merchant)
└── aggregated across many merchants
    └── discovered through deal-centric surfaces (feed / categories / stores / alerts)
        └── redeemed at the merchant (link-out, code, or activation)
```

The platform itself never sells: it holds no catalog, takes no order, and processes no payment for goods. Its role is to know about saving opportunities the shopper didn't set out to find, keep them current, and route the shopper to them. Everything else commonly associated with the category — community voting, editorial verification, browser extensions, cash back wallets, price-drop alerts, personalized feeds — is widespread in current products but is not what makes the product a deal discovery platform.
leaves.overview_zh:
一个**优惠发现平台**是一种消费者应用程序，其记录单元是**优惠**——即在外部商家处限时提供的节省机会（如降价、优惠券码、返现比例、促销或免费赠品）。它将来自众多独立商家的优惠汇集到一处，通过发现界面（信息流、分类、商店页面、提醒）将其呈现出来，并将购物者引导至商家处以兑换优惠。

其定义性结构很小：

```text
优惠（在外部商家处限时提供的节省机会）
└── 跨多个商家聚合
     └── 通过以优惠为中心的界面发现（信息流 / 分类 / 商店 / 提醒）
         └── 在商家处兑换（链接跳转、代码或激活）
```

平台本身从不销售：它不持有目录，不接收订单，也不处理商品支付。其角色是了解购物者未主动寻找的节省机会，保持其时效性，并将购物者引导至这些机会。通常与该类别相关的其他所有内容——社区投票、编辑验证、浏览器扩展、返现钱包、降价提醒、个性化信息流——在当前产品中很普遍，但这并不是使该产品成为优惠发现平台的原因。
leaves.dc:
Four properties. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as a deal discovery platform:

- **The deal as unit of record** — a discrete, time-limited saving opportunity at a merchant: what's on offer (discount, code, cash back rate, sale, free item), at which merchant, under what terms, valid until when. Deals are often store-wide or category-wide rather than tied to one product. Without this, the product is a product catalog or shopping search.
- **Multi-merchant aggregation** — deals from many independent merchants collected in one place, organized by merchant, category, and season. Without this, it's a single store's own promotions page.
- **Discovery surface over deals** — the shopper finds deals without a query: a recency- or popularity-ordered feed, category and store browsing, seasonal pages, and alerts. Without this, it's a database nobody browses.
- **Redemption handoff to the merchant** — the loop ends by sending the shopper to the merchant: a tracked outbound link, a coupon code to apply, or a cash back offer to activate before shopping. Without this, it's a deals-themed media site with no working path — or, if the platform itself sold the offer, a marketplace.
leaves.dc_zh:
四个属性。如果移除任何一个，该产品将不再被识别为优惠发现平台：
1. 交易作为记录单位 — 在商家处的一个离散、限时的省钱机会：提供什么（折扣、代码、返现率、促销、免费物品），在哪个商家，根据什么条款，有效至何时。交易通常是店铺范围或类别范围的，而不是针对单个产品。没有这一点，该产品就是产品目录或购物搜索。
2. 多商家聚合 — 来自多个独立商家的交易收集在一个地方，按商家、类别和季节组织。没有这一点，它就是单个商店自己的促销页面。
3. 交易发现表面 — 购物者无需查询即可发现交易：按时间或流行度排序的提要、类别和商店浏览、季节性页面和警报。没有这一点，它就是没人浏览的数据库。
4. 兑换移交给商家 — 循环通过将购物者发送到商家而结束：一个跟踪的出站链接、一个要应用的优惠代码，或一个在购物前激活的返现优惠。没有这一点，它就是一个以交易为主题的媒体网站，没有工作路径——或者，如果平台本身出售该优惠，则是一个市场。
leaves.rules:
### Deals expire — and expiry is visible

A deal is a time-limited event. Mature products treat expiration as a managed state: expired deals are marked, surfaced ("expired deals" sections), or filtered — not silently erased. A deal that looked great yesterday may be gone today; the platform's value depends on keeping this honest.

### Validity is often conditional

Many deals carry restrictions — membership requirements, limited inventory, regional limits, price-match dependence. Community-driven products have an explicit label for "works, but your mileage may vary" deals, and structured reasons for downvoting (couldn't replicate, wrong price, wrong merchant). Verification machinery exists precisely because deals fail in the field.

### Cash back must be activated before the purchase

In cash back variants, the reward is earned only if the offer was activated and the purchase happened through the platform's tracked path. Shopping at the merchant directly, without activation, earns nothing. Purchases typically appear as "pending" until the merchant confirms them, and payout is subject to the platform's schedule and minimum-balance rules (which vary by product).

### The platform routes, never sells

The platform holds no inventory and processes no payment for goods. Every redemption path terminates at the merchant. This is the structural line between this Type and a marketplace or voucher seller.

### Monetization is merchant-side and disclosed

The consumer side is free; the platform earns commissions from merchants when shoppers route through it. Promoted placements are labeled as such in mature products. In cash back variants, part of the commission is shared back to the shopper — which is the platform's stated reason for being free.

### Community curation is a governance rule, not a feature

In community-driven products, prominence is earned: votes (with structured negative reasons) determine what rises, editors validate what reaches the frontpage, and members can report problems. The vote is simultaneously a ranking mechanism and a quality-control system.
leaves.rules_zh:
### 优惠会过期——且过期是可见的

优惠是一个限时事件。成熟产品将过期视为一种受管理状态：过期优惠被标记、展示（“过期优惠”部分）或过滤——而不是静默删除。昨天看起来很好的优惠今天可能已经消失；平台的价值取决于保持这种诚实。

### 有效性通常是条件性的

许多优惠带有限制——会员要求、有限库存、区域限制、价格匹配依赖。社区驱动的产品对“有效，但效果因人而异”的优惠有明确标签，以及结构化的反对理由（无法复制、价格错误、商家错误）。验证机制的存在正是因为优惠在现场会失败。

### 返现必须在购买前激活

在返现变体中，只有当优惠被激活且购买通过平台的跟踪路径发生时，奖励才会赚取。直接在商家处购物而不激活，什么都赚不到。购买通常显示为“待处理”，直到商家确认，支付受平台计划和最低余额规则约束（因产品而异）。

### 平台路由，从不销售

平台不持有库存，也不处理商品支付。每个兑换路径都在商家处终止。这是此类型与市场或代金券销售者之间的结构界限。

### 货币化在商家端且已披露

消费者端免费；当购物者通过平台路由时，平台从商家赚取佣金。在成熟产品中，推广位置被标记为推广。在返现变体中，部分佣金返还给购物者——这是平台声称免费的原因。

### 社区策划是一种治理

leaves.name: Deal Management for Private Equity / VC
leaves.overview:
A **Deal Management application for Private Equity / VC** is the investment firm's front-office system of record for its deal flow: it holds each prospective investment as a persistent deal record, moves it through pipeline stages the firm defines, links it to the companies and people involved, and accumulates the firm's history of interactions, notes, and decisions — from first sighting of a target through sourcing, evaluation, and the invest-or-pass decision.

It solves a specific problem: an investment firm's most valuable working assets are its pipeline of opportunities and its network of counterparties, and both must outlive any individual deal, spreadsheet, or employee's inbox. The defining core is deliberately small — deal records, firm-defined pipeline stages, counterparty records, and persistent history. Everything else commonly associated with modern products (relationship intelligence, auto-captured email and calendar activity, market-data enrichment, analytics dashboards) is widespread but not what makes the product this Type.
leaves.overview_zh:
一款面向私募股权/风投的 **交易管理应用** 是投资公司前台业务的核心记录系统，用于管理其交易流：它将每个潜在投资作为一条持久的交易记录进行保存，使其沿公司定义的流程阶段推进，关联相关的公司与人员，并积累公司从发现目标、搜寻、评估到投资或否决决策全过程的互动、笔记和决议历史。

它解决了一个特定问题：投资公司最有价值的营运资产是其机会管线和交易对手方网络，这两者都必须比任何单个交易、电子表格或员工的收件箱更具持久性。其定义性的核心部分有意保持精简——即交易记录、公司定义的流程阶段、交易对手方记录和持久化历史。其他通常与现代产品相关的功能（关系智能、自动捕获的邮件和日历活动、市场数据丰富、分析仪表板）虽然普遍存在，但并非使其成为此类产品的核心要素。
leaves.dc: A persistent, identified record for a prospective investment — a company, a funding round, a buyout target, or another transaction the firm might pursue. It carries the firm's own attributes: pipeline stage, owner, and typically amounts and dates (deal size, expected close) where relevant. The deal record is the center of the workflow; everything else attaches to it.
leaves.dc_zh: 一个持久的、标识化的潜在投资记录——一家公司、一轮融资、一个收购目标，或公司可能追求的另一笔交易。它携带公司自身的属性：管道阶段、所有者，以及通常相关的金额和日期（交易规模、预期关闭时间）。交易记录是工作流程的中心；其他所有内容都附加其上。
leaves.rules:
- **Stages are firm-defined, not universal.** Each firm (and often each pipeline list within a firm) configures its own stage vocabulary; the system enforces the sequence the firm designs, not an industry standard.
- **The pipeline is the shared state.** Stage changes made by one team member are immediately visible to all; the board/table views are the coordination mechanism for the whole deal team.
- **Passed is a first-class outcome.** Deals end in an invested or passed disposition, and passed records are kept — the pipeline is also the firm's memory of what it declined.
- **Counterparty records persist across deals.** The same company or person appears in many deals over the years; deduplication and record merging are ongoing data-quality concerns, especially where records are auto-created from email sync.
- **Confidentiality is structural.** Sensitive deals can be restricted so that only authorized firm members see them, even inside a shared pipeline; permission models distinguish firm-wide visibility from deal-level restriction.
- **Auto-captured data needs curation.** Where email/calendar sync creates records automatically, duplicates and misattributions occur; products provide merge and review tooling, and firms adopt conventions (required fields, triggers) to keep the record trustworthy.
leaves.rules_zh:
- **阶段是公司定义的，而非通用的。** 每家公司（甚至公司内的每个流程管线列表）都会配置自己的阶段术语表；系统执行的是公司设计的序列，而非行业标准。
- **流程管线是共享状态。** 一个团队成员所做的阶段更改会立即对所有人可见；看板/表格视图是整个交易团队的协调机制。
- **“否决”是一级结果。** 交易以“已投资”或“已否决”的处置方式结束，且被否决的记录会被保留——流程管线也是公司记忆其否决过的项目的工具。
- **交易对手方记录跨交易持久存在。** 同一家公司或同一个人可能在多年间的许多交易中出现；去重和记录合并是持续的数据质量挑战，尤其是在记录从邮件同步自动创建的情况下。
- **机密性是结构性的。** 敏感交易可以被限制，使得只有授权的公司成员才能看到，即使在共享的流程管线内部也是如此；权限模型区分公司范围的可见性和交易级别的限制。
- **自动捕获的数据需要人工管理。** 在邮件/日历同步自动创建记录的情况下，会出现重复和错误归因的问题；产品提供合并和审核工具，而公司则采用规范（必填字段、触发器）来保持记录的准确性。

leaves.name: Dealer / Distributor Commerce Portal
leaves.name_zh: 经销商/分销商商务门户
leaves.overview:
A **Dealer / Distributor Commerce Portal** is an ordering portal operated by an upstream seller — typically a manufacturer or brand — for its own channel partners: the dealers, distributors, and resellers who buy the seller's products and resell them downstream.

Its purpose is to replace phone, fax, and email ordering with 24/7 partner self-service, while keeping the seller in control of its distribution channel. The defining structure is small:

```text
Seller (manufacturer / brand)
└── Portal for its channel partners
    └── Per-partner account
        ├── Partner-specific pricing and catalog visibility
        └── Partner-initiated orders
            └── Into the seller's fulfillment pipeline
```

Everything else commonly associated with these portals — order approval gates, rebates and channel programs, marketing asset libraries, partner onboarding, integrated payments — is widespread in current products but is not what makes the product a dealer/distributor portal.
leaves.overview_zh:
一个**经销商/分销商商务门户**是由上游卖方（通常是制造商或品牌）为其自身的渠道合作伙伴（即购买卖方产品并向下游转售的经销商、分销商和转售商）运营的订购门户。

其目的是用全天候的合作伙伴自助服务取代电话、传真和电子邮件订购，同时让卖方保持对其分销渠道的控制。其定义性结构很小：

```text
卖方（制造商/品牌）
└── 为其渠道合作伙伴提供的门户
     └── 每个合作伙伴的账户
         ├── 合作伙伴特定的定价和目录可见性
         └── 合作伙伴发起的订单
             └── 进入卖方的履行管道
```

通常与这些门户相关联的其他所有内容——订单审批关卡、返利和渠道计划、营销资源库、合作伙伴入职、集成支付——在当前产品中很普遍，但这并不是使该产品成为经销商/分销商门户的原因。
leaves.dc:
Three structures held together by one binding — the partner relationship:

```text
Seller's channel program
└── Partner account (dealer / distributor)
    ├── Partner-specific commercial terms
    │   ├── Pricing (contract rates, volume tiers, discounts)
    │   └── Catalog visibility (which products this partner may see and order)
    └── Partner-initiated order
        └── Flows into the seller's order / fulfillment pipeline
```

- **Seller-operated partner-facing venue.** The portal belongs to the upstream seller and is branded for it. The logged-in customer is a reselling business, not an end consumer. Without this, the product is just a B2B storefront.
- **Per-partner account with partner-specific commercial terms.** Each partner is a persistent account. What the partner sees and pays is a function of its account: negotiated contract pricing, volume tiers, and a catalog scoped to what that partner is authorized to sell (by tier, region, or exclusive line). Without this, the product is an anonymous wholesale site.
- **Partner-initiated ordering into the seller's pipeline.** The partner composes orders — browse, cart, reorder from history — and the submitted order enters the seller's own order/ERP pipeline for fulfillment. Without this, the product is a partner-communication site with no commerce.
leaves.dc_zh:
一个绑定条件维系的三方结构——合作伙伴关系：

卖方渠道计划
└── 合作伙伴账户（经销商/分销商）
    ├── 合作伙伴专属商务条款
    │   ├── 定价（合同价格、数量阶梯、折扣）
    │   └── 商品目录可见范围（该合作伙伴可见并可订购的产品）
    └── 合作伙伴发起的订单
        └── 流入卖方订单/履约管道

- **卖方运营的面向合作伙伴的场所。** 该门户属于上游卖方，并以其品牌呈现。登录的客户是转售企业，而非终端消费者。若缺乏此要素，产品将仅是一个B2B店面。

- **拥有合作伙伴专属商务条款的每伙伴独立账户。** 每个合作伙伴是一个独立持续账户。合作伙伴所见及所付价格取决于其账户：协商的合同定价、数量阶梯，以及限定于该合作伙伴授权销售范围（按等级、区域或独家产品线）的商品目录。若缺乏此要素，产品将是一个匿名的批发网站。

- **合作伙伴发起订单并流入卖方管道。** 合作伙伴可组合订单——浏览、购物车、从历史记录中重新订购——提交的订单将进入卖方自身的订单/ERP管道进行履约。若缺乏此要素，产品将是一个无商务功能的合作伙伴沟通网站。
leaves.rules:
### What a partner sees is a function of its account

Pricing and catalog visibility are per-partner, not public. Two partners logging into the same portal can see different prices and different product sets. This is the structural privacy/access surface of the Type.

### Self-service does not necessarily mean uncontrolled

Some products make a seller-side review-and-approve gate the headline behavior: no order ships until the seller approves it. Others run straight-through into fulfillment. Both are in-type; the approval gate is a policy choice of the seller, not a defining structure.

### The portal is not the books of record

Approved orders flow into the seller's ERP/accounting system; inventory and pricing flow out of it. The portal is an ordering and visibility layer over the seller's back office.

### The partner is a reseller, not the end consumer

Orders are wholesale-channel transactions between the seller and its distribution network. The end customer of the partner is out of scope of the portal.
leaves.rules_zh:
### 合作伙伴看到的内容是其账户的函数

定价和目录可见性是每合作伙伴的，不是公开的。两个登录同一门户的合作伙伴可以看到不同的价格和不同的产品集。这是该类型的结构性隐私/访问面。

### 自助服务不一定意味着不受控制

一些产品将卖方端的审查和批准关卡作为头条行为：在卖方批准之前，没有订单发货。其他产品直接运行到履行。两者都在类型内；审批关卡是卖方的政策选择，而不是定义性结构。

### 门户不是记录账簿

批准的订单流入卖方的 ERP/会计系统；库存和定价从中流出。门户是卖方后台之上的订购和可见性层。

### 合作伙伴是转售商，不是最终消费者

订单是卖方与其分销网络之间的批发渠道交易。合作伙伴的最终客户不在门户范围内。

leaves.name: Debt Collection Management
leaves.overview:
A **Debt Collection Management** application is the system of record for a professional debt recovery operation — a collection agency, debt buyer or debt servicer, collection law firm, or recovery unit that pursues debt on behalf of others. Its subject matter is debt the operator did not originate and does not hold through an ongoing customer relationship: accounts placed with it by creditor clients, or portfolios it has acquired outright.

The defining core is deliberately small:

```text
Creditor client (or acquired portfolio)
  ↓ lists / places / sells
Placed or purchased debt account (per debtor)
  ↓ accumulates
Recorded pursuit (contacts, tracing, promises, plans, payments, legal steps)
  ↓ closes in
Recovery outcomes → paid/settled → remit & report to client · payment plan → monitor ·
legal/judgment · recalled/returned to client · uncollectible
```

Everything commonly associated with modern collection software — AI work queues, propensity-to-pay scoring, digital self-service portals, dialers, bureau reporting, compliance tooling — is widespread in current products but is not part of the defining core. Paper-era agencies and 1980s PC-era packages satisfy the same core with ledger cards, commission statements, and remittance checks.

When the pursued debt sits on the operator's own book and the operator still owns the customer relationship (early-stage arrears treatment of one's own borrowers), the product is a different Application Type — Collections Platform. When the pursued population is open trade invoices of one's own B2B customers, it is Collections Automation. Debt Collection Management begins where the debt has left that first-party relationship: charged off, placed out, or sold.
leaves.overview_zh:
一款 **债务催收管理** 应用是专业债务追偿业务的系统记录核心——该业务面向催收机构、债务购买者或债务服务商、催收律所，或代表他人追讨债务的追偿部门。其业务对象并非由运营者自行发起、也非通过持续客户关系持有的债务：即由债权人客户委托的账户，或其完全收购的资产组合。

其定义性核心被刻意精简：

```text
债权人客户（或收购的资产组合）
  ↓ 委托/放置/出售
委托或购买的债务账户（按债务人划分）
  ↓ 累积形成
记录在案的催收行动（联系、追踪、承诺、计划、付款、法律步骤）
  ↓ 最终结果
追回结果 → 已付/已和解 → 向客户汇款及报告 · 分期付款计划 → 监督 ·
法律/判决 · 召回/退还客户 · 无法追讨
```

与现代催收软件相关的常见功能——人工智能工作队列、付款倾向评分、数字化自助服务门户、自动拨号器、征信局报告、合规工具——在当前产品中已广泛普及，但它们并非定义性核心的一部分。纸质时代的催收机构与1980年代的PC软件包，同样使用账页卡片、佣金报表和汇票来满足这一核心需求。

当被追讨的债务记在运营者自身的账上，且运营者仍保有客户关系时（例如对自身借款人进行的早期逾期处理），该产品属于另一种应用类型——催收平台。当被追讨对象是自有B2B客户的未结算贸易发票时，则属于催收自动化。债务催收管理始于债务脱离第一方关系之时：已核销、已委托外包或已出售。
leaves.dc:
- **Work queues and assignment** — accounts prioritized and distributed to collectors; strategy-based routing; performance-visible queues. Current products increasingly use AI scoring (propensity to pay, best channel/time, suggested arrangements) to drive these queues.
- **Tracing and data services** — locating debtors whose contact data has gone stale: bureau data, contact enrichment, asset and bankruptcy verification; in North America, furnishing account status to credit bureaus on behalf of clients is a standard service capability.
- **Outreach machinery** — letters with batch printing and mail-house integration, SMS/email, dialer integration for high-volume calling, increasingly conversational channels.
- **Payment capture and allocation** — multi-method payments, allocation across balances and charge types, settlements, and consumer self-service payment portals.
- **Client-facing reporting and portals** — per-client scoped reporting; secure data exchange with creditors; in mature products, self-service client portals showing status, balances, and progress on exactly the accounts the client owns.
- **Legal and asset machinery** — judgment/lien/asset records, legal-cost tracking, e-filing integration, attorney-network management, repossession and remarketing where debts are secured.
- **Compliance machinery** — jurisdiction-aware contact rules and guardrails built into workflows, dispute handling, and the audit trail behind them.
- **Analytics** — liquidation and success-rate reporting per client and per portfolio, collector performance, strategy effectiveness.
leaves.dc_zh:
- **工作队列与分配** — 账户按优先级分配给催收员；基于策略的路由；绩效可视的队列。当前产品越来越多地使用 AI 评分（还款倾向、最佳渠道/时间、建议方案）来驱动这些队列。
- **追踪与数据服务** — 定位联系信息已失效的债务人：征信局数据、联系信息增强、资产与破产核查；在北美，代客户向征信局提供账户状态信息是标准服务能力。
- **外联机制** — 批量打印与邮件服务集成的信件、短信/电子邮件、用于大规模呼叫的拨号器集成，以及日益普及的对话式渠道。
- **收款与分配** — 多种支付方式、跨余额和费用类型的分配、结算，以及消费者自助支付门户。
- **面向客户的报告与门户** — 按客户范围定制的报告；与债权人进行安全数据交换；在成熟产品中，提供自助客户门户，展示客户所拥有账户的状态、余额及进度。
- **法律与资产机制** — 判决/留置权/资产记录、法律成本跟踪、电子归档集成、律师网络管理，以及有抵押债务的收回和转售。
- **合规机制** — 在工作流程中内置司法管辖区感知的联系规则和防护措施。
leaves.rules:
### The operator is not the creditor

Payments collected belong, after the operator's compensation, to the creditor client. The system therefore tracks two money perspectives simultaneously: the account's balance (what the debtor owes) and the client's position (what is held for, earned from, and remitted to the client). Getting this separation wrong is not a bookkeeping nuisance; it is the structural difference from first-party collections.

### Placement is reversible

Accounts are held on behalf of clients, not absorbed into the operator's book. Recall and return are normal, first-class transitions — a client may pull an account back for its own servicing, another agency, or litigation. Systems treat recall as an outcome state, not a data delete.

### Per-client configuration cascades

How a client's accounts are worked, lettered, reported, and remitted is determined by the client's terms. In well-established products, the client record's settings propagate into account behavior by default — which is why misconfigured client setup is treated as an operational hazard, not a cosmetic issue.

### The treatment history is the evidence

Contact rules for debt collection are regulated and vary by jurisdiction, and disputes are routine. The auditable per-account history — what was attempted, promised, agreed, and paid — is the operation's defense and its memory. Mature products build compliance guardrails into the workflow and keep the trail complete.

### Outcomes generate work; closure is earned

A promise suspends pursuit until it lapses; a plan generates a monitoring schedule; a legal referral opens its own cost-and-progress track; a recall ends the agency's work but must preserve the record for the client. Accounts do not quietly disappear — every state change is explicit.
leaves.rules_zh:
### 运营者并非债权人

催收的款项在扣除运营者佣金后，属于债权人客户。因此，系统必须同时追踪两个资金视角：账户的余额（债务人所欠金额）与客户的立场（为客户持有的、赚取的及汇付给客户的金额）。将这两者混淆并非记账上的麻烦，而是与第一方催收在结构上的根本区别。

### 委托是可逆的

账户是代客户持有，而非并入运营者的账簿。召回与退还属于常规的、一等公民式的状态转换——客户可能为自身服务、委托另一家机构或进行诉讼而撤回某个账户。系统将召回视为一种结果状态，而非数据删除。

### 客户配置逐级生效

客户账户的处理方式、信函发送、报告和汇付均由客户条款决定。在成熟的软件产品中，客户记录的设置默认会传播至账户行为——这就是为什么错误的客户配置被视为操作风险，而非表面问题。

### 处理历史即证据

债务催收的联系规则受监管且因辖区而异，争议也属常态。可审计的每账户历史记录——尝试过什么、承诺了什么、约定了什么、支付了什么——是该运营的辩护依据和记忆。成熟的产品将合规保障措施内置于工作流中，并保持完整的记录轨迹。

### 结果产生工作；结案需争取而来

承诺会暂停催收直至其到期；付款计划会生成监督日程；法律转介会开启独立的成本与进度跟踪；召回终止了机构的工作，但必须为客户保留记录。账户不会悄无声息地消失——每一次状态变更都有明确记录。

leaves.name: Debt Management Application
leaves.overview:
A **Debt Management Application** is a person-side application for getting out of debt. It holds a person's own debts as individual liability records, builds a repayment plan that allocates a stated repayment capacity across those debts, and tracks actual repayment against that plan until each debt is retired.

The defining core is small:

```text
The user's own debts as liabilities of record
└── A repayment plan over those debts (order + allocation of repayment capacity)
    └── Repayment tracked against the plan
        (payments recorded → balances updated → progress surfaced → plan adjusted)
```

Everything else commonly associated with the category — named payoff strategies like "snowball" and "avalanche", month-by-month schedules, what-if scenarios, reminders, bank sync, credit-score features, or administration by a counseling agency — is a widespread realization of one of these three structures or a layer around them, not part of what makes the application what it is. A person with a paper ledger, a written payoff order, and a payment log is doing the same job; a spreadsheet that only prints a schedule is doing less (and is recognizably a calculator, not a debt management application).

The user is always the debtor. When the system's subject is other people's debts being pursued by an organization, the product belongs to a different family entirely (collection and servicing software).
leaves.overview_zh:
一款 **债务管理应用程序** 是一款面向个人的、旨在帮助其摆脱债务的应用程序。它将个人自身的债务记录为单个负债记录，制定一个将既定还款能力分配到这些债务上的还款计划，并持续跟踪实际还款情况与计划的对比，直至每笔债务清偿完毕。

其定义的核心是精简的：

```text
用户自身的债务作为负债记录
└── 针对这些债务的还款计划（顺序 + 还款能力的分配）
    └── 根据计划跟踪还款情况
        （记录付款 → 更新余额 → 显示进度 → 调整计划）
```

通常与该类别相关的所有其他功能——诸如“雪球法”或“雪崩法”等命名的还款策略、月度还款计划表、假设情景模拟、提醒、银行账户同步、信用评分功能，或由咨询机构管理——都是这三种结构中某一种的普遍实现方式，或是在其之上构建的附加层，而非构成该应用程序本质的部分。一个使用纸质账簿、手写还款顺序和付款日志的人，也在做着同样的工作；一个仅能打印计划表的电子表格所做的事情则更少（并且它显然只是一个计算器，而非债务管理应用程序）。

用户始终是债务人。当系统涉及的主体是某个组织在追讨的其他人的债务时，该产品则完全属于另一个类别（催收与服务软件）。
leaves.dc:
**1. The debts of record.** Each debt is a persistent, individually addressable record: who is owed, the current balance, and the payoff-relevant terms — the interest rate and the minimum payment. Debts can be of many kinds (credit cards, loans, medical bills — anything with a balance and a payment). This record is what makes the application about debt *management* rather than about spending: an expense is a past event, a debt is a living liability with a retirement date to be engineered.

**2. The repayment plan.** The plan is the organizing object. It has two inputs and one output:

- the debts of record,
- the **repayment capacity** — one stated amount available per month (the sum of the minimums plus whatever extra the person can afford),
- the **ordering** — which debt is targeted with the extra payment first, and where each freed payment goes next.

The plan's output is a schedule: for each debt, when it will be paid off; for the whole, a projected debt-free date and total interest. The ordering may be a named strategy (lowest balance first, highest interest first, cash-flow-oriented, or fully custom) or an agency-structured allocation; conceptually it is the same thing — a rule that decides where the next dollar of extra payment goes.

**3. The tracking loop.** Payments (or program deposits) are recorded as they happen. Recording updates the debt's balance and due date, advances the schedule, and moves the progress picture: which debts are paid off, how far along the active ones are, and how the projected completion date has moved. The plan is then adjusted — the ordering can be changed, the capacity revised, extra or reduced payments recorded — and the loop repeats monthly until nothing is left.

All three are needed together. A calculator without payment recording and progress is below this Type; a liability list without a plan is a net-worth view; a schedule without the debts behind it is a generic planner.
leaves.dc_zh:
1. 记录的债务。每个债务是一个持久、可单独寻址的记录：欠谁、当前余额、以及与还清相关的条款——利率和最低还款额。债务可以有多种类型（信用卡、贷款、医疗账单——任何有余额和付款的东西）。这个记录使得应用程序关注的是债务*管理*而非消费：支出是过去的事件，债务是活生生的负债，有一个需要设计的退休日期。

2. 还款计划。计划是组织对象。它有两个输入和一个输出：
- 记录的债务，
- 还款能力——每月可用的一个固定金额（最低还款额总和加上个人能负担的额外部分），
- 排序——哪个债务优先用额外付款支付，以及每个释放的付款接下来用于何处。

计划的输出是一个时间表：对于每个债务，何时还清；对于整体，预计无债日期和总利息。排序可能是一个命名策略（最低余额优先、最高利息优先、面向现金流或完全自定义）或机构结构分配；在概念上是同一件事——一个决定下一美元额外付款去向的规则。

3. 跟踪循环。付款（或程序存款）在发生时被记录。记录更新债务的余额和到期日期，
leaves.rules:
### The rollover rule

The plan's engine is rollover: when a debt is retired, the payment that used to go to it (minimum plus extra) is applied to the next debt in the ordering. The total monthly outlay stays constant while the extra payment on the current target grows. This single rule is what makes the schedule accelerate, and it is shared across realizations that otherwise have nothing in common.

### The snowball amount is calculated, not typed

The extra payment (the "snowball") is derived — capacity minus the sum of minimums. Changing it means changing the capacity or the minimums; products enforce this rather than letting the two drift apart.

### Balances move in both directions

Real debts are not one-way: purchases land on credit cards again, a month can be short-paid or skipped, an account can be deferred. A debt management application records these and recomputes; a tool that assumes only downward balances will desync from reality quickly. (One documented caveat of static spreadsheets: they typically assume a fixed minimum payment, so credit-card minimums that shrink as balances fall must be updated by hand.)

### Payments update state immediately

Recording a payment adjusts the balance, the due date, and the schedule in the same motion. The record and the plan are one system — this coupling is what separates the Type from a calculator whose output is a snapshot.

### Concessions are program facts, not user controls

In the program-mediated variant, interest reductions depend on creditor participation and are negotiated by the agency; they are never guaranteed and vary per creditor. The person's controllable inputs are the deposit and their own adherence, not the terms.

### Manual-entry privacy posture

Some products deliberately hold no bank connections — all figures are user-entered. Where integration exists (for example, syncing with a budgeting product), it is an add-on bridge, not the data foundation.
leaves.rules_zh:
### 滚雪球规则

该计划的核心是滚雪球：当一笔债务被清偿后，原本用于支付该债务的金额（最低还款额加超额部分）被应用到排序中的下一笔债务上。每月总支出保持不变，而当前目标债务上的超额付款额则不断增长。这一单一规则使得还款计划表能够加速，它也是所有看似毫不相关的实现方式之间的共同点。

### “雪球”金额是计算得出的，而非手动输入

超额付款额（即“雪球”）是推导出来的——等于还款能力减去所有最低还款额之和。改变它意味着改变还款能力或最低还款额；产品会强制执行这一逻辑，而非让两者脱节。

### 余额可双向变动

真实债务不是单向变动的：消费会再次增加信用卡欠款，某个月可能少还或跳过还款，账户可能被推迟。债务管理应用程序会记录这些情况并重新计算；而一个仅假设余额只会减少的工具会很快与现实脱节。（一个已知的静态电子表格的局限性是：它们通常假设每月最低还款额是固定的，因此随着余额下降而减少的信用卡最低还款额必须手动更新。）

### 付款即时更新状态

记录一笔付款会同时调整余额、到期日和计划表。记录与计划是同一系统——这种耦合正是将该类型软件与仅提供快照式输出的计算器区分开来的关键。

### 让步是项目事实，而非用户控制项

在由咨询机构协调的变体中，利息减免取决于债权人的参与并由咨询机构协商；它们从未被保证，且因债权人而异。个人可控的输入是存款额及其自身的履约情况，而非条款。

### 手动录入的隐私策略

一些产品刻意不与银行建立连接——

leaves.name: Debugger
leaves.overview:
A **Debugger** is a tool that takes a running program under its control so a developer can stop that program at chosen points, examine what it is actually doing at those moments, and advance it step by step to find the cause of incorrect behavior.

It answers questions no other development tool answers directly: *Where exactly is the program right now? How did execution get here? What values did the variables actually hold?* Rather than reading code or scanning logs, the developer observes the program's real state while it is frozen and drives it forward one statement at a time.

The defining core is small — three structures that must all be present:

```text
Program under debug
└── taken under the debugger's control
    (launch under supervision · attach to a running program · open a captured snapshot)
    └── The declared pause
        (execution stopped at chosen points or on chosen events)
        └── Inspection of the stopped state
            in the program's own execution terms
            (current position · call stack · variables · expression evaluation)
```

Everything else commonly associated with debugging — stepping buttons, watch windows, conditional breakpoints, logpoints, thread panels, remote debugging — is standard capability layered on this core, and is not what makes a tool a debugger. A tool that only aggregates error reports, only measures performance, or only writes log lines is a different kind of application, however much it helps with defects.
leaves.overview_zh:
一款 **调试器** 是一款能够将正在运行的程序置于其控制之下的工具，使开发者能够在选定的程序执行点暂停程序，检查其在这些时刻实际正在执行的操作，并一步步推进以定位导致行为错误的原因。

它回答了其他开发工具无法直接回答的问题：*程序当前的确切位置在哪里？执行是如何到达这里的？变量当时实际持有的是什么值？* 开发者无需阅读代码或扫描日志，而是在程序被冻结时观察其真实状态，并逐条语句驱动其前进。

其定义性的核心很简单——必须同时具备的三个结构：

```text
被调试的程序
└── 被置于调试器控制之下
    （在监督下启动 · 附加到正在运行的程序 · 打开捕获的快照）
    └── 声明的暂停点
        （在选定的点或选定的事件上停止执行）
        └── 对停止状态的检查
            使用程序自身的执行术语
            （当前位置 · 调用栈 · 变量 · 表达式求值）
```

其他通常与调试相关的所有内容——单步按钮、监视窗口、条件断点、日志点、线程面板、远程调试——都是建立在此核心之上的标准能力，并非使一款工具成为调试器的本质。一款只聚合错误报告、只衡量性能或只写入日志行的工具，是另一种类型的应用程序，无论它对解决缺陷有多大帮助。
leaves.dc:
**1. Control relationship with the program under debug.** The debugger does not watch from outside; it holds the program's execution. There are three standard ways to establish this relationship, and a mature tool usually offers more than one:

- **Launch** — the debugger starts the program itself, in debug mode, so control exists from the first instruction. The debugger typically manages the program's arguments, environment, and working directory.
- **Attach** — the debugger connects to a program that is already running. The user started the program; the debugger joins it mid-flight. On detach, the program normally continues without the debugger.
- **Captured snapshot (post-mortem)** — the debugger opens a file holding a captured execution state of a process (a core dump in native environments). Nothing can be resumed, but everything can be inspected. This is a long-standing, fully recognized mode of debugging.

**2. The declared pause.** The debugger's central event is the stop: execution is frozen at a point the user declared in advance (a **breakpoint**), or on an event the program hit (an exception, a crash), or on demand (a manual pause). Breakpoints attach to the program's own locations — a line of source, a function, an instruction — optionally qualified with conditions. When a stop happens, the debugger surfaces it with its reason and location; this stop is what everything else in the tool exists to serve.

**3. Inspection of the stopped state in the program's own terms.** While stopped, the debugger answers, in the vocabulary of the program itself:

- *Where am I?* — the current execution position, mapped back to the code the developer wrote (the highlighted source line; or, at the machine level, the current instruction).
- *How did I get here?* — the **call stack**: the chain of function calls (stack frames) that led to this point, each frame selectable so its own context can be examined.
- *What are the values?* — the variables and their values in each frame's scope, browsable structurally (an object's fields, an array's elements).
- *What else can I ask?* — evaluation of arbitrary expressions in the program's own language and current context, including calling the program's own functions.

The phrase "in the program's own terms" carries the Type's real breadth. For a **source-level debugger** the terms are source names — variables, functions, lines. For a **machine-level debugger** the terms are registers, memory, and disassembly. For a **managed-runtime debugger** the terms are VM objects and the heap. What is invariant is that inspection happens at the program's own semantic level, not through external artifacts.
leaves.dc_zh:
1. 与被调试程序的控制关系。调试器不是从外部观察；它持有程序的执行控制。有三种标准方式建立这种关系，成熟的工具通常提供不止一种：
- 启动（Launch） — 调试器自身以调试模式启动程序，因此控制从第一条指令开始。调试器通常管理程序的参数、环境和工作目录。
- 附加（Attach） — 调试器连接到一个已经运行的程序。用户启动了程序；调试器在中途加入。分离时，程序通常继续运行而不依赖调试器。
- 捕获快照（事后分析） — 调试器打开一个文件，该文件包含进程的捕获执行状态（在原生环境中是核心转储）。无法恢复执行，但所有内容都可检查。这是一种长期存在、完全认可的调试模式。

2. 声明暂停。调试器的中心事件是停止：执行在用户预先声明的点（断点）上冻结，或在程序命中的事件（异常、崩溃）上冻结，或按需（手动暂停）冻结。断点附加到程序自身的位置——一行源代码、一个函数、一条指令——可选择性地用条件限定。当停止发生时，调试器显示其原因和位置；这个停止是每个...
leaves.rules:
### Debug information is the substrate of source-level debugging

Source-level inspection — source names, line mapping, rich types — depends on debug information carried with the program. Build without it and the debugger falls back to lower-level views or degraded detail. This dependency is structural, not an edge case: it is why "compile for debugging" is a documented build concern.

### The source↔execution correspondence can break

Compilation and optimization relocate code: statements may be reordered, functions inlined, tail calls collapsed. Debuggers compensate where they can, but breakpoints can land on adjusted addresses, and some variables can be unobservable in optimized builds. Minified or transpiled front-end code raises the same correspondence problem at the source level.

### Breakpoints have a lifecycle

A breakpoint is a request. It can be verified (bound to an actual location), unverified (not currently bindable — shown as a hollow or gray marker), or adjusted (bound to a nearby address). Its state can change over the life of a session, and mature tools surface those changes to the user.

### The debugger interferes with the program

Debugging is not passive observation: the program runs under the debugger's control, stops at breakpoints, and may execute developer-supplied expressions — including function calls that can themselves stop at breakpoints or crash the target. Timing and behavior under the debugger can differ from the undisturbed run; timing-sensitive defects sometimes behave differently in a debug session. Products offer varying stop modes (for example, pausing one thread versus the whole process), and these semantics are user-visible.

### Attach and detach are asymmetric with launch

An attached program outlives the debugging session: detach, and it continues. A launched program's life is the session's life. This asymmetry shapes how each mode is used — attach for problems that only reproduce in the real running process, launch for controlled reproduction.

### Post-mortem inspection is read-only

In a captured snapshot nothing can be resumed, stepped, or modified; the debugger's value is complete, repeatable inspection of a state that no longer exists anywhere else. Live modification of program state (set variable, early return, calling functions) belongs to live sessions.
leaves.rules_zh:
### 调试信息是源代码级调试的基础

源代码级检查——源文件名、行号映射、丰富的类型信息——依赖于随程序携带的调试信息。若构建时未包含这些信息，调试器将回退到更底层的视图或细节受损的视图。这种依赖是结构性的，并非边缘情况：这就是为什么“为调试而编译”是一个被记录在案的构建关注点。

### 源代码与执行之间的对应关系可能被破坏

编译和优化会重新安置代码：语句可能被重排，函数被内联，尾部调用被折叠。调试器会在可能的情况下进行补偿，但断点可能落在调整后的地址上，并且在优化构建中，某些变量可能变得不可观测。前端代码的压缩或转译也会在源代码层面引发同样的对应问题。

### 断点具有生命周期

断点是一个请求。它可以被验证（绑定到实际位置）、未验证（当前不可绑定——显示为空心或灰色标记）或已调整（绑定到附近地址）。其状态可以在会话生命周期内发生变化，成熟的工具会将这些变化呈现给用户。

### 调试器会干扰程序

调试并非被动观察：程序在调试器的控制下运行，在断点处停止，并可能执行开发者提供的表达式——包括那些可能在断点处停止或导致目标崩溃的函数调用。调试器下的时序和行为可能与未受干扰的运行时不同；对时序敏感的缺陷有时在调试会话中表现不同。产品提供不同的暂停模式（例如，暂停单个线程与整个进程），这些语义对用户是可见的。

### 附加和分离与启动不对称

已附加的程序会比调试会话更长寿：分离后它继续运行。附加操作按设计是非破坏性的。

leaves.name: Decarbonization Planning Platform
leaves.overview:
A **Decarbonization Planning Platform** is an organization's system for planning and governing the reduction of its own greenhouse gas emissions. It anchors on the organization's measured emissions, organizes a persistent plan for getting from today's footprint to stated reduction ambitions, composes that plan from discrete reduction projects, and tracks delivery against the target trajectory over time.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Emissions evidence (the organization's own measured emissions — baseline and hotspots)
        ↓ anchors
A decarbonization plan — persistent, structured, organized toward a reduction ambition
        ↓ composed of
Discrete reduction levers / projects / initiatives (attributable, costed)
        ↓ tracked through
Recorded implementation progress (planned vs realized, over time)
```

Everything else commonly associated with these products — science-based target validation, marginal abatement cost curves, multi-year scenario simulation, initiative template libraries, AI recommendations — is widespread in current products but is not what makes the product a decarbonization planning platform. Earlier corporate and municipal climate action plans built on emissions inventories, lists of measures, and progress reporting satisfy the same defining loop without any of the modern machinery.

When the forward-looking program disappears and only the measured, auditable inventory of record remains, the product is a carbon accounting platform. When the emissions anchor is replaced by climate hazards, the same loop becomes climate adaptation planning.
leaves.overview_zh:
**脱碳规划平台**是一个组织用于规划和管理其自身温室气体排放减少的系统。它锚定在组织的测量排放上，组织一个从当前碳足迹到既定减排目标的持久计划，通过离散的减排项目组合该计划，并随时间跟踪目标轨迹的交付情况。

定义结构很简单：

```text
排放证据（组织自身的测量排放——基线和热点）
        ↓ 锚定
一个脱碳计划——持久的、结构化的、面向减排目标的
        ↓ 组合自
离散的减排杠杆/项目/倡议（可归因的、已计成本的）
        ↓ 通过跟踪
记录的实施进展（计划 vs 实现，随时间）
```

其他通常与这些产品相关的内容——科学目标验证、边际减排成本曲线、多年情景模拟、倡议模板库、AI 推荐——在当前产品中普遍存在，但并不是使产品成为脱碳规划平台的要素。早期的企业和市政气候行动计划基于排放清单、措施列表和进展报告，满足相同的定义循环，而无需任何现代机制。

当前瞻性程序消失，只有可测量、可审计的记录清单保留时，产品就是碳核算平台。当排放锚点被气候危害取代时，相同的循环就变成了气候适应规划。
leaves.dc:
```text
Emissions evidence (baseline + hotspots)
        ↓ anchors
Decarbonization plan (persistent roadmap toward a stated reduction ambition)
        ↓ composed of
Reduction levers / projects / initiatives
        ↓ tracked through
Implementation progress (planned vs realized)
```

Four properties. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as this Type:

- **Emissions evidence as the anchor** — the plan is built on the organization's own quantified emissions: a baseline and the hotspots within it. The evidence may be computed in the same product, imported from a carbon accounting system, or assembled with advisors — what matters is that the plan is anchored to the organization's real emissions rather than generic benchmarks. Without this, the product is generic strategy-execution or project-portfolio software.
- **The plan as a persistent structured artifact** — a roadmap or pathway that organizes how the organization moves from the baseline toward its reduction ambition over years. It survives sessions and reporting cycles, is edited as circumstances change, and is the single reference for what the organization has committed to. Without it, the product is hotspot analytics or a target dashboard.
- **Discrete reduction levers as managed records** — the individual projects, initiatives, or measures through which reduction happens (an energy-efficiency retrofit, a fuel switch, a supplier change, a fleet electrification). Each is identifiable and attributable, commonly carries an expected abatement amount and cost, and is drawn from a curated library or authored custom. Without them, the product is target-setting tooling.
- **Recorded implementation progress** — status, ownership, and realized reductions maintained over time, compared against what the plan promised. Reductions are projections until delivered; the platform keeps the difference visible. Without this, the product is a one-shot plan document.
leaves.dc_zh:
排放证据（基线 + 热点）
        ↓ 锚定
脱碳计划（面向既定减排雄心的持久路线图）
        ↓ 由...组成
减排杠杆 / 项目 / 倡议
        ↓ 通过...跟踪
实施进展（计划 vs 实际）
leaves.rules:
### The plan must reconcile with the inventory

The plan's numbers are anchored to the organization's measured emissions. Mature products keep baseline, footprint, disclosures, and reduction plan on one data spine so the plan cannot drift from the inventory; plans built on generic benchmarks are explicitly rejected by the market's own framing.

### Reductions are projections until delivered

A lever's abatement is a modeled expectation. The platform's tracking discipline is the comparison of planned outcomes with realized reductions once the inventory reflects the work — the gap between the two is a first-class object, not an embarrassment to be hidden.

### Targets constrain the plan

The plan exists to close the gap between baseline and target. Scenario modeling tests whether a lever mix can close it; if delivery slips or assumptions change, the plan is revised — the roadmap is a living artifact, not a one-time document.

### Capital allocation is part of the workflow

Levers carry cost, and choosing among them is an investment decision. The financial machinery (project economics, budget views, abatement-cost ranking) exists so that sustainability, finance, and operations converge on what to fund.

### Multi-level consistency

Site- and entity-level plans must roll up to the corporate roadmap without contradiction; consolidation works top-down and bottom-up, and dependencies between levers are representable.

### Within value chain, by default

The defining scope is the organization's own emissions and its value chain. Offsets and beyond-value-chain financing are adjacent capabilities — some products carry them as separate modules, but the planning core is about reducing the organization's own emissions.
leaves.rules_zh:
### 计划必须与清单协调

计划的数字锚定在组织的测量排放上。成熟的产品将基线、碳足迹、披露和减排计划保持在一个数据脊柱上，因此计划不能偏离清单；基于通用基准构建的计划被市场自身的框架明确拒绝。

### 减排在交付前是预测

杠杆的减排是建模预期。平台的跟踪纪律是将计划成果与清单反映工作后的实现减排进行比较；两者之间的差距是一级对象，而不是需要隐藏的尴尬。

### 目标约束计划

计划的存在是为了弥合基线和目标之间的差距。情景建模测试一组杠杆是否能弥合；如果交付延迟或假设改变，计划就修订——路线图是活生生的构件，而不是一次性文档。

### 资本分配是工作流的一部分

杠杆带有成本，选择它们是一个投资决策。财务机制（项目经济性、预算视图、减排成本排名）的存在是为了让可持续性、财务和运营在资助什么上达成一致。

### 多层一致性

地点和实体级计划必须汇总到企业路线图而不矛盾；整合自上而下和自下而上进行，杠杆之间的依赖关系可以表示。

### 默认在价值链内

定义范围是组织自身的排放及其价值链。抵消和超越价值链的融资是相邻能力——有些产品将它们作为单独模块包含，但规划核心是关于减少组织自身的排放。

leaves.name: Deception Platform
leaves.overview:
A **Deception Platform** is a defender-operated security system that plants fake-but-plausible assets — decoy hosts and services, planted credentials, deceptive documents and data, triggerable tokens — across an organization's own environment. Because legitimate users have no business reason to touch any of these assets, **any interaction with them is treated as a high-fidelity signal of malicious activity**, and the platform captures what the interacting party did.

It solves a specific detection problem: signature- and behavior-based tools watch real assets for signs of evil and drown analysts in plausible-looking alerts. A deception platform inverts this — it adds assets whose *only* function is to be touched by someone who should not be there. The result is alerts that are rare and, by construction, near-zero false positives.

The defining core is small:

```text
Decoy assets of no production function
  └── any interaction = presumptively malicious → high-fidelity alert
      └── observation of what the interacting party did
          └── all held together by a central management plane over the decoy fleet
```

Everything else commonly associated with the category — lures and breadcrumbs, credential seeding, automated decoy placement, SIEM integration, forensics capture — is standard capability that makes the core practical, not what makes the product a deception platform.
leaves.overview_zh:
一个**欺骗平台**是防御者操作的安全系统，它在组织自身的环境中植入虚假但看似合理的资产——诱饵主机和服务、植入的凭据、欺骗性文档和数据、可触发令牌。因为合法用户没有业务理由触碰这些资产，**任何与它们的交互都被视为恶意活动的高保真信号**，平台会捕获交互方的行为。

它解决了一个特定的检测问题：基于签名和行为的工具监视真实资产以寻找恶意迹象，并使分析师淹没在看似合理的警报中。欺骗平台颠倒了这一点——它添加的资产*唯一*功能是被不应该在那里的人触碰。结果是警报罕见，并且在结构上几乎零误报。

定义核心很小：

```text
无生产功能的诱饵资产
  └── 任何交互 = 推定恶意 → 高保真警报
      └── 观察交互方的行为
          └── 所有内容通过欺骗舰队的中央管理平面保持在一起
```

与该类别通常相关的所有其他内容——诱饵和面包屑、凭据播种、自动化诱饵部署、SIEM集成、取证捕获——是使核心实用的标准能力，而不是使产品成为欺骗平台的东西。
leaves.dc:
**1. The deception surface — decoy assets of no production function.**
The platform creates and maintains fake assets deployed into the environment. They imitate things an attacker wants: file servers and shares, login pages, databases, industrial-control systems, cloud storage, admin credentials, juicy-looking documents. What unifies them is that they serve no legitimate business purpose — their entire function is to be found by the wrong person. Decoys take many forms (see Variants); the invariant is the asset itself, not any particular form.

**2. The presumptive-malice engagement signal.**
Any interaction with a decoy — a connection, a login attempt, a file opened, a credential used — is surfaced as an alert to defenders. The premise is structural: there is no legitimate workflow that touches a decoy, so engagement is presumptively malicious. This is what makes the alert high-fidelity and the false-positive rate near zero (with limited tuning for known scanners — see Rules).

**3. The engagement observation.**
When a decoy is engaged, the platform records what the interacting party did: source and protocol detail, commands run, credentials attempted, files accessed, the direction of lateral movement. This turns a single alert into evidence — for triage, for incident response, and for understanding attacker techniques.

**4. The management plane.**
A central console deploys, configures, monitors, and reports on the whole decoy fleet: where decoys live, what they imitate, which alerts fired, and what the engagement looked like. This is what makes the product a *platform* rather than a single trap.
leaves.dc_zh:
**1. 欺骗面 — 无生产功能的诱饵资产。**
平台创建并维护部署到环境中的虚假资产。它们模仿攻击者想要的东西：文件服务器和共享、登录页面、数据库、工业控制系统、云存储、管理员凭证、看似重要的文档。它们的统一之处在于没有合法的业务功能——其全部功能是被错误的人发现。诱饵有多种形式（见变体）；不变的是资产本身，而不是任何特定形式。

**2. 预设恶意交互信号。**
与诱饵的任何交互——连接、登录尝试、文件打开、凭证使用——都会作为警报呈现给防御者。前提是结构性的：没有合法工作流会接触诱饵，因此交互被预设为恶意。这使得警报高保真，误报率接近零（针对已知扫描器有有限调整——见规则）。

**3. 交互观察。**
当诱饵被交互时，平台记录交互方所做的事情：源和协议详细信息、运行的命令、尝试的凭证、访问的文件、横向移动的方向。这将单个警报转化为证据——用于分类、事件响应和理解攻击者技术。

**4. 管理平面。**
一个中央控制台部署、
leaves.rules:
- **Presumptive malice, with tuned exceptions.** The near-zero-false-positive premise holds only if the traps are scoped correctly. Known scanners, monitoring tools, and admin workflows that might legitimately sweep the network are excluded via ignore lists and scoping; everything else that touches a decoy is treated as an intrusion signal.
- **Decoys must stay believable.** A deception layer only works while it mirrors the real environment; products automate decoy refresh for this reason. A decoy that has gone stale relative to its surroundings is a liability.
- **Decoys carry no production function and no sensitive data.** They exist only to be touched by the wrong party. Hosting real data on them would create real risk; this is a standing constraint of the approach.
- **Alerts are few and loud.** Unlike signature-based tooling, a deception alert is inherently rare; SOC practice treats it as high-priority by default.
- **Coverage is a design decision.** The deception surface must be placed where intruders actually go — near valuable assets and along lateral-movement paths — or it will simply never fire. Placement guidance and automation exist because coverage, not realism alone, determines value.
- **Both outsiders and insiders are in scope.** The same decoy that catches an intruder's lateral movement catches an insider misusing privileged access; products treat both as legitimate detection targets.
leaves.rules_zh:
- **推定恶意，带有调优例外。** 近零误报的前提只有在陷阱范围正确时才成立。已知的扫描仪、监控工具和可能合法扫描网络的管理员工作流通过忽略列表和范围排除；其他触碰诱饵的一切都被视为入侵信号。
- **诱饵必须保持可信。** 欺骗层只有在镜像真实环境时才有效；产品因此自动化诱饵刷新。相对于环境变得陈旧的诱饵是一种负担。
- **诱饵不承载生产功能和敏感数据。** 它们仅存在以便被错误方触碰。在它们上托管真实数据会产生真实风险；这是该方法的永久约束。
- **警报少而响亮。** 与基于签名的工具不同，欺骗警报本质上罕见；SOC实践默认将其视为高优先级。
- **覆盖范围是设计决策。** 欺骗面必须放置在入侵者实际去的地方——靠近有价值资产和沿着横向移动路径——否则它根本不会触发。放置指导和自动化存在，因为覆盖范围，而不仅仅是现实性，决定了价值。
- **外部和内部人员都在范围内。** 捕获入侵者横向移动的同一诱饵也捕获滥用特权访问的内部人员；产品将两者都视为合法的检测目标。

leaves.name: Decision Management Platform
aliases_zh: 业务规则与模型管理平台
leaves.overview:
A **Decision Management Platform** is an enterprise system that manages an organization's automated operational **decisions** as governed, continuously improvable assets. The decision is the central object of the whole type: a named, versioned definition that composes executable logic — business rules plus predictive models — and runs it against the facts of individual transactions, applications, or cases to return an actionable outcome to the operational system that asked for it. Executed outcomes are captured and measured, and the measurements feed back into revising the decision itself.

The problem the type exists to solve: high-volume operational decisions — whether to approve a loan application, what premium and coverage apply to a policy, whether a transaction is fraudulent, what price to quote, what offer to make, whether an equipment reading signals a fault — must be made consistently, instantly, and explainably, and must keep improving as the business learns. Hard-coding this logic couples its evolution to software release cycles; an isolated analytics model produces scores nobody acts on. A decision management platform holds the decision as a business-owned asset between the two: logic and models are composed into decisions, decisions are executed by operational systems, and decision performance is measured and improved on a cadence independent of application releases.

The boundary is easiest to see by what sits on either side. A business rules management system is the rules-centric core of this space — its central managed artifact is the rule, not the composed decision. A machine learning platform's central artifact is the model. A decision management platform treats rules and models as first-class inputs to the artifact it actually manages — the decision — and closes the loop by measuring what those decisions achieve. If a product only produces a risk score, it is a scoring application; if it routes requests to human approvers, it is approval workflow software; if it manages the surrounding business process end to end, it is a process platform. The decision management platform is the layer that decides.
leaves.overview_zh:
一个**决策管理平台**是一个企业系统，它将组织自动化的运营**决策**作为受管控、可持续改进的资产进行管理。决策是整个类型的核心对象：一个带版本、命名的定义，它组合可执行逻辑——业务规则加预测模型——并针对单个事务、申请或案例的事实运行它，向请求它的运营系统返回一个可操作的结果。执行的结果被记录和衡量，而这些衡量结果又反馈到决策本身的修订中。

该类型旨在解决的问题是：高容量的运营决策——无论是批准贷款申请、适用何种保费和保单范围、交易是否欺诈、报价多少、提供何种优惠、还是设备读数是否表明故障——必须保持一致、即时且可解释，并且必须随着业务学习而持续改进。将这种逻辑硬编码会使其演进与软件发布周期紧密耦合；一个孤立的分析模型产生的分数无人采取行动。决策管理平台将决策作为业务拥有的资产置于两者之间：逻辑和模型被组合成决策，决策由运营系统执行，决策绩效则按照独立于应用程序发布的节奏进行衡量和改进。

其边界最易通过两侧的事物来观察。业务规则管理系统是这个领域的规则核心——其中心管理工件是规则，而非组合后的决策。机器学习平台的中心工件是模型。决策管理平台则将规则和模型视为其实际管理的工件——决策——的一级输入，并通过衡量这些决策所达成的成果来闭环。如果一个产品只产生风险评分，它是一个评分应用；如果它将请求路由给人工审批者，它是审批流程软件；如果它管理整个端到端的业务流程，它是一个流程平台。决策管理平台则是进行决策的那一层。
leaves.dc:
Four structures. All four are present together; remove any one and the product is no longer this type:

```text
Decision asset (named, versioned definition composed of decision logic:
                rules + predictive models as first-class inputs)
  └── governed by
Decision lifecycle (author → test → approve → deploy, independent of
                    application releases)
  └── executed as
Runtime decision execution (per-transaction/case evaluation returning
                            outcomes to operational systems)
  └── closed by
Measurement loop (executed outcomes captured, analyzed, and fed back
                  into revising the decision)
```

- **The decision asset.** A decision is a named, reusable, versioned definition — not buried logic inside an application. What distinguishes the type is what the decision is allowed to compose: business rules (the universal core form — conditions paired with actions) *and* predictive/analytics models as equal, first-class inputs. A decision might evaluate eligibility rules, invoke a risk model, apply a threshold, and return an outcome with reasons; the platform manages the rules, the models, and the composed decision as governed assets in their own right. A platform that manages only rules is a rules management system; the composed decision with models as co-equal inputs is what makes this a decision management platform.
- **The decision lifecycle.** Decision assets move through their own change management: authoring, testing, approval, promotion across environments, and versioned deployment — all without re-releasing the applications that consume the decisions. This independence is the economic reason the type exists: policy and strategy change far more often than software does.
- **Runtime decision execution.** When an operational event occurs — an application is submitted, a transaction arrives, a claim is filed — the calling system invokes the platform with the facts of that case. The platform evaluates the current decision version and returns an actionable outcome: approve or decline, a price or rate, a risk classification, the next best action, flags and notifications. Execution is a short evaluation against one case, repeated at operational volume, through a decision API, a deployed service, or an embedded runtime.
- **The measurement loop.** The platform captures what its decisions did — outcomes, volumes, and the business results that follow — and makes decision performance visible and analyzable: dashboards, KPIs, alerts, comparisons between decision versions. This is the "management" in decision management: decision assets are revised on the basis of measured performance, deliberately and continuously, rather than only when something breaks.
leaves.dc_zh:
四大结构。四者必须同时存在；移除任何一个，产品就不再是此类型：

```
决策资产 (一个命名的、版本化的定义，由决策逻辑构成：
                规则 + 预测模型作为一等输入)
  └── 受
决策生命周期 (创建 → 测试 → 审批 → 部署，独立于
                    应用发布) 治理
  └── 作为
运行时决策执行 (按事务/案例进行评估，将结果返回给
                    业务运营系统) 执行
  └── 由
测量闭环 (捕获执行结果，分析，并反馈以修订
                  决策) 闭环
```

- **决策资产。** 决策是一个命名的、可复用的、版本化的定义——而非深埋在应用内部的逻辑。定义此类型的关键在于，决策被允许组合什么：业务规则（普遍的内核形式——条件与动作配对）*和*预测/分析模型作为平等的一等输入。一个决策可能评估资格规则、调用风险模型、应用阈值，并返回带有原因的结果；该平台将规则、模型以及组合而成的决策作为受治理的资产进行管理。一个仅管理规则的平台是规则管理系统；以模型为共同平等输入的组合决策，是使其成为决策管理平台的关键。
leaves.rules:
### Decisions change without application releases

The structural behavior of the type: the deployed decision version changes on its own cadence while consuming applications stay untouched. Applications are written against the decision's inputs and outputs, not against its current logic.

### Every decision is explainable

Because the platform records which rules fired, which models scored, and which branches resolved, it can answer "why was this outcome produced?" — for a single past decision, replayed exactly, or for a population. In regulated deployments this is the compliance requirement that drives adoption, not an add-on.

### Version consistency is a governed choice

Multiple decision versions can coexist. Which version serves a given invocation is controlled behavior — typically the latest deployed version, with some products allowing invocation by explicit version. Channels are kept consistent by pointing them all at the same decision asset.

### Models are governed inputs with their own lifecycle

A model inside a decision degrades as the world drifts away from its training data. Mature platforms commonly monitor model performance, alert on drift, and support retraining or swapping a model — sometimes automatically when performance crosses thresholds — without rebuilding the decision around it.

### Outcomes are measured — by design

The platform does not treat an executed decision as the end of the story. Outcomes feed analytics that exist to trigger revision. A decision management platform whose decisions never change as a result of their measurements is being used below its purpose.

### Governance gates the improvement loop

Who may author, test, approve, and deploy is role-controlled, with approval workflows and audit trails as the normal path. The combination of business-side authorship and machine-speed execution is exactly why the governance machinery is structural.
leaves.rules_zh:
### 决策变更无需应用发布

该类型的结构性行为：部署的决策版本按照其自身节奏变化，而消耗它的应用程序保持不变。应用程序是基于决策的输入和输出编写的，而非其当前逻辑。

### 每个决策都是可解释的

由于平台记录了哪些规则被触发、哪些模型进行了评分以及哪些分支被解析，它可以回答“为什么会产生这个结果？”——无论是针对单个过去的决策，精确重放，还是针对整体人群。在受监管的部署中，这是推动采用的合规要求，而非附加功能。

### 版本一致性是受治理的选择

多个决策版本可以共存。哪个版本服务于给定调用是受控行为——通常是最新部署的版本，有些产品允许通过显式版本进行调用。通过将所有渠道指向同一个决策资产来保持渠道一致性。

### 模型是具有自身生命周期的受治理输入

决策中的模型会随着世界偏离其训练数据而退化。成熟的平台通常监控模型性能、对漂移发出警报，并支持重新训练或更换模型——有时在性能超过阈值时自动进行——而无需围绕模型重建决策。

### 结果是被衡量的——这是设计使然

平台不将执行的决策视为故事的终结。结果会馈送到分析中，而分析的存在是为了触发修订。一个其决策从不因其衡量结果而改变的决策管理平台，其使用价值低于其设计目的。

### 治理门控改进循环
