Positions are marked against price feeds and maintained curves. Curve changes restate the value of the whole book, so curve governance (who may change a curve, when, and with what history) is a structural concern, not a convenience feature.

### Market clocks gate the work

What can be executed, amended, or submitted depends on the session state of each market the participant trades — gate closures, intraday windows, settlement cycles. The platform reflects these clocks; the asset-bidding loop in particular is deadline-driven by construction.

### Limits gate trading

Market-risk limits and counterparty credit limits are enforced as conditions on doing business: a proposed deal that would breach a limit is blocked or flagged for approval, depending on the product's and the desk's controls. Credit availability is checked before the deal, exposure recomputed after it.

### Periodic finality

The book closes daily and monthly; closed periods are frozen for accounting and audit. Settlement statements later arrive from market operators and counterparties and are checked against the participant's own expectations — but that reconciliation discipline belongs to the scheduling-and-settlement side of the house; the trading record supplies the deals those statements settle.
leaves.rules_zh:
### 交易从不仅仅是一行数据

每笔交易都绑定一个交割期，对于实物交割的交易，它还关联着物流现实：能源必须流动、被提报并调度、被运输。因此，交易记录承载着超出交易本身的义务，而平台的下游交接（调度、结算、开票）正是因此而存在。

### 头寸完整性

每笔交易都必须进入账簿，对已记录交易的更改（修订、中止、回溯估值）本身也是被跟踪的事件。平台的权威性建立于此：交易员、风险经理和高管所看到的头寸只有在记录完整且受控时才值得信赖——这正是厂商反对基于电子表格操作的核心论点。

### 估值的好坏取决于其价格

头寸根据价格源和维护的曲线进行标记。曲线的变更会重新陈述整个账簿的价值，因此曲线管理（谁可以更改曲线、何时更改、如何保留历史记录）是一个结构性问题，而非便利功能。

### 市场时钟控制工作流程

可以执行、修改或提交什么，取决于参与者交易的每个市场的交易时段状态——收盘窗口、日内窗口、结算周期。平台反映了这些时钟；资产竞价循环尤其在设计上受截止日期驱动。

### 限额控制交易

市场风险限额和交易对手信用限额作为业务进行的条件被强制执行：一笔拟议的交易如果会突破限额，将被阻止或标记以待批准，具体取决于产品和交易台的控制措施。信用额度在交易前进行检查，风险敞口在交易后重新计算。

### 定期终局性

账簿按日和按月结算；已结算的周期被冻结用于会计处理。

leaves.name: Engineering Change Management
leaves.overview:
An **Engineering Change Management** application governs how changes to a product's engineering definition are proposed, evaluated, approved, and put into effect. Its world is built around a change record — commonly realized as an engineering change request, change order, or change notice — that travels through a controlled lifecycle and, when approved, supersedes the released revisions of the engineering objects it affects: parts, bills of materials, drawings, documents, files, and specifications.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Change record (request / order / notice)
└── binds to affected revisioned engineering records
    │   (items, BOMs, drawings, documents, files, specifications)
└── governed progression
    │   (propose → assess → approve → implement → release)
└── recorded decisions and controlled release
        (who approved what, when, why — often with effectivity)
```

Everything else commonly associated with modern products — electronic signatures, impact dashboards, AI-assisted redlines, automated routing, cycle-time analytics — is widespread in current products but is not part of the defining core. Paper-era practice (change request forms, change board minutes, change orders, change notices, redlined drawings) satisfies the same structure without any of it.

When the center of gravity shifts to owning the whole product-record estate across the product's life, the product is a Product Lifecycle Management system; when it shifts to a commercial contract's scope, price, and time among contracting parties, it is construction change order management. The change process itself — not the estate, not the contract — is what this Type owns.
leaves.overview_zh:
一个**工程变更管理**应用程序，用于管理对产品工程定义的变更如何被提出、评估、批准和生效。其核心世界围绕着一个变更记录展开——通常以工程变更请求、变更单或变更通知的形式实现——该记录在受控的生命周期中流转，并在获批时，取代其影响的已发布工程对象的版本：零部件、物料清单、图纸、文档、文件和规格。

其核心结构很简单：

```text
变更记录（请求 / 单据 / 通知）
└── 绑定到受影响的带版本工程记录
    │   （项目、BOM、图纸、文档、文件、规格）
└── 受管的进程
    │   （提出 → 评估 → 批准 → 实施 → 发布）
└── 记录决策与受控发布
        （谁批准了什么，何时，为何——通常带有生效期）
```

与现代产品通常相关的其他一切——电子签名、影响仪表盘、AI辅助红线标注、自动路由、周期时间分析——在当前产品中普遍存在，但并不属于定义核心。纸质时代的实践（变更请求表、变更委员会会议记录、变更单、变更通知、红线标注的图纸）无需这些工具也能满足相同的结构。

当重心转移到拥有整个产品生命周期的产品记录资产时，该产品就是产品生命周期管理系统；当重心转移到商业合同的范围、价格和签约方之间的时间时，它就是施工变更单管理。变更过程本身——而非资产、也非合同——才是此**类型**所定义的核心。
leaves.dc:
Three structures, held together. Remove any one and the product stops being recognizable as this Type.

**1. The change record — the unit of work.**

A persistent, identified record that carries what is changing, why it is changing, who must decide, and the outcome. Products realize it in one or more forms:

- a **request** (engineering change request) documenting the problem or opportunity and the justification
- an **order** (engineering change order) authorizing the change against an established baseline
- a **notice** (engineering change notice/notification) delivering the implemented change to the enterprise

Some products keep all three as separate record types; others merge them into a single change object with phases. Both realizations satisfy the same structure: a formal, tracked record moving from proposal to disposition. The record typically names the affected records, the reason (design improvement, obsolescence, quality event, cost, customer request, regulatory requirement), the approvers, and the outcome (approved, rejected, withdrawn).

**2. The revisioned engineering record base the change acts upon.**

The change record binds to the engineering objects it affects — parts/items, BOMs, drawings, documents, CAD files, specifications, procedures. These objects exist as sequences of identified revisions, and an approved change produces new released revisions of the affected objects. The record base is wider than BOMs alone: in mature products a change routinely touches documents, files, and specifications alongside items and structures. This binding is what makes the application engineering change management rather than a generic approval workflow — the change record is meaningless without the revisioned records it supersedes, and the records are uncontrolled without the change process.

**3. The governed progression with designated authority and traceability.**

The change record moves through a defined lifecycle — commonly propose → assess → approve → implement → release — and each decision is recorded: who approved what, when, and why. Approval authority is cross-functional and configurable: a standing change review board in process-heavy organizations, or a per-change approver list elsewhere. Release of the new revisions is controlled, commonly gated by an effectivity decision (when the change takes effect). Without the governed progression, the record base is just a version archive; without traceability, the process cannot support audits or quality investigations.
leaves.dc_zh: 三个结构，紧密结合。移除其中任何一个，该产品都将不再被识别为此类型。
leaves.rules:
### A record is in one active change at a time

Several products enforce that a given item or file can appear in only one open change order at a time, preventing conflicting edits from being approved out of sequence. This makes the change process an access-control surface as well as a governance one.

### Approval gates release, not editing

Working on a proposed change is generally unrestricted; what is restricted is advancing the released revision. In some products the restriction is strict — lifecycle state changes of released records are only permitted through a change order — making the change record the sole gate to production.

### Effectivity decides when a change takes effect

Approval alone does not complete the change. Release commonly requires setting effectivity — the date (or condition) from which the new revision is the released definition — and the implementation work being complete. Some products close the change automatically on approval; others keep it open until implementation is confirmed.

### Rejection is a revision, not a dead end

A rejected change record returns to its owner, is edited (affected records may be added or removed), and is resubmitted. The record and its history persist.

### Validation runs before review

Rule checks (required data, status requirements, parent/child consistency, missing documents) run during preparation; errors block submission, warnings do not. Strictness commonly increases with the release status of the affected records.

### The audit trail is the product

Every decision — who approved, when, what changed, why — is recorded against the change record and commonly against the affected data. This is what makes the process usable in quality audits and investigations, and it is why traceability belongs to the defining core rather than to a feature list.
leaves.rules_zh:
### 一条记录一次只处于一个活动变更中

一些产品强制规定，给定的项目或文件一次只能出现在一个打开的变更单中，以防止冲突的编辑被按错误顺序批准。这使得变更过程既是一个治理层面，也是一个访问控制层面。

### 批准是发布的关卡，而非编辑的关卡

处理拟议变更通常是不受限制的；受限的是推进已发布的版本。在某些产品中，限制是严格的——已发布记录的生命周期状态变更仅允许通过变更单进行——这使得变更记录成为通往生产的唯一关卡。

### 生效期决定变更何时生效

仅仅批准并不会完成变更。发布通常需要设置生效期——新版本成为已发布定义的日期（或条件）——并且实施工作已完成。一些产品在批准后自动关闭变更；另一些则保持打开直到确认实施完成。

### 拒绝是修订，而非死路

被拒绝的变更记录返回给其所有者，进行编辑（受影响记录可增删），然后重新提交。记录及其历史得以保留。

### 验证运行在评审之前

规则检查（必填数据、状态要求、父/子一致性、缺失文档）在准备阶段运行；错误会阻止提交，警告则不会。严格性通常随受影响记录的发布状态而增加。

### 审计追踪就是产品本身

每一个决策——谁批准的、何时、什么被改变、为何——都被记录在变更记录上，通常也记录在受影响数据上。这使得流程在质量审计和调查中可用，也是可追溯性属于定义的一部分的原因。

leaves.name: Engineering Document Management
leaves.overview:
An **Engineering Document Management** application is an engineering organization's system of record for its engineering documents and drawings. It holds each document as a **registered record** — a persistent, individually identified entry that exists independently of any file — tracks a **revision lineage** in which exactly one version is current and authoritative while earlier revisions remain as superseded history, and moves documents through **governed, permission-controlled states** from authoring to review to approval, with an attributable audit trail. Approved revisions are then published to the parties who consume them — as renditions, distribution packages, or handover sets — without granting them authoring rights.

The defining core is deliberately small:

```text
Engineering document of record (registered identity; files attach to it)
└── Revision lineage with one current authoritative version
    └── Governed progression through controlled states (review → approval)
        └── Publication of approved revisions to consumers
```

Everything else commonly associated with the category — CAD-tool integration, reference management, title-block exchange, PDF renditions, viewers and markup, transmittal portals, EAM/ERP integrations, compliance e-signatures — is standard capability that mature products add, not what makes the product an engineering document management system. A pre-software drawing register with revision letters, checker/approver signatures, and a distribution ledger satisfies the same core without any of them.

When the center of gravity shifts from the engineering organization's vault to a construction project's cross-organization issue and field consumption, the product is drifting toward a different Application Type (Construction Document Management). When the center shifts to part/item records, BOMs, and change orders, it is drifting toward Product Data Management / PLM.
leaves.overview_zh:
一个**工程文档管理**应用程序是工程组织对其工程文档和图纸的系统记录。它将每份文档保存为一个**注册记录**——一个持久、独立标识的条目，独立于任何文件而存在——跟踪一个**修订谱系**，其中只有一个版本是当前且权威的，而早期修订则作为已废止的历史保留下来，并通过**受控、权限受控的状态**将文档从编写流转到审查再到批准，并留下可归因的审计轨迹。批准的修订版随后发布给使用方——以呈现形式、分发包或移交集的形式——但不授予其编辑权限。

其定义性核心被有意设计得非常精简：

```text
工程记录文档（注册身份；文件附属于它）
└── 具有一个当前权威版本的修订谱系
    └── 在受控状态下的受控推进（审查 → 批准）
        └── 将批准的修订版发布给使用方
```

通常与此类别相关的其他所有内容——CAD工具集成、参考管理、标题栏交换、PDF呈现、查看器和标记、传送门户、EAM/ERP集成、合规电子签名——都是成熟产品会增加的标准功能，而非使其成为工程文档管理系统的要素。一个预先存在的、带有修订字母、校核/批准签名和分发记录的纸质图纸登记簿，在不借助任何这些功能的情况下，也能满足同样的核心要求。

当重心从工程组织的资料库转移到施工项目的跨组织问题处理和现场使用时，该产品就偏向了另一种应用类型（施工文档管理）。当重心转移到零件/项目记录、物料清单（BOM）和变更单时，它就偏向了产品数据管理（PDM）/产品生命周期管理（PLM）。
leaves.dc:
**The engineering document of record.** The central object is a registered record for one document — a drawing, model, specification, datasheet, calculation, or vendor document. The record carries its own identity (a document number/name distinct from any file name), controlled attributes (type, discipline, status, revision, ownership), and its own access permissions. Files attach to the record; the record can exist before any file does (a register entry awaiting content), and replacing the attached file does not create a new record. The register is the organization's authoritative list of what engineering documents exist.

**Revision lineage with one current authoritative version.** Changes to a document attach to the same record as new revisions. Earlier revisions are retained — visible, retrievable, and marked as superseded — never silently overwritten. Exactly one revision is the **current** one: the version downstream consumers work from and the one that may be edited next. When new material arrives that might match an existing record, the system adjudicates: it is either a new revision of that record or a new record — the register stays unambiguous. Dependency relationships between documents (a drawing referencing other documents) are part of the lineage too: a master document can be pinned to specific revisions of its references or follow their current ones.

**Governed progression through controlled states.** A document advances through named states — work in progress, review, approved/released; exact labels are configured per organization — and the system enforces who may move it and who may act on it in each state. State-based access control means a document under review is visible or editable only to the parties the state allows. Reaching an approved or final state typically renders the document read-only for everyone, regardless of permissions. Every transition is attributable: who changed what, when, and (where configured) with a required comment. In compliance-heavy deployments, formal approvals carry electronic signatures.

**Publication to consumers.** The approved current revision is what leaves the vault: rendered renditions (PDF-class outputs of authoring formats), distribution packages to other organizations, or handover sets to the owner at project completion. Publication is a controlled act — recorded, attributable, and tied to specific revisions — not a file copy.
leaves.dc_zh:
权威工程文档记录。核心对象是单个文档的注册记录——图纸、模型、规范、数据表、计算书或供应商文件。记录拥有独立标识（区别于任何文件名的文档编号/名称）、受控属性（类型、专业、状态、版本、归属）及其独立访问权限。文件附加于记录；记录可在任何文件存在之前即创建（等待内容的注册条目），替换附件不会生成新记录。该登记簿是组织内存在的工程文档的权威清单。

具有唯一当前权威版本的版本谱系。文档变更以新版本形式附加到同一记录。早期版本被保留——可见、可检索且标记为已替代——永远不会被静默覆盖。有且仅有一个版本是**当前**版本：下游使用者据此工作的版本，以及后续可能被编辑的版本。当新材料可能匹配现有记录时，系统将进行判定：它要么是该记录的新版本，要么是新记录——登记簿始终保持明确性。文档间的依赖关系（如一张图纸引用其他文档）也属于谱系的一部分：主文档可固定引用其参考文档的特定版本，或跟随其当前版本。

治理控制
leaves.rules:
- **The current revision is authoritative.** Consumers work from the current approved revision; superseded revisions remain readable but are never the working version. Only the current revision can be checked out for editing.
- **Changes are serialized.** The edit lock prevents concurrent modification of the current revision; read-only copies keep everyone else productive. Committing work and releasing the lock are separable acts in some products.
- **Approval is a gate, not a label.** Released/final states render the document read-only regardless of permissions; reopening requires a new revision cycle under the same governed rules.
- **State controls access.** Who can see and act on a document depends on its state; moving state requires specific permissions and leaves an attributable, often commented, audit entry.
- **Register integrity is adjudicated.** Incoming material that matches an existing record becomes either a new revision or a new record — the system forces the choice so the register never silently forks.
- **Publication is attributable.** What was sent, to whom, in which revision, and what came back is part of the record — distribution is a controlled transaction, not a file copy.
- **Lineage extends to references.** A master document's references are managed at the revision level (pinned or follow-current), so a published set is internally consistent.
leaves.rules_zh:
- **当前修订版具有权威性。** 使用方基于当前批准的修订版工作；已废止的修订版保持可读但从不作为工作版本。只有当前修订版可以被签出以进行编辑。
- **变更被序列化。** 编辑锁防止对当前修订版进行并发修改；只读副本使其他人员保持高效。在一些产品中，提交工作和释放锁是可分离的动作。
- **批准是一个关口，而非一个标签。** 已发布/最终状态使文档无论权限如何都变为只读；重新打开需要遵循相同受控规则的新修订周期。
- **状态控制访问。** 谁能查看和操作文档取决于其状态；状态变更需要特定权限并留下可归因的、通常带有注释的审计条目。
- **登记完整性由系统裁定。** 匹配现有记录的新进材料将被强制选择成为新修订版或新记录——系统强制做出选择，使登记簿永远不会静默分裂。
- **发布是可归因的。** 发送了什么、发给谁、以哪个修订版、以及收到了什么回复，都是记录的一部分——分发是一个受控的交易，而非文件复制。
- **谱系延伸至引用。** 主文档的引用在修订版层级进行管理（固定或跟随当前），因此发布的集合在内部是一致的。

leaves.name: Engineering Productivity Analytics
leaves.overview:
An **Engineering Productivity Analytics** application is an engineering organization's measurement system for its own work process. It continuously assembles a record of the organization's software development activity from the tools where the work happens — version control, issue trackers, CI/CD, incident systems — computes defined process metrics over that record, and presents the results as dashboards and reports through which engineering leaders review delivery flow, investment balance, and developer experience, and drive improvement.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Engineering activity record (from the org's own dev tools)
└── Derived process metrics with defined semantics
    └── Insight surface for engineering management
        └── Improvement loop (goals, agreements, triage)
```

Everything else commonly associated with the category — team hierarchies, DORA metrics, developer surveys, benchmarks, AI-tool measurement, capitalization reporting — is widespread in current products but is not what makes the product this Type. The measurement intent predates all of it: before platforms automated the work, engineering leaders assembled the same picture by hand, aggregating version-control and issue-tracker data into spreadsheets — a practice the vendors in this category themselves document as the state their products replaced.

The subject of measurement is the **work process** — how code, review, and release flow, where engineering effort goes, how developers experience their environment. It is not the health of the code (that is the code-quality platform's subject) and not the behavior of production systems (that is observability's subject).
leaves.overview_zh:
一个**工程生产力分析**应用是工程组织对其自身工作流程的度量系统。它持续地从工作实际发生的工具中——版本控制、问题跟踪器、CI/CD、事件系统——汇编组织软件开发活动的记录，基于该记录计算既定的流程指标，并通过仪表板和报告呈现结果，工程领导者借此审视交付流程、投资平衡和开发者体验，并推动改进。

其定义性结构很简单：

```text
工程活动记录（来自组织自身的开发工具）
└── 具有定义语义的派生流程指标
    └── 供工程管理层使用的洞察界面
        └── 改进循环（目标、协议、分类处理）
```

与此类别通常相关的其他所有内容——团队层级结构、DORA 指标、开发者调查、基准测试、AI 工具衡量、资本化报告——在当前产品中普遍存在，但并非构成该**类型**产品的本质。度量的意图先于所有这些内容而存在：在平台自动化工作之前，工程领导者通过手动方式组装相同的图景，将版本控制和问题跟踪器数据汇总到电子表格中——这一实践在该类别供应商自己的文档中被记录为他们的产品所取代的状态。

度量的主题是**工作流程**——代码、评审和发布如何流转，工程精力投入何处，开发者如何体验其环境。它不是代码的健康度（那是代码质量平台的主题），也不是生产系统的行为（那是可观测性的主题）。
leaves.dc:
```text
Engineering activity record
└── Derived process metrics
    └── Insight surface for engineering management
```

Three structures. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as this Type:

- **Engineering activity record** — a persistent, continuously updated record of the organization's development activity, assembled from connected systems: code changes and reviews from version control, work items from issue trackers, pipeline and deployment events from CI/CD, incidents from incident tools. The record is built by observation, not by asking engineers to report or tag differently. Without it there is nothing to measure.
- **Derived process metrics** — measures computed over the record with explicit, inspectable definitions: how long work takes (cycle time and its phases), how much flows through (throughput, deployment frequency), how reliable the process is (change failure, rework), and where effort goes (investment distribution). Without defined metrics the product is just a data feed.
- **Insight surface for engineering management** — dashboards and reports through which leaders review trends over time, compare teams and periods, and act. Without it the product is a metrics pipeline, not an analytics application.
leaves.dc_zh:
工程活动记录
└── 派生过程指标
    └── 工程管理洞察界面

三个结构。如果任何一个被移除，产品就不再可识别为此类型：

- **工程活动记录** — 一个持久、持续更新的组织开发活动记录，从连接系统组装：来自版本控制的代码变更和审查、来自问题跟踪器的工作项、来自CI/CD的管道和部署事件、来自事件工具的事故。记录通过观察构建，而不是要求工程师报告或标记。如果没有它，就没有可测量的东西。
- **派生过程指标** — 在记录上计算的具有明确、可检查定义的指标：工作持续时间（周期时间及其阶段）、吞吐量（吞吐量、部署频率）、流程可靠性（变更失败、返工）、努力分布（投资分布）。如果没有定义指标，产品只是数据源。
- **工程管理洞察界面** — 领导者回顾趋势、比较团队和时期并采取行动的仪表板和报告。如果没有它，产品是指标管道，而不是分析应用程序。
leaves.rules:
### Metric semantics are product-defined and configurable

There is no industry-standard cycle time. Where the clock starts (first commit vs ticket moved to in-progress), what counts as a deployment, and which branches are excluded are all configuration choices, and products document that these choices materially change the numbers. Backfilled data can also retroactively adjust historical values. Two organizations comparing raw numbers are often not comparing the same thing.

### Attribution is a modeled choice, not a fact

Which team gets credit for a change, which ticket a pull request belongs to, and whether a file is code or test are all inferred by rules the organization configures. Products track team membership historically so attribution survives reorganizations, but the attribution itself remains a model of the org, not the org itself.

### Individual-level visibility is governed, and the category polices itself

Products in this category commonly treat individual-level metrics as a governed surface: role-based visibility settings (from open to leaders-only to fully hidden), team-scoped views, and in the strongest documented case de-identification that redacts a person across all reports while keeping aggregates accurate — a posture documented for works-council and regional-law contexts. Product guidance in this category explicitly cautions against using the metrics for individual performance evaluation, and at least one product recommends assembling any such composite report outside the platform. The measurement system is designed for process improvement, and using it as surveillance is both a trust risk and — per the vendors' own guidance — a measurement-quality risk, because developers who know they are individually measured change their behavior.

### The metrics measure the process, not the output's value

A fast cycle time is not a good product; a large throughput is not a productive team. Products document their own metric limitations (deployment-dependent calculations, inflated coding time on long-lived branches, volatile small samples) and position the numbers as signals for conversation, not verdicts. The improvement loop — team-owned agreements, triage, retros — exists precisely because the numbers alone do not decide anything.

### Non-intrusion is a structural commitment

The record is assembled from tools engineers already use; engineers do not tag, timer, or report differently for the system's sake. This is what distinguishes the Type from time tracking and from manual reporting practices, and it is also why the data can go stale in exactly the places the org's own hygiene is weak (for example, unmapped tickets or misconfigured deployment detection).
leaves.rules_zh:
### 指标语义由产品定义且可配置

没有行业标准的周期时间。时钟从何时开始（首次提交 vs 工单移至“进行中”）、什么算作一次部署、哪些分支被排除在外，这些都是配置选择，而产品文档指出这些选择会实质性地改变数值。回填数据也可能追溯性地调整历史值。两个组织比较原始数字时，往往比较的并非同一事物。

### 归因是一种建模选择，而非事实

哪个团队因一项变更获得认可、一个拉取请求属于哪个工单、一个文件是代码还是测试，这些都由组织配置的规则推断得出。产品会历史地跟踪团队成员信息，因此归因在重组后仍然有效，但归因本身仍然是组织的一个模型，而非组织本身。

### 个人层面的可见性受到管控，该类别进行自我监管

该类别的产品通常将个人层面的指标视为受管控的界面：基于角色的可见性设置（从开放到仅限领导层可见再到完全隐藏）、团队范围内的视图，以及在记录最详尽的情况下去标识化处理——在所有报告中删除个人信息，同时保持聚合数据的准确性——这种立场是为职工委员会和区域法律背景而制定的。该类别的产品指南明确警告不要将指标用于个人绩效评估，至少有一款产品建议在平台之外编写任何此类综合报告。度量系统是为流程改进而设计的，将其用作监控工具既是一种信任风险，而且——根据供应商自身的指南——也是一种度量质量风险，因为知道自己被单独衡量的开发者会改变其行为。

### 度量的范围是演进的

leaves.name: Engineering Project Management Platform
leaves.name_zh: 软件工程项目管理平台
leaves.overview:
An **Engineering Project Management Platform** is an engineering organization's system of record for planning and tracking software delivery work. Teams capture planned work as typed work items — features, stories, bugs, tasks — organize them in an engineering container (project, repository, team), group them into delivery containers such as releases, versions, milestones, or iterations, and track each item from planning through the code changes that implement it to shipping.

The defining core is small:

```text
Engineering container (project / repo / team)
└── Work items of software delivery (typed, with workflow status)
    ├── Bound to the code changes that implement them
    │   (branches, commits, pull/merge requests)
    └── Grouped into delivery containers (release / version / milestone / iteration)
        └── Progress toward shipping
```

Three properties held together. Remove the work items and nothing is being managed; remove the binding to code changes and the product is a generic or agile work tracker with the engineering subject gone; remove the delivery containers and it is issue tracking with no delivery management.

Everything else commonly associated with this category — ordered backlogs, boards, sprints, estimation, velocity and burndown charts, epics, roadmaps, cross-team plans — is standard capability shared with agile project management tools, not what makes the product an engineering delivery system. The full development lifecycle in one product (repositories, CI/CD, test management, deployments) is a common suite form, not a requirement.
leaves.overview_zh:
一个**工程项目管理平台**是工程组织规划与跟踪软件交付工作的系统记录。团队将计划的工作捕获为类型化的工作项——功能、用户故事、缺陷、任务——将它们组织在一个工程容器（项目、代码仓库、团队）中，将它们分组到诸如发布、版本、里程碑或迭代等交付容器中，并跟踪每个项目从规划到实现它的代码变更，再到最终交付的全过程。

其定义核心精简如下：

```text
工程容器（项目 / 代码仓库 / 团队）
└── 软件交付工作项（类型化，具有工作流状态）
    ├── 绑定到实现它们的代码变更
    │   （分支、提交、拉取/合并请求）
    └── 分组到交付容器（发布 / 版本 / 里程碑 / 迭代）
        └── 面向交付的进展
```

三个属性相互依存。移除工作项，则无物可管理；移除与代码变更的绑定，产品将变成一个通用或敏捷的工作跟踪器，失去了工程主题；移除交付容器，则变成了没有交付管理的问题跟踪。

与该类别通常相关的所有其他内容——有序的待办事项列表、看板、冲刺、估算、速率与燃尽图、史诗、路线图、跨团队计划——是与敏捷项目管理工具共享的标准能力，并非该产品作为工程交付系统的核心所在。将完整的开发生命周期（代码仓库、CI/CD、测试管理、部署）整合在一个产品中是一种常见的套件形式，而非必要条件。
leaves.dc:
**Work items.** The unit of planned and tracked work is a persistent, typed record — commonly a story or feature, a bug, a task, and a larger grouping such as an epic — carrying an owner, a status, and descriptive fields. Items form hierarchies (epic → item → subtask) and carry typed relationships (blocks, duplicates, relates to). Bugs are ordinary work items here, not a separate system.

**Development-artifact binding.** Work items are linked to the code changes that implement them: branches, commits, and pull/merge requests. The link is maintained by the system, not by memory — created from commit messages that reference the item, from branch names derived from it, from pull-request descriptions, or from explicit linking. The binding is live in both directions: the work item shows the state of its code (open PRs, reviews, builds, deployments where the platform covers them), and code events can move the item's status.

**Delivery containers.** Work is grouped into containers that represent a shipping event — a release or version, a milestone, or a timeboxed iteration — each with a target date and visible progress. A container collects the work items destined for a delivery and, in platform products, the associated code changes as well; its progress view answers "what is in this release, and how close is it to done?"

**Engineering container.** All of the above lives inside an engineering org container — a project, a repository or group of repositories, or a team workspace — which scopes visibility, workflow configuration, and permissions.
leaves.dc_zh:
**工作项。** 计划和跟踪的工作单元是一个持久的、类型化的记录——通常是一个故事或特性、一个缺陷、一个任务，以及更大的分组如史诗——携带所有者、状态和描述性字段。工作项形成层次结构（史诗 → 工作项 → 子任务）并携带类型化关系（阻塞、重复、关联）。在这里，缺陷是普通的工作项，不是一个单独的系统。

**开发工件绑定。** 工作项链接到实现它们的代码变更：分支、提交和拉取/合并请求。链接由系统维护，而不是靠记忆——从引用工作项的提交消息、从派生自工作项的分支名称、从拉取请求描述或从显式链接创建。绑定在两个方向上都是实时的：工作项显示其代码的状态（打开的PR、审查、构建、部署，如果平台覆盖的话），并且代码事件可以移动工作项的状态。

**交付容器。** 工作被分组到代表交付事件的容器中——一个发布或版本、一个里程碑，或一个时间盒迭代——每个都有目标日期和可见进度。容器收集注定用于交付的工作项，在平台产品中，还有相关的代码变更；其进度视图回答“这个发布中有什么，以及它离完成有多近？”

**工程容器。** 以上所有内容都存在于一个
leaves.rules:
### The binding is maintained by the system, through conventions

Links between items and code changes arise from naming and reference conventions — item IDs in branch names, commit messages, or pull-request descriptions — or from explicit linking. Teams adopt the conventions; the system enforces nothing about style but reliably creates and displays the links. Some products distinguish "closing" references (merge closes the item) from purely informational ones.

### Code events can drive item status — configurably

A pull request opening typically moves its item to in-progress; merging moves it to done or closes it. The mapping is team-configurable, including per-branch rules (e.g., merged to a staging branch means one state, merged to the main branch another). Automation can be disabled; the manual workflow always remains available.

### Containers span both work items and code changes

In platform products, a milestone or release view tracks not only items but the pull/merge requests themselves (open, waiting for merge, merged), because a delivery is not done until its changes are merged — an item can be "done" as work while its code is still unmerged. Products differ in how explicitly they model this; the delivery view is the place where the two object classes are reconciled.

### Bugs are first-class work items

Defect tracking is not a separate system here: bugs are an item type in the same backlog, workflow, and containers as features. A defect found in operation re-enters the same planning surface.

### Workflow states are team property

States, transitions, and what counts as "done" are configured per team or project; enterprise products normalize states into broad categories so cross-team reporting stays possible. Delivery metrics are computed from state transitions — changing the workflow changes the numbers.

### Progress is completed work, not percent-of-plan

There are no baselines or percent-complete schedules in the defining core. Progress is read as completed items and merged changes against the container's target — the same planning philosophy that distinguishes this family from plan-driven project management.

### Permissions follow the engineering container

Access is scoped by project/repo/team, with role differentiation (who can configure, who can plan, who can transition items, who can only read). Enterprise products add read-mostly stakeholder access tiers.
leaves.rules_zh:
### 绑定由系统通过约定维护

项与代码变更之间的链接源于命名和引用约定——在分支名称、提交消息或拉取请求描述中的项ID——或源于显式链接。团队采用这些约定；系统不强制执行任何样式，但可靠地创建和显示链接。一些产品区分'关闭'引用（合并会关闭该项）和纯粹信息性的引用。

### 代码事件可以驱动项状态——可配置

拉取请求的打开通常会将其关联项移至'进行中'状态；合并会将其移至'完成'或关闭。此映射由团队配置，包括按分支的规则（例如，合并到暂存分支意味着一个状态，合并到主分支则意味着另一个状态）。自动化可以禁用；手动工作流始终可用。

### 容器涵盖工作项和代码变更

在平台产品中，里程碑或发布视图不仅跟踪项，也跟踪拉取/合并请求本身（打开、等待合并、已合并），因为一个交付只有在变更合并后才算完成——一个项作为工作可能'完成'，但其代码可能仍未合并。不同产品对此建模的显式程度有所不同；交付视图是调和这两类对象的地方。

### 缺陷是一等公民工作项

在此，缺陷跟踪不是一个独立的系统：缺陷是一种工作项类型，与功能处于相同的待办列表、工作流和容器中。在运维中发现的缺陷重新进入相同的规划界面。

### 工作流状态是团队属性

状态、转换以及什么算作'完成'，按团队或项目进行配置；企业产品将状态规范化为广泛的类别，以便跨团队报告仍然可行。交付指标根据状态转换计算

leaves.name: Engineering Requirements Management
leaves.overview:
An **Engineering Requirements Management** application is the engineering organization's system of record for the requirements a product must satisfy. It captures each requirement as a persistent, individually identified record; organizes requirements into structured specifications; links them traceably to the stakeholder needs above them and the designs, tests, and risks below them; and manages their change through version history, baselines, and controlled review and approval.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Requirement of record
└── Structured specification (hierarchy / document / tree)
    └── Traceability links (upstream needs ↔ requirements ↔ design, tests, risks)
        └── Managed change (version history → baselines → controlled change)
```

Everything else commonly associated with these products — review centers with electronic signatures, test coverage machinery, reuse across product lines, ReqIF and Office interchange, generated specification documents, compliance report packs, AI-assisted requirement quality checks — is widespread in current products but is not what makes the product a requirements management system. Classic requirements tools used for decades in high-compliance programs, and even disciplined spreadsheet-and-document practice before them, exhibit the same four-part core without any of the modern additions.

When the center of gravity shifts away from the requirement record — to formal system models, to the physical product structure, to work items to be executed, or to market-facing prioritization — the product is drifting toward a different Application Type (MBSE Platform, PLM, Issue Tracker, Product Management Platform).
leaves.overview_zh:
一个**工程需求管理**应用程序是工程组织记录产品必须满足的需求的系统。它将每个需求捕获为持久、独立标识的记录；将需求组织成结构化的规范；将它们可追溯地链接到上游的利益相关者需求和下游的设计、测试、风险；并通过版本历史、基线和受控的评审和批准来管理其变更。

定义性结构很小：

```text
Requirement of record
└── Structured specification (hierarchy / document / tree)
    └── Traceability links (upstream needs ↔ requirements ↔ design, tests, risks)
        └── Managed change (version history → baselines → controlled change)
```

其他通常与这些产品相关的一切——带有电子签名的评审中心、测试覆盖机制、跨产品线的重用、ReqIF和Office交换、生成的规范文档、合规报告包、AI辅助的需求质量检查——在当前产品中很普遍，但不是使该产品成为需求管理系统的原因。经典需求工具在高合规性计划中使用了数十年，甚至之前的有纪律的电子表格和文档实践，都表现出相同的四部分核心，没有任何现代添加。

当重心从需求记录转移——到正式系统模型、物理产品结构、待执行的工作项或面向市场的优先级排序——产品正漂移向不同的应用类型（MBSE平台、PLM、问题跟踪器、产品管理平台）。
leaves.dc:
**The requirement of record.** A requirement is a persistent, individually identified statement of a capability, condition, or constraint the product must satisfy. Each requirement carries a stable unique identifier that survives edits and reorganizations, a statement (typically rich text), and attributes — commonly rationale, verification method, status, ownership, priority, and allocation to a discipline or release. Every change to a requirement produces a recorded version. Without stable requirement records there is nothing to manage.

**Structured specification.** Requirements are not a loose list. They live inside a project in a structured collection: a hierarchy of requirements, a specification document whose sections and paragraphs are individually addressable, or a tree of folders and modules organized by abstraction level and discipline. The structure expresses the specification's breakdown — stakeholder needs at the top, system requirements below them, subsystem and component requirements further down. Without structure, the product is a flat ticket list rather than an engineering specification.

**Traceability links.** Requirements are connected by explicit, typed, navigable links. Upstream links tie a requirement to the stakeholder need, regulation, or hazard it addresses; downstream links tie it to the requirements derived from it, the design elements that realize it, the test cases that verify it, and — in some products — the risks or source code related to it. Links are directional and typed (derive, satisfy, verify, and similar relationships), and they are the substrate for coverage: whether a requirement has been derived, designed, and verified is computed from the link graph. Without traceability, the product is a document editor.

**Managed change.** The requirement set evolves under control. Every requirement has a version history; the set can be frozen as a baseline — a named snapshot of the specification at a point in time — and changes after a baseline are proposed, analyzed for downstream impact, reviewed, and approved before they take effect. Baselines can be compared (what was added, removed, changed since the last one), and historical states remain inspectable. Without managed change, the product is a static snapshot, and the "management" in the Type name is gone.

These four are jointly held. A versioned document with numbered requirements but no links is requirements authoring, not management. A flat list of linked items with no specification structure loses the engineering character. Change machinery with no requirement records has nothing to change.
leaves.dc_zh:
**记录的要求。** 要求是产品必须满足的能力、条件或约束的持久、独立标识的陈述。每个要求都带有一个稳定的唯一标识符，该标识符在编辑和重组后仍然存在；一个陈述（通常是富文本）；以及属性——通常包括理由、验证方法、状态、所有权、优先级和分配给某个学科或版本。对要求的每次更改都会产生一个记录的版本。没有稳定的要求记录，就没有什么可管理的。

**结构化规范。** 要求不是一个松散的列表。它们在一个项目的结构化集合中：一个要求层次结构、一个规范文档（其章节和段落可以独立寻址）、或一个按抽象级别和学科组织的文件夹和模块树。该结构表达了规范的分解——利益相关者需求在顶部，系统需求在其下，子系统和组件需求更进一步。没有结构，产品将是一个扁平的工单列表，而不是一个工程规范。

**可追溯性链接。** 要求通过显式的、类型的、可导航的链接连接。上游链接将一个要求与它所解决的利益相关者需求、法规或危险联系起来；下游链接将它与其派生的要求、实现它的设计元素联系起来...
leaves.rules:
- **Identity is stable.** A requirement's unique ID persists across edits, moves, and renumbering; traceability depends on it. Deletion is typically controlled — some products deactivate rather than destroy, so history and links survive.
- **Baselines freeze.** After a baseline, the recorded set is immutable as a snapshot; further change happens as new, controlled versions. Comparisons are always against a named baseline.
- **Links are typed and directional.** Coverage is computed from the link graph, so an unlinked requirement is visibly unverified — the system makes gaps a first-class object, not an accident.
- **Workflow states and locks restrict editing.** Requirements under review, approved, or baselined are commonly locked or state-restricted; who may change what in which state is configurable and audited.
- **Signatures gate release.** In regulated settings, an approved-and-signed state is a precondition for releasing a specification to production; the signature record (who, what, when) is part of the audit trail.
- **Documents are outputs, not the record.** The specification document is generated from the requirement records. Editing the document outside the system breaks the record, which is why round-trip import/export and two-way Office sync exist.
- **Impact precedes approval.** Change proposals are evaluated by their downstream impact on derived requirements, designs, and tests before approval; propagation of approved changes is recorded per artifact.
leaves.rules_zh:
- **身份稳定。** 需求的唯一ID在编辑、移动和重新编号中持久存在；可追溯性依赖于它。删除通常是受控的——一些产品停用而不是销毁，因此历史和链接得以保留。
- **基线冻结。** 基线之后，记录的集合作为快照不可变；进一步的更改作为新的、受控的版本发生。比较总是针对命名的基线。
- **链接是有类型和方向的。** 覆盖率从链接图计算，因此未链接的需求明显未经验证——系统使缺口成为一等对象，而不是意外。
- **工作流状态和锁限制编辑。** 正在评审、已批准或已基线化的需求通常被锁定或状态受限；在哪个状态下谁可以更改什么是可配置和可审计的。
- **签名门控发布。** 在受控环境中，已批准和签名的状态是向生产发布规范的前提条件；签名记录（谁、什么、何时）是审计跟踪的一部分。
- **文档是输出，而不是记录。** 规范文档从需求记录生成。在系统外部编辑文档会破坏记录，这就是为什么往返导入/导出和双向Office同步存在。
- **影响先于批准。** 变更提案在批准之前根据其对派生需求、设计和测试的下游影响进行评估；批准变更的传播记录在每个工件中。

leaves.name: Enrollment Management
leaves.overview:
An **Enrollment Management** application is institution-operated software for managing who is actually committed to attend an educational institution for a specific academic period — new members arriving from admissions decisions and returning members renewing their place. It captures the commitment itself (enrollment contracts, deposits, offer acceptances), tracks each enrollee's readiness for the coming period, manages their enrollment standing through the period, and gives the enrollment office a population-level view of the period as a whole: who has committed, who is incomplete, who declined or withdrew.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Enrollment record — an identified person bound to the institution
                    for a specific academic period (year / term)
└── Commitment capture — the recorded binding act (signed contract and/or
    deposit / acceptance), completed by the family or student
└── Readiness tracking — per-enrollee requirements (forms, materials, payments)
    completed before the period starts
└── Managed standing — statuses including holds, withdrawal, and "not enrolling"
└── Population oversight — the period's enrollees tracked and worked as a whole
```

Everything else commonly associated with modern enrollment offices — family portals, e-signature machinery, bulk communications, aid-and-scholarship assembly, enrollment reporting, automatic re-enrollment models — is widespread standard capability, but the product remains enrollment management without it. Paper-era enrollment offices, SIS-embedded re-enrollment modules, and non-US institutions fit the same definition.

The market also uses "enrollment management" more broadly, as the name of a higher-education *discipline* spanning recruitment, admissions, yield, and retention, and as a suite label for products that bundle admissions and enrollment together. Those usages describe positioning over several application types; this document covers the distinct enrollment machinery itself. When the primary object becomes the *application to be evaluated* or the *prospect relationship*, the product has moved into Admissions Management or Student Recruitment CRM.
leaves.overview_zh:
一个**入学管理**应用程序是机构运营的软件，用于管理那些实际承诺在特定学术周期入学教育机构的人员——包括来自录取决定的新成员和续期学籍的回归成员。它捕获承诺本身（入学合同、押金、录取确认书），跟踪每位入学新生为即将到来的周期的准备情况，管理他们在该周期内的入学状态，并为招生办公室提供整个周期的人口级视图：谁已承诺、谁未完成手续、谁拒绝或撤回。

其核心结构定义清晰：

```text
入学记录——已绑定机构的指定人员
                    用于特定学术周期（学年/学期）
└── 承诺记录——已记录的绑定行为（签署合同和/或
    押金/录取确认），由家庭或学生完成
└── 准备跟踪——每位入学新生的要求（表格、材料、付款）
    需在周期开始前完成
└── 状态管理——包括保留状态、退出及“未入学”的状态
└── 人口监督——周期内所有入学新生作为整体进行跟踪和处理
```

现代招生办公室通常关联的其他所有功能——家庭门户、电子签名机制、批量沟通、助学金与奖学金组合、入学报表、自动重新入学模型——都是普遍标准功能，但即使没有这些，该产品仍属于入学管理。纸质时代的招生办公室、学生信息系统内嵌的重新入学模块以及非美国的机构均符合此定义。

市场也更广泛地使用“入学管理”一词，作为高等教育涵盖招生、录取、转化率和保留率的*学科*名称，以及作为捆绑招生和入学功能的产品套件标签。这些用法描述的是对多个应用类型的定位；本文档涵盖的是独立的入学机制本身。当主要对象变为*待评估的应用*或*潜在生源关系*时，该产品已进入招生管理或学生招募CRM领域。
leaves.dc: The central object is an enrollment: a binding of one identified person to one academic period of the institution — a school year, a term, or a comparable academic context. It is distinct from both the person record (who the student is, maintained across periods) and from any application record (the candidacy that may have produced an offer). One person accumulates a series of enrollments across periods, and a well-formed history survives withdrawal.
leaves.dc_zh: 核心对象是一个注册：一个已识别的人与机构的一个学术周期——学年、学期或类似学术背景——的绑定。它既不同于个人记录（学生是谁，跨周期维护），也不同于任何申请记录（可能产生录取的候选资格）。一个人在多个周期中积累一系列注册，并且一个格式良好的历史在退出后仍然存在。
leaves.rules:
### The institution controls document validity

Commitment documents are generated by the institution from configured terms; a family cannot commit against a document the institution has not issued, and an incorrectly generated document is corrected and reissued rather than edited in place. The family's completion is the second party of a two-party act.

### Signed commitments are treated as binding

Where the commitment is a legal contract, the signature is a binding boundary: terms and content can update dynamically before signature, but once signed, changes require reissuing the document rather than silently altering it — a discipline documented directly in the sampled contract machinery. In such configurations, deposit payment may be withheld until all required signatures exist.

### The deposit completes the commitment

Across implementations, the commitment is not complete on signature or confirmation alone: the deposit (or an equivalent payment) is part of the committed state, and "signed but unpaid" is a first-class chased state with its own follow-up patterns.

### Holds gate, exits preserve

Academic or financial holds can block a student's progression to enrolled standing until resolved. Withdrawal and "not enrolling" are managed exits: they remove the person from the active period population but keep the record, history, and (where applicable) any mid-period accounting of the departure.

### Eligibility and deadlines shape the season

Re-enrollment operations select their population by eligibility conditions (current standing, not in the final year, not already enrolled for the next period), and family access is deadline-governed; extending a deadline and re-sending is a normal operation, not an exception.

### Everything is period-scoped

Statuses, documents, checklists, and money all attach to a specific period; the same person appears in successive periods as a series of enrollments, and history is retained across periods rather than overwritten.

### Attribution and permissions matter

Commitment documents and payments are consequential: products separate financially responsible parties, support school countersigners as distinct roles, and carry role-based access to sensitive enrollment data (financial, health, conduct) in mature implementations.
leaves.rules_zh:
### 机构控制文件有效性

承诺文件由机构根据已配置的条款生成；家庭无法对机构未签发的文件做出承诺，且生成错误的文件会被更正并重新签发，而非直接编辑。家庭的完成是双方行为中的第二方。

### 签署的承诺被视为有约束力

在承诺为法律合同的情况下，签名是约束边界：条款和内容可在签名前动态更新，但一旦签署，更改需要重新签发文件而非静默修改——这是在抽样合同机制中直接记录的规范。在此类配置中，押金支付可能在所有必需签名齐全前被暂扣。

### 押金完成承诺

在所有实现中，仅凭签名或确认承诺并不完整：押金（或等效付款）是承诺状态的一部分，“已签未付”是一个一级催办状态，有其特定的跟进模式。

### 保留状态控制，退出保持记录

学术或财务保留状态可阻止学生进入已入学状态，直至问题解决。退出和“未入学”是受控退出：他们将人员从活跃周期人口中移除，但保留记录、历史以及（如适用）任何周期中途的会计记录。

### 资格与截止日期定义周期

重新入学操作根据资格条件（当前状态、非最后一年、未为下一周期入学）选择其人口，且家庭访问受截止日期控制；延长截止日期并重新发送是常规操作，而非例外。

### 一切皆为周期限定

状态、文件...

leaves.name: Enterprise AI Assistant
leaves.overview:
An **Enterprise AI Assistant** is an AI assistant that an organization buys, operates, and governs for its own workforce. Employees interact with it in natural language — asking questions, drafting work, summarizing material, analyzing information, and triggering actions in the organization's systems — and the assistant's responses are generated by AI models rather than fixed scripted flows.

The defining core is small:

```text
Organization-operated        the org provisions its people, administers, governs
└── Workforce-facing         serves the org's own employees in their work context
    └── AI-driven conversational assistance
                             natural-language requests → model-generated responses
```

Everything else the market associates with the category — grounding in company knowledge with citations, actions in connected systems, agents, embedding inside productivity apps, admin consoles, usage analytics — is standard equipment of mature products, not what makes the product an enterprise AI assistant. A minimally configured organization assistant with none of those extras is still recognizable as one; a consumer chat account, a customer-facing support bot, or a scripted FAQ bot is not, no matter how capable.

The Type sits at the top of the enterprise AI stack: enterprise search and data platforms supply what it draws on, AI gateways and governance layers route and restrain it, agent platforms extend it — but the assistant itself is the end-user product employees actually open.
leaves.overview_zh:
一个 **企业AI助手** 是一个组织为其员工购买、运营和管理的AI助手。员工使用自然语言与其交互——提出问题、起草工作内容、总结材料、分析信息以及触发组织系统中的操作——助手的回复由AI模型生成，而非固定的脚本流程。

其定义的核心要素非常精炼：

```text
组织运营型         组织为其人员配置、管理和治理
└── 面向员工         服务于组织自身的员工，在其工作场景中提供服务
    └── AI驱动的对话式协助
                             自然语言请求 → 模型生成的响应
```

市场与该类别关联的其他所有特性——基于公司知识的引用、在连接系统中的操作、代理、嵌入生产力应用、管理控制台、使用分析——都是成熟产品的标准配置，并非构成企业AI助手的必要条件。一个未配置任何此类附加功能的最小化组织助手，仍然可以被识别为该类型；而一个消费者聊天账户、一个面向客户的支持机器人，或一个脚本化的常见问题解答机器人，无论其功能多么强大，都不属于此类。

该类型位于企业AI技术栈的顶端：企业搜索和数据平台为其提供数据源，AI网关和治理层负责路由和约束，代理平台对其进行扩展——但助手本身才是员工实际使用的终端产品。
leaves.dc:
Three properties, held together:

- **Organization-operated.** The customer is the organization, not the individual. The organization attaches the assistant to its workforce identity, pays per its own arrangement, administers it, and governs it. This is what separates an enterprise assistant from a consumer AI chat account — the same underlying model technology serves both, but the consumer surface has no organizational operator, no workforce identity, and no admin layer.
- **Workforce-facing.** The served population is the organization's own people acting in their work context. This is what separates it from customer-facing chatbots and guest-facing concierges, which serve the organization's customers and visitors. Where a product offers a public-facing mode, it is an explicit exception configuration, not the center.
- **AI-driven conversational assistance.** The employee states what they need in natural language; the assistant understands the request and generates its response. This is what separates it from scripted decision-tree bots (which can only follow pre-authored paths) and from search UIs (which return lists, not composed assistance).
leaves.dc_zh:
三个属性，紧密结合：
- **组织运营。** 客户是组织，而不是个人。组织将助手与其员工身份关联，按自身安排支付费用，管理并治理它。这就是企业助手与消费者AI聊天账户的区别——底层模型技术相同，但消费者界面没有组织运营者、员工身份和管理层面。
- **面向员工。** 服务对象是组织自身的人员在其工作上下文中行动。这就是它与面向客户的聊天机器人和面向访客的礼宾服务的区别，后者服务组织的客户和访客。如果产品提供面向公众的模式，那是明确的例外配置，而非核心。
- **AI驱动的对话式辅助。** 员工用自然语言陈述需求；助手理解请求并生成响应。这就是它与脚本化决策树机器人（只能遵循预设路径）和搜索界面（返回列表而非组合辅助）的区别。
leaves.rules:
### The assistant is an access-control surface, not a bypass

Permission scoping is the load-bearing rule of the Type: answers are composed from content the asking user may already access, and permission changes in the source systems are reflected in what the assistant will surface. This makes the assistant simultaneously a productivity tool and an extension of the organization's information-access model — which is why its deployment is an administrative decision rather than an individual one.

### Grounding posture is an organization decision

Whether the assistant may answer from enterprise data only, or may also use the public web, or may fall back on general model knowledge, is configured by the administrator. When the answer is outside the permitted material, the assistant reports that it could not find it rather than improvising — unless the organization allowed the fallback.

### Citations are the verification mechanism

Grounded answers carry their sources. The employee is expected to check them before acting; the organization expects the trail for trust and audit.

### The assistant supports, does not replace, human decisions

Products state this explicitly for high-stakes domains (for example, employment or evaluative decisions): the assistant informs and executes, while accountable humans decide. Guardrails and governance machinery express the same posture elsewhere.

### Administration gates capability

Features are enabled or removed at the organization level: web access, image generation, agent creation and use, model selection, even the assistant itself. An employee's experience is the intersection of their permissions and the organization's policy.

### Conversations persist, briefly

Conversation history is retained for a bounded period (windows vary by product) so employees can resume and search prior exchanges; retention is part of the organization's data-governance surface. Queries, answers, and actions are commonly logged for audit.
leaves.rules_zh:
### 助手是访问控制面，而非绕过手段

权限范围是该类型的核心支撑规则：回答由请求用户可能已有权限访问的内容组成，源系统中的权限变更会反映在助手呈现的内容中。这使得助手同时是生产力工具和组织信息访问模型的扩展——因此其部署是一项管理决策，而非个人决策。

### 知识依据是组织决策

助手是否仅可依据企业数据回答，是否可使用公共网络，或是否可回退到通用模型知识，由管理员配置。当答案超出被允许的材料范围时，助手会报告无法找到，而非随意编造——除非组织允许回退。

### 引用是验证机制

有依据的回答会附带其来源。员工被期望在行动前进行核查；组织期望有追踪记录以建立信任并支持审计。

### 助手辅助而非替代人类决策

产品在高风险领域（例如雇佣或评估决策）会明确说明这一点：助手提供信息并执行操作，而负有责任的人类做出决定。防护机制和治理工具在其他地方体现了同样的立场。

### 管理控制着功能

功能在组织层面被启用或禁用：网络访问、图像生成、代理创建和使用、模型选择，甚至助手本身。员工的体验是其个人权限与组织策略的交集。

### 对话记录会短暂保存

对话历史会保留一段有限的时间（窗口期因

leaves.name: Enterprise Asset Management / EAM
leaves.overview:
An **Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) application** is an organization's system of record for the physical assets it operates — plant, equipment, vehicles, facilities, infrastructure — held across their entire service life: from acquisition, through years of operation and maintenance, to decommissioning and disposal.

It solves a problem that only appears at organizational scale: an asset-intensive organization owns thousands of individually distinct, long-lived, expensive things that must stay in service, and every one of them accumulates money, work, risk, and history over a lifespan measured in decades. Departmental spreadsheets and tribal knowledge can schedule a repair; they cannot answer, with evidence, the questions that recur at the organizational level: *What do we own, where is it, what condition is it in? What has it cost us to keep alive — and what will it cost to keep it alive next year? When does it stop being worth repairing? Can we prove any of this to auditors, regulators, and insurers?*

The defining core is three structures held together in one system:

```text
Enterprise asset register      — what the organization owns, as identified records
Maintenance work management    — the work that keeps each asset in service
Whole-life asset governance    — what the asset costs and how its life ends
```

The second structure is, on its own, the territory of maintenance management systems (CMMS). What makes a product an EAM is that the asset is managed as a long-lived, cost-bearing entity *from acquisition to disposal* — with whole-life cost and lifecycle state as first-class, inspectable structures — at the scope of the whole organization rather than a single maintenance department.
leaves.overview_zh:
一个**企业资产管理系统（EAM）**是组织用于管理其运营实物资产——工厂、设备、车辆、设施、基础设施——在其整个服务寿命周期内（从采购、经过多年的运营和维护，到退役和处置）的记录系统。

它解决的问题只在组织层面才会显现：一个资产密集型的组织拥有成千上万个各不相同、寿命长久、昂贵且必须保持在用的物品，而每一件物品在其长达数十年的生命周期中，都会积累资金、工作、风险和历史。部门电子表格和经验知识可以安排一次维修；但它们无法有证据地回答在组织层面反复出现的问题：*我们拥有什么资产？它们在哪里？状态如何？我们维持它们运转花了多少钱——明年需要多少钱？什么时候它们就不值得维修了？我们能向审计师、监管机构和保险公司证明这一切吗？*

其定义性的核心是由三个结构在一个系统中组合而成：

```text
企业资产登记册       — 组织所拥有的资产，作为已识别的记录
维护工作管理         — 使每个资产保持在用的工作
全生命周期资产治理   — 资产的成本以及其生命周期如何结束
```

第二个结构本身是维护管理系统（CMMS）的领域。使一个产品成为EAM的是，该资产作为长期的、承载成本的实体*从采购到处置*被管理——全生命周期成本和生命周期状态是首要的、可检查的结构——范围是整个组织，而非单个维护部门。
leaves.dc:
### Standard capabilities of mature products

These are expected in current EAM products but do not define the type — several are inherited from the maintenance-management core the type contains:

- **Preventive maintenance engine** — recurring schedules per asset triggered by calendar time, meter/usage readings, or condition data, generating work orders automatically; reusable job plans and task lists.
- **Work request intake** — anyone in the organization (often without a license) can report a problem or a need; requests are screened by criticality, safety, and compliance, then converted into work orders.
- **MRO spare-parts inventory** — storerooms and bins, stock levels, reservations against upcoming work, reorder points and replenishment, parts issued to work orders and costed to the asset.
- **Procurement linkage** — purchasing parts and services directly from work; supplier records; contracted (external) maintenance labor; supplier warranty tracking against repairs.
- **Planning and scheduling surfaces** — backlog views, calendars, resource availability, dispatch of the right skills to the right job.
- **Mobile execution** — technicians work from a device, online or offline: asset lookup by barcode/RFID scan, step execution, photos, measurements, confirmations.
- **Multi-site governance** — a shared asset and work structure across sites and regions, with role-scoped visibility and organization-wide standards.
- **Analytics and reporting** — asset health, downtime, backlog, preventive-maintenance compliance, and maintenance cost analysis (planned versus actual, total cost of ownership).
- **Integration fabric** — connections to ERP/finance, procurement, sensors/SCADA/IIoT (condition triggers opening work orders), GIS for spatial assets, and engineering document systems.
leaves.dc_zh:
### 成熟产品的标准能力

这些是当前EAM产品中预期的功能，但不定义该类型——其中一些继承自该类型包含的维护管理核心：

- **预防性维护引擎** — 基于日历时间、计量/使用读数或状态数据，按资产触发重复计划，自动生成工作订单；可重用的作业计划和任务列表。
- **工作请求接收** — 组织内的任何人（通常无需许可证）可以报告问题或需求；请求根据紧急性、安全性和合规性进行筛选，然后转换为工作订单。
- **MRO备件库存** — 仓库和货箱、库存水平、针对即将到来工作的预留、再订购点和补充、分配给工作订单的部件并计入资产成本。
- **采购链接** — 直接从工作中采购部件和服务；供应商记录；合同（外部）维护劳动力；针对维修的供应商保修跟踪。
- **规划和调度界面** — 待办事项视图、日历、资源可用性、将正确技能分配给正确工作。
- **移动执行** — 技术人员使用设备工作，联机或脱机：通过条形码/RFID扫描查找资产、步骤执行、照片、测量、确认。
- **多站点治理** — 跨站点和区域的共享资产和工作结构，具有角色范围的可视性。
leaves.rules:
- **The work order is the unit of accountability.** Labor, parts, services, and findings are recorded against work orders bound to assets; undocumented work is, from the system's perspective, work that did not happen. This is what makes asset history and cost trustworthy.
- **History is append-and-retain.** Closed work orders and lifecycle events persist on the asset, including after retirement. Disposal ends the asset's active state, not its record — the register remains usable as audit and regulatory evidence.
- **The hierarchy governs roll-up.** Costs, downtime, and failure statistics aggregate through the location/functional hierarchy, so a site or system manager sees the whole while technicians work the unit.
- **Triggers are layered.** Preventive work originates from calendar time, from meter/usage readings, and — where condition monitoring is connected — from machine data crossing thresholds. The same work-order engine consumes all of them.
- **Requests are gated, access is not universal.** Requesters can submit without holding maintenance roles; screening (criticality, safety, compliance) decides what becomes work. Execution surfaces are role-scoped: what a technician, planner, or asset manager may see and do is controlled, and audited.
- **Organization-wide scope is structural.** The register, standards, and schedules are shared across sites; local variation is configuration within the governance structure, not separate systems.
- **Finance stays reachable but separate.** Asset costs accumulate in the EAM and post outward to the finance system; even where the EAM is an ERP module, general-ledger accounting remains a finance concern. The EAM's contract is visibility — what each asset has cost and why — not bookkeeping.
leaves.rules_zh:
- **工单是问责单位。** 人工、部件、服务和发现都被记录在绑定到资产的工单上；从系统的角度来看，未记录的工作就是未发生的工作。这就是资产历史和成本可靠的原因。
- **历史记录是追加且保留的。** 已关闭的工单和生命周期事件在资产上持续存在，包括在退役后。处置结束了资产的活动状态，而非其记录——登记册保留可用作审计和监管证据。
- **层级控制汇总。** 成本、停机时间和故障统计通过位置/功能层级进行聚合，因此站点或系统经理可以看到全貌，而技术人员则处理单个单元。
- **触发是分层的。** 预防性工作源自日历时间、来自计量/使用读数，以及——在连接了状态监测的情况下——来自超过阈值的机器数据。同一个工单引擎处理所有这些。
- **请求是受控的，访问并非普遍。** 请求者无需拥有维护角色即可提交；筛选（关键性、安全、合规性）决定哪些成为工作。执行界面是角色限定的：技术人员、规划人员或资产经理可以看到和执行什么受到控制和审计。
- **全组织范围是结构性的。** 登记册、标准和计划在站点之间共享；本地差异是治理结构内的配置，而非独立系统。
- **财务保持可达但独立。** 资产成本在EAM中累积并向外发送到财务系统；即使EAM是ERP模块，总账核算仍然是财务部门的事务。EAM的契约是可见性——每个资产花了多少钱以及为什么——而非簿记。

leaves.name: Enterprise Asset Registry
aliases_zh: 企业固定资产管理系统
leaves.overview:
An **Enterprise Asset Registry** is an organization's item-level system of record for the things it holds: one durable, individually identified record per asset — equipment, devices, tools, vehicles, furniture, instruments — carrying the organization's own identifier for the item, its classification, its acquisition context, and its tracked state over time: current status, location, and who holds it.

The problem it solves is accountability at scale. Organizations acquire, deploy, lend, move, and retire thousands of individually distinct items across sites and departments. Spreadsheets and tribal knowledge cannot answer, with evidence, the questions that recur constantly: *What do we have? Where is it? Who has it? What condition is it in? Can we prove it?* The registry exists to answer those questions against a single maintained record per item, and to keep the records true through custody events and periodic verification rather than occasional manual cleanups.

Its defining core is deliberately narrow: an organization-scoped register of individually identified holdings — one persistent record per item, with tracked per-item state (status, location, custody) maintained over time and retained through retirement. Financial reporting depth, maintenance programs, reservation queues, and IT-specific automation are common additions that push a product toward neighboring types (accounting, CMMS/EAM, ITAM), not part of what makes a registry a registry. The definition also fits the older, pre-software forms of the same practice — the numbered paper asset register maintained by facilities or finance — which is the same record system without the scanning and cloud machinery.
leaves.overview_zh:
一个**企业资产注册系统**是组织内部用于记录其所持物品的、基于项目级别的权威系统：为每项资产——设备、装置、工具、车辆、家具、仪器——提供一份持久的、独立标识的记录，该记录携带组织自身的唯一标识符、资产的分类信息、获取背景，以及随时间变化的被跟踪状态：当前状况、位置和持有者。

它解决的问题是大规模环境下的责任归属问题。组织在不同地点和部门获取、部署、借用、移动和退役成千上万件独立的物品。电子表格和口口相传的知识无法回答那些反复出现的问题，并且无法提供证据：*我们有什么？它在哪里？谁在保管它？它状况如何？我们能证明吗？* 注册系统存在的意义，就是通过维护每项物品的单一记录来回答这些问题，并通过监管事件和定期验证，而非偶尔的手动清理，来确保记录的准确性。

其定义的核心是刻意收窄的：一个组织范围内的、独立标识资产的登记簿——每项物品一份持久记录，其随时间变化的逐项状态（状况、位置、保管权）得到跟踪和维护，并在退役后保留。财务报告深度、维护计划、预约队列以及 IT 专用自动化是常见的附加功能，它们会推动产品向邻近类型（会计、CMMS/EAM、ITAM）靠拢，但这些并非构成一个注册系统的要素。该定义同样适用于该实践在软件出现之前的旧形式——由设施或财务部门维护的编号纸质资产登记簿——那是在没有扫描和云技术架构下的同一套记录系统。
leaves.dc:
```text
Organization (owner of the register)
└── Asset record — one per individually identified item
    ├── Identity        — the organization's own identifier (asset tag / label),
    │                     typically alongside the manufacturer serial
    ├── Classification  — what it is (model/type, category, manufacturer)
    ├── Holding terms   — owned / leased / issued; acquisition date & cost, supplier
    ├── Tracked state   — status (available / deployed / under maintenance / retired…)
    │                     + current location + current custodian
    └── History         — dated log of movements, changes, and verifications
```

Four properties carry the type:

- **One record per individually identified item.** The registry counts things by identity, not by quantity. Ten identical laptops are ten records, not "10 units". This is the structural divide from inventory/stock systems, which track quantities of undifferentiated stock. (Registry products commonly *also* carry quantity-tracked classes for consumables, licenses, and bulk stock — an accommodation, not the core.)
- **Organization-level identity.** Each record carries an identifier the organization controls — an asset tag or label, often a scannable barcode or QR code — in addition to any manufacturer serial. This identifier is how the physical item and its record are matched in the field.
- **Tracked per-item state over time.** Status (availability/condition), current location, and current custodian are living attributes, updated by recorded events — checkout, return, transfer, audit — rather than occasional re-typing. The dated event log is what makes a record usable as evidence later.
- **Persistence through retirement.** Retiring, disposing of, or archiving an item ends its active state, not its record. Past records remain queryable; this is what makes the register usable as audit and insurance evidence.
leaves.dc_zh:
文本
拥有者（登记簿组织方）
└── 资产记录——每个独立识别的项目对应一条
    ├── 标识        — 组织自身的标识符（资产标签/编号），通常伴随厂商序列号
    ├── 分类        — 物品属性（型号/类型、类别、制造商）
    ├── 持有条款    — 所有权/租赁/发放状态；获取日期与成本、供应商
    ├── 追踪状态    — 状态（可用/已部署/维护中/已退役…）
    │                     + 当前位置 + 当前保管人
    └── 历史记录    — 按时间记录的移动、变更与验证日志

四个核心属性定义该类型：
- **每个独立识别项目对应一条记录。** 登记簿按身份标识计数物品，而非按数量。十台相同笔记本电脑对应十条记录，而非“10台”。这与跟踪无差别库存数量的库存/仓库系统形成本质区别。（登记簿产品通常也兼容数量追踪类目，用于消耗品、许可证及批量库存——这是适配扩展，而非核心定义）
- **组织级身份标识。** 每条记录包含组织自主控制的标识符（资产标签/编号，通常为可扫描条形码或二维码），与厂商序列号并列。该标识符用于现场匹配物理物品与其记录。
- **按项追踪状态
leaves.rules:
- **Identity is expected to be unique per item.** The register's integrity rests on one-record-per-item; products support manual or auto-generated tag schemes, and identity is what field interactions resolve against.
- **Custody is a tracked state, not a note.** Who holds an item is a first-class attribute with an event history; movement without a recorded event is precisely the failure mode the register exists to prevent.
- **Custody binding is broader than people.** Items can be assigned to locations and to other assets — a rack slot, a vehicle, a parent machine — which is how nested and site-bound holdings stay addressable.
- **Status vocabularies are organization-configurable.** Concepts like available / deployed / under maintenance / retired appear across products, but the exact states — and which states count as "deployable" — are configured per organization.
- **Verification is a designed loop, not an afterthought.** Audit schedules, acceptance confirmation, and self-report exist because registry data decays; products treat keeping records true as part of the workflow, and unanswered verifications surface as alerts.
- **Retirement retains the record.** Deleted history would defeat the audit purpose; ended items are archived with their history intact.
- **Non-unique holdings follow different mechanics.** Consumables, license seats, and bulk stock are commonly tracked as quantity records (with their own check-out semantics) rather than per-item records, inside the same product.
- **Permissions mirror accountability.** Who may view, request, check out, move, or administer is controlled — often scoped by location or organization unit — because custody records are accountability records.
leaves.rules_zh:
- **身份标识预期为每项物品唯一。** 注册系统的完整性建立在一条物品一条记录的基础上；产品支持手动或自动生成标签方案，身份标识是现场交互所依据的基准。
- **保管权是一种被跟踪的状态，而非备注。** 谁持有某件物品是一项具有事件历史的一等属性；未经记录事件的移动，正是该注册系统旨在防止的失效模式。
- **保管权绑定的对象范围超越人员。** 物品可以被分配给地点和其他资产——一个机架插槽、一辆载具、一台母机——这是嵌套式和场地绑定式资产保持可寻址性的方式。
- **状态词汇表由组织可配置。** 类似可用 / 已部署 / 维修中 / 已退役的概念在不同产品中普遍存在，但具体的状态——以及哪些状态被视为“可部署”——由每个组织配置。
- **验证是设计好的循环，而非事后补充。** 审计计划、验收确认和自行报告的存在，是因为注册数据会衰减；产品将保持记录准确性作为工作流程的一部分，而未响应的验证会作为警报提示。
- **退役保留记录。** 删除历史记录会违背审计目的；已结束的物品会以其完整的历史记录被归档。
- **非唯一性资产遵循不同的机制。** 消耗品、许可证席位和散装库存通常作为数量记录（具有其自己的借出语义）而非逐项记录在同一产品内跟踪。
- **权限映射责任。** 谁可以查看、请求、借出、移动或管理受到控制——通常按地点或组织单元划分范围——因为保管记录就是责任记录。

leaves.name: Enterprise Content Management
leaves.overview:
An **Enterprise Content Management (ECM) application** is an organization-operated system of record for its business content: content is captured into a central, governed repository under organization rules, described with organization-defined metadata and document types, secured by organization-defined permissions, tracked through change, moved through document-centric processes, and held over time under retention rules until an authorized retirement or disposition.

It solves a problem no personal or team storage tool addresses: an organization's contracts, invoices, HR files, policies, correspondence, engineering documents, and scanned paper must survive employee turnover, satisfy auditors and regulators, remain findable for decades, and be disposable only under controlled rules.

The defining core is deliberately small. Everything commonly associated with ECM in the market — workflow automation, records schedules, scanning/OCR, AI classification, web publishing, digital asset management — is widespread in current products but is not what makes the product ECM. When the center of gravity shifts to publishing web content, indexing systems the product does not manage, or personal file storage, the product has drifted toward a different Application Type (CMS, Enterprise Search, cloud drive).
leaves.overview_zh:
**企业内容管理（ECM）应用**是组织为其业务内容运营的记录系统：内容根据组织规则被捕获到一个集中、受管的存储库中，通过组织定义的元数据和文档类型进行描述，通过组织定义的权限进行保护，跟踪变更过程，穿越以文档为中心的流程，并根据保留规则长期保存，直至经授权进行退役或处置。

它解决了个人或团队存储工具均未涉及的一个问题：组织的合同、发票、人事文件、政策、信函、工程文档和扫描纸质文件必须经受员工流动的影响，满足审计员和监管机构的要求，在数十年内保持可查找性，并且只能在受控规则下进行处置。

其定义性核心刻意保持精简。市场上通常与ECM相关的所有功能——工作流自动化、记录计划、扫描/OCR、AI分类、网站发布、数字资产管理——在当前产品中都很普遍，但并非产品成为ECM的核心要素。当产品的重心转向发布网络内容、索引其未管理的系统或个人文件存储时，该产品就已偏离并趋向于另一种应用类型（CMS、企业搜索、云盘）。
leaves.dc:
```text
Organization-operated repository
└── Controlled capture/intake of content
    └── Content item described by organization-defined metadata / document types
        └── Organization-governed access (permissions)
            └── Managed persistence across the content lifecycle
                (durable retention + tracked change + eventual retirement/disposition)
```

Five properties. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as ECM:

- **Organization-operated repository** — the organization's unstructured content (documents, email, images, records) held as individually identified, managed items in a system operated for the organization. Without it, the product is personal or team storage.
- **Controlled capture/intake** — content enters under organization rules: check-in with required description, scan/capture pipelines, email filing, or feeds from business systems. Without it, the system is an indexing or sharing surface, not a system of record.
- **Organization-defined description** — every item carries metadata and/or belongs to a defined document type (for example "Invoice", "Contract", "Personnel File"). The description is what makes content organizable, retrievable, and governable at organizational scale. Without it, the product collapses into a shared drive with folders.
- **Organization-governed access** — permissions determine who can see and act on content, set by the organization rather than by individual file owners alone.
- **Managed persistence across the content lifecycle** — content is retained durably as the organization's record, kept consistent under successive or concurrent edits (versioning where content is revisable), and eventually retired or disposed under organization rules, with actions on it tracked. Without lifecycle governance, the product is file sharing.
leaves.dc_zh:
组织运营的仓库
└── 受控的内容捕获/摄入
    └── 由组织定义的元数据/文档类型描述的内容项
        └── 组织管理的访问权限（权限）
            └── 跨内容生命周期的受管理持久化
                （持久保留 + 跟踪变更 + 最终退役/处置）
leaves.rules:
### Description precedes management

Content must be described (metadata/type) to be governed. Products enforce required fields at intake; auto-classification exists precisely to reduce the human cost of that requirement. Items without description sit outside the governance system (some products explicitly surface them as "unmanaged" until promoted).

### Retention overrides ordinary deletion

Once retention applies — and especially once an item is declared a record — ordinary edit/delete rights are suspended: records may block content edits, deletion, or both, until the retention period is satisfied and an authorized review disposes of the item. Legal holds suspend disposition entirely, even over administrator objections; in the strictest configurations a record status cannot be removed by anyone.

### Permissions come from the organization

Access follows organization-defined rules — inherited through containers, attached to the item, or derived from metadata. Changing an item's classification can change who sees it. Deny rules and metadata-driven security mean the same folder can show different content to different roles.

### Workflow state gates action

Items carry state (draft, in review, released, superseded, archived), and transitions are guarded: only users in the right role, with the right fields populated, can move an item forward. The state is visible on the item and drives the task queues.

### Everything leaves evidence

Access, edits, permission changes, workflow steps, holds, and dispositions are logged and attributable. The audit trail is not a diagnostic extra; it is part of the product's value as a system of record.

### Exceptions that recur in real use

- content captured with wrong or missing metadata (misfiling that must be corrected without losing audit history)
- duplicate or near-duplicate documents (multiple versions of "the same" contract)
- items under hold that cannot be destroyed despite an expired retention period
- disposition events waiting on a manual review that must not be skipped or bulk-approved
- external/legacy content (file shares, paper archives) that must be surfaced or scheduled without clean metadata
- capture/conversion failures producing partial or unsearchable results that must be reprocessed
leaves.rules_zh:
### 描述先于管理

内容必须被描述（元数据/类型）才能被治理。产品在捕获时强制要求填写必填字段；自动分类的存在正是为了降低该要求的人力成本。没有描述的项目位于治理体系之外（有些产品会明确将其显示为“未受管”，直至其被提升）。

### 保留优先于普通删除

一旦保留生效——特别是当项目被声明为记录后——普通的编辑/删除权限即被暂停：记录可能会阻止内容编辑、删除或两者兼有，直到保留期限满足且经授权审查处置该项目。法律保留则完全暂停处置，即使管理员反对；在最严格的配置中，记录状态无法被任何人移除。

### 权限来源于组织

访问遵循组织定义的规则——通过容器继承、附加到项目，或从元数据派生。更改项目的分类可能会改变谁能看到它。拒绝规则和基于元数据的安全性意味着同一个文件夹可以向不同角色显示不同的内容。

### 工作流状态门控操作

项目带有状态（草稿、审查中、已发布、已被取代、已归档），并且状态转换受到门控：只有处于正确角色、且填写了正确字段的用户才能将项目向前推进。状态在项目上可见，并驱动任务队列。

### 所有操作都留下证据

访问、编辑、权限变更、工作流步骤、保留和处置都被记录且可追溯。审计跟踪并非附加的诊断工具；它是该产品作为记录系统价值的一部分。

### 实际使用中反复出现的例外情况

- 内容以错误或缺失的元数据被捕获（需要在不丢失的情况下进行纠正的错误归档）

leaves.name: Enterprise Knowledge Assistant
leaves.overview:
An **Enterprise Knowledge Assistant** is an AI assistant operated by an organization for its own workforce, whose defining job is answering employees' questions with answers composed from the organization's own knowledge — the applications it uses and the content it has authored — rather than returning a list of documents or a human's reply.

The defining core is small:

```text
Organization-operated, workforce-facing assistant
└── The organization's own knowledge as the grounding corpus
    └── Natural-language question from an employee
        └── Composed grounded answer (commonly with source references)
```

Everything that makes modern products trustworthy and useful — permission-scoped retrieval, citations, verification states, knowledge-gap detection, multi-surface delivery, admin governance — is standard equipment in mature products, not part of the definition. A minimally configured deployment (a team's knowledge base with an ask surface and permission filtering) is still recognizably this Type.

When the center of gravity shifts to general work assistance — drafting, summarizing, analysis, and actions in systems, with answering as one capability among many — the product is drifting toward a different Application Type (Enterprise AI Assistant). When the deliverable becomes a results list over the estate, it is Enterprise Search territory.
leaves.overview_zh:
**Enterprise Knowledge Assistant** 是一个由组织为其员工运营的 AI 助手，其核心工作是利用组织自身的知识——其使用的应用程序和创作的内容——来回答员工的问题，而不是返回文档列表或人工回复。

核心定义很小：

```text
组织运营、面向员工的助手
└── 组织自身的知识作为基础语料库
    └── 员工用自然语言提问
        └── 组织生成的有依据的回答（通常带有来源参考）
```

使现代产品值得信赖和有用的一切——权限范围检索、引用、验证状态、知识缺口检测、多渠道交付、管理治理——在成熟产品中是标准配置，不是定义的一部分。最小化配置的部署（一个团队的知识库，带有询问界面和权限过滤）仍然可以识别为此类型。

当重心转向一般工作辅助——起草、总结、分析以及系统中的操作，回答只是众多能力之一时——产品正在向不同的应用类型（Enterprise AI Assistant）漂移。当交付物成为整个领域的结果列表时，它就是 Enterprise Search 的领域。
leaves.dc:
Three structures, held together. Remove any one and the product stops being this Type:

- **Organization-operated, workforce-facing assistant.** The organization buys, provisions, and governs the assistant; the served population is its own employees acting in their work context. Without this, the product is consumer AI chat or a customer-facing bot.
- **The organization's own knowledge as the grounding corpus.** What the organization knows — its connected application estate (documents, messages, tickets, wikis) and/or its own authored and curated content — is assembled into one answerable body. The corpus defines what is answerable. Without this, the product is a general assistant with no enterprise grounding.
- **The composed grounded answer as the deliverable.** An employee asks in natural language; the system composes a direct answer from retrieved organization knowledge — not a results list, not a human reply. Without this, the product is enterprise search.
leaves.dc_zh: 三个结构紧密结合：1. 由组织采购、部署并管理的助手，面向自身员工在工作场景中的使用；2. 以组织自有知识库（包括关联的应用程序、文档、消息、工单、维基及自主整理的内容）作为基础语料库，定义可回答范围；3. 以从组织知识中检索并合成的直接答案为交付物，而非结果列表或人工回复。
leaves.rules:
### Permission scoping is the trust substrate

The assistant answers only from content the asking employee may access, mirroring the organization's own access rules. This makes the employee's permissions both a relevance filter and an access-control surface — and it means two employees can receive different answers to the same question, correctly.

### Citations are the verification mechanism

Answers are attributed to sources so employees can verify before acting. Organizations commonly restrict or flag ungrounded (model-knowledge-only) responses precisely because they cannot be checked this way.

### The corpus decays; the product fights the decay

Knowledge goes stale, duplicates, and contradicts itself. Mature products treat this as a first-class problem: verification states with owners and review cadence, staleness flagging, deprecation, and gap detection that turns unanswered questions into content work. An assistant over an unmaintained corpus produces confidently wrong answers — the failure mode these mechanisms exist to prevent.

### The assistant supports, not replaces, judgment

Products in this Type typically frame themselves as support for human decisions, with high-stakes operations (hiring, termination, compliance determinations) explicitly out of scope and governance machinery (guardrails, audit, policies) around everything else.

### Out-of-corpus behavior is a policy decision

What the assistant does when the organization's knowledge cannot answer — refuse, flag uncertainty, or fall back to web/model knowledge — is configured by the organization, not fixed by the Type.
leaves.rules_zh:
### 权限范围是信任基质

助手仅从提问员工可能访问的内容中回答，镜像组织自身的访问规则。这使得员工的权限既是相关性过滤器，又是访问控制界面——并且这意味着两个员工对同一问题可以得到不同的正确回答。

### 引用是验证机制

回答归属于来源，以便员工可以在行动前验证。组织通常限制或标记未扎根（仅模型知识）的响应，正是因为无法以这种方式检查。

### 语料库会衰减；产品与之对抗

知识会过时、重复并自相矛盾。成熟产品将其视为一级问题：具有所有者和审查节奏的验证状态、过时标记、弃用以及将未回答的问题转化为内容工作的缺口检测。基于未维护语料库的助手会产生自信但错误的答案——这些机制存在的目的就是防止这种失败模式。

### 助手支持而不是替代判断

此类型的产品通常将自己定位为人类决策的支持工具，高风险操作（招聘、解雇、合规性判定）明确不在范围内，并且围绕其他所有内容都有治理机制（护栏、审计、策略）。

### 超出语料库的行为是策略决策

当组织知识无法回答时助手做什么——拒绝、标记不确定性或回退到网络/模型知识——由组织配置，而不是由类型固定。

leaves.name: Enterprise Records Management
leaves.overview:
An **Enterprise Records Management** application governs the organization's records: content held as evidence of business activity, protected from change and deletion under organization-defined retention rules, and ultimately disposed of — destroyed or transferred — through an authorized, evidenced process.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Record (content under record governance)
└── Retention schedule / file plan (organization-defined rules)
    └── Governed disposition (authorized, reviewable, evidenced)
```

Three properties. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as records management:

- **Records as the managed object** — once content is under record governance, its change and deletion are controlled by the governing rules rather than by ordinary user discretion. How an item becomes a record varies (declared at creation, declared later, applied automatically); the record state itself is what matters.
- **Organization-defined retention schedule (file plan)** — rules that assign classes of records to retention periods and disposition actions, anchored in the organization's legal, regulatory, and business requirements. The schedule, not the folder structure, is the governance instrument.
- **Governed, evidenced disposition** — at the end of retention, destruction or transfer is executed as an authorized, reviewable process with recorded proof. Silent deletion is precisely what records management exists to prevent.

Notably, the defining core does **not** include owning the repository. In the current market this Type appears in three packaging postures: a governance layer over an existing collaboration estate, a records-centric system of record, and a records component inside a broader content-management suite. It also does not require electronic-only content — physical records can be governed by the same machinery.

When the center of gravity shifts to the working content lifecycle (capture, collaboration, versioning, publishing) in a general repository, the product is drifting toward Enterprise Content Management. When retention rules exist without the record state (retain/delete policies only), it is data lifecycle governance, not records management.
leaves.overview_zh:
