leaves.rules:
### The run is permission-gated before money moves

Executing a run triggers real money movement (employee payments plus remittance of withheld taxes). Products therefore gate it: only permitted roles can run or approve payroll, and the final step is an explicit confirmation that shows the breakdown and the debit it will cause. Separating preparation from approval is a common control in larger organizations.

### Withholding happens at run time

Statutory amounts are computed and captured with each run — not reconciled later. This is what makes the subsequent remittance and filing loop reliable, and it is why a skipped or late run creates compliance consequences, not just late pay.

### Pay records are durable and legally significant

Registers, pay statements, and year-to-date history persist and accumulate. Year-end forms are derived from them; audits and disputes are answered from them. Corrections are recorded as corrections (off-cycle runs, retro adjustments, amended forms), not as rewrites.

### The employee pay record drives the computation

Changes to pay terms, elections, or work location take effect through the record and apply to subsequent runs. Work location in particular determines which jurisdiction's rules apply to each employee — a structural rule in products that handle multi-jurisdiction workforces.

### Payment timing depends on the rail

Direct deposit requires lead time between run confirmation and payday; checks and other rails differ. Products expose this as scheduling constraints (submission deadlines for a given pay date) rather than as instant settlement.

### The cycle is strict, exceptions are explicit

The regular cycle is scheduled and repeating; anything outside it — bonuses, missed payments, terminations, corrections — goes through explicit off-cycle paths so that the regular run's integrity and the compliance loop are preserved.
leaves.rules_zh:
### 运行在资金移动前受权限控制

执行运行会触发真实资金移动（员工支付加上预扣税款汇缴）。因此，产品对其进行控制：只有被允许的角色才能运行或批准薪资，最后一步是显示明细及其将导致的扣款的显式确认。在较大组织中，将准备与批准分开是常见控制。

### 预扣发生在运行时

法定金额在每次运行时计算和捕获——而不是在之后协调。这使得后续的汇缴和申报循环可靠，这就是为什么跳过或延迟运行会产生合规后果，而不仅仅是延迟支付。

### 薪资记录持久且具有法律意义

登记、薪资声明和年初至今历史持续存在并累积。年终表格从中派生；审计和争议从中解答。更正被记录为更正（非周期运行、追溯调整、修订表格），而不是重写。

### 员工薪资记录驱动计算

薪资条款、选择或工作地点的变更通过记录生效并应用于后续运行。工作地点尤其决定了每个员工适用哪个管辖区域的规则——在处理多管辖区域劳动力的产品中的结构性规则。

### 支付时间取决于通道

直接存款需要在运行确认和支付日之间留出时间；支票和其他通道不同。产品将其显示为调度约束（给定支付日的提交截止日期），而不是即时结算。

### 周期严格，例外显式

常规周期是计划和重复的；其外的任何内容——奖金、错过支付、终止、更正——都通过显式

leaves.name: PCB Design
leaves.overview:
A **PCB Design application** is an engineering design application for printed circuit boards: the designer places components onto a layered board substrate and draws copper — tracks, vias, and zones — that realizes the circuit's electrical connections, verifies the result against manufacturing constraints, and produces the fabrication data a board manufacturer needs to build the board.

The defining core is small:

```text
Board (outline + layer stackup) — the design of record
└── Footprints (components as physical pads) placed on the board
    └── Nets (the electrical connectivity model binding pads together)
        └── Copper geometry (tracks / vias / zones realizing the nets)
            └── Fabrication outputs (artwork, drill, assembly data)
```

Everything else commonly associated with these tools — schematic capture, design-rule checking, 3D visualization, simulation, signal-integrity analysis, cloud collaboration, supply-chain data — is standard capability or variant, not the definition. Notably, the schematic is not part of the defining core: several products support laying out a board directly, without a schematic, and the connectivity model can be defined in the board editor itself. What the Type cannot exist without is the board, the footprints on it, the nets that govern its copper, and the manufacturing data that ends the work.
leaves.overview_zh:
一个**PCB设计应用程序**是用于印刷电路板的工程设计应用程序：设计者将元件放置在分层的板基板上，并绘制铜——走线、过孔和覆铜区域——以实现电路的电气连接，根据制造约束验证结果，并生成板制造商制造电路板所需的制造数据。

其定义性核心很简单：

```text
电路板（轮廓 + 层叠结构）— 设计记录本
└── 封装（作为物理焊盘的元件）放置在电路板上
    └── 网表（将焊盘绑定在一起的电气连接模型）
        └── 铜几何图形（实现网表的走线/过孔/覆铜区域）
            └── 制造输出（光绘文件、钻孔数据、装配数据）
```

通常与这些工具相关的其他一切——原理图绘制、设计规则检查、3D可视化、仿真、信号完整性分析、云协作、供应链数据——都是标准功能或变体，并非定义核心。值得注意的是，原理图并非定义核心的一部分：一些产品支持直接进行电路板布局，无需原理图，连接模型可以在电路板编辑器本身中定义。此类型无法缺少的是电路板、其上的封装、控制其铜层的网表，以及结束工作的制造数据。
leaves.dc:
**Footprints.** Components enter the board as footprints: the physical counterpart of a schematic symbol, carrying the pads (copper lands, with or without drilled holes) at which the component connects to the board. Footprints are placed, oriented, and flipped between the board's sides. Designs are composed from catalogued footprints held in libraries; mature products ship large libraries and provide dedicated footprint editors, and a placed footprint is typically embedded as a copy in the board so the design stays independent of library changes.

**Nets.** The application maintains an electrical connectivity model: nets that bind specific pads together as "must be connected". This model is what makes the copper electrical rather than decorative. Nets enter the board from an upstream schematic in integrated suites, from an imported netlist, or — in board-only workflows — are defined directly in the board editor. Wherever it comes from, the connectivity model drives the most characteristic display of the Type: the ratsnest (also called connection lines or ratlines), which draws every not-yet-routed connection as a direct line between the pads it must join, and disappears connection by connection as the board is routed.

**Copper geometry.** The designer realizes the nets by drawing copper: tracks (routes) that carry a signal between pads, vias that jump between copper layers, and zones (copper pours) that fill areas of a layer with a net — commonly ground or power. Routing is governed by the design rules (see below); zones fill automatically around obstacles while keeping clearance and connecting to same-net pads, often through thermal-relief spokes. The copper geometry is the physical realization of the connectivity model, and the gap between them — connections not yet routed — is exactly what the ratsnest shows.

**Fabrication outputs.** The design terminates in manufacturing data: layer-by-layer artwork (today overwhelmingly Gerber format), drill data for holes, pick-and-place files listing each component's position and orientation for assembly machines, and a bill of materials. These outputs are generated from the design, never drawn by hand, and they are the deliverable the board manufacturer consumes. Many products also generate fabrication/assembly drawings and can exchange richer manufacturing-data formats.
leaves.dc_zh:
**元件封装。** 元件通过封装进入板中：封装是原理图符号的物理对应物，承载着元件与板相连的焊盘（铜区域，可带有或不带有钻孔）。封装被放置、定向，并在板的两侧之间翻转。设计由目录化封装构成，这些封装保存在库中；成熟产品会附带大型封装库，并提供专用封装编辑器，而一个已放置的封装通常作为副本嵌入板中，以使设计独立于库的更改。

**网络连接。** 应用维护一个电气连接模型：网络将特定的焊盘绑定在一起，表示“必须连接”。这个模型使得铜层具有电气功能，而非仅仅是装饰。网络在集成套件中从上游原理图进入板中，或从导入的网表获取；在仅限板的工作流程中，则直接在板编辑器中定义。无论来源如何，这个连接模型驱动着该类型最具特征的显示：飞线（也称为连接线或鼠线），它将每个尚未布线的连接绘制为它必须连接的两个焊盘之间的直线，并随着板子的布线而逐步消失。

**铜层几何结构。** 设计师通过绘制铜层来实现网络：用于在焊盘之间承载信号的导线（布线），用于在不同铜层之间跳转的过孔，以及
leaves.rules:
- **Connectivity is semantic, not visual.** Copper only "counts" where the nets say so: two pads are connected when a continuous copper path of the same net joins them, and the ratsnest keeps showing any connection that is not yet realized. The checker's unconnected-items report is the authoritative statement of what remains to be routed.
- **Schematic and board must not drift apart.** Whether synchronization is a designer-triggered update or a shared data model, a mismatch between the logical circuit and the physical board is a defect — mature products check for it explicitly.
- **Design rules gate the release.** Fabrication outputs are meant to be generated from a checked design; unresolved violations are meant to block or at least flag the handoff. Rule severity is configurable, and justified exclusions are a normal part of the workflow — but they are recorded decisions, not silence.
- **Deliverables are derived, never hand-drawn.** Editing a Gerber file or a BOM by hand does not change the design; the design of record is the board (and its schematic), and the manufacturing data is regenerated from it.
- **Zone fills are computed state.** A zone's copper is recalculated from the outline, the rules, and the objects it interacts with; products treat stale fills as an error condition before checking or output, because the fill is what actually gets manufactured.
- **The library is the quality backbone.** Pad geometry, courtyard outlines, and 3D models come from footprints; a wrong footprint produces a board that cannot be assembled. Mature deployments treat library maintenance as a governed discipline, and boards embed library copies so they do not change unexpectedly.
- **The board outline is load-bearing.** Zones fill only inside it, 3D and several checks depend on it being a valid closed shape, and mechanical fit is judged against it — a malformed outline is itself a checkable violation.
leaves.rules_zh:
- **连接性是语义性的，而非视觉性的。** 铜层仅在网表指示的地方才“算数”：两个焊盘在相同的网表通过连续铜路径连接时才算连接，而飞线会持续显示任何尚未实现的连接。检查器的未连接项目报告是剩余待布线内容的权威声明。
- **原理图与电路板不得出现偏差。** 无论是由设计者触发的更新还是共享数据模型，逻辑电路与物理电路板之间的不匹配都是缺陷——成熟产品会明确检查这一点。
- **设计规则控制发布。** 制造输出应从经过检查的设计中生成；未解决的违规旨在阻止或至少标记移交。规则严重性可配置，合理的排除是工作流程的正常部分——但它们是已记录的决策，而非默许。
- **交付物是派生的，绝非手工绘制。** 手动编辑Gerber文件或BOM不会改变设计；设计记录本是电路板（及其原理图），制造数据从中重新生成。
- **区域填充是计算状态。** 区域的铜层根据轮廓、规则及其交互对象重新计算；产品在检查或输出之前将过时的填充视为错误条件，因为填充是实际被制造的内容。
- **库是质量的支柱。** 焊盘几何图形、Courtyard轮廓和3D模型来自封装；错误的封装会产生无法组装的电路板。成熟的部署将库维护视为受控的学科，电路板嵌入库副本以防意外更改。
- **电路板轮廓是承重的。** 区域仅在其内部填充，3D和一些检查依赖于它

leaves.name: PDF / Document Reader
leaves.overview:
A **PDF / Document Reader** is an application for reading document files produced elsewhere: it opens a whole document — regardless of subject matter or origin — renders its pages faithfully in the layout the file defines, and lets the reader move through the document and interact with its content without changing what the document *is*.

The defining core is small:

```text
Document file from an external source
└── Faithful fixed-layout page rendering
    └── Movement through the paginated document
        (paging, jumping, scale adjustment)
```

Everything else commonly associated with PDF applications — annotation, form filling, digital signatures, text search, page reorganization, enterprise security tooling, AI assistance — is widespread in current products but is not what makes the product a document reader. The Type's historical root is the plain read-only viewer, and a viewer with none of the modern machinery remains fully inside the Type.

When the center of gravity shifts — re-laying-out content for reading comfort, authoring or editing the document's content, curating a collection of books or papers — the product has drifted toward a different Application Type (E-book Reader, Document Editor, E-book Library, Academic Paper Reader).
leaves.overview_zh:
一款 **PDF / 文档阅读器** 是用于阅读在其他地方生成的文档文件的应用程序：它打开整个文档——无论主题或来源如何——按照文件定义的布局忠实地渲染其页面，并允许读者在文档中移动并与内容交互，而不改变文档*本身*的性质。

其定义性核心很小：

```text
来自外部源的文档文件
└── 忠实的固定布局页面渲染
     └── 在分页文档中的移动
         （翻页、跳转、缩放调整）
```

通常与 PDF 应用程序相关联的其他一切——注释、表单填写、数字签名、文本搜索、页面重组、企业安全工具、AI 辅助——在当前产品中很普遍，但这并不是使该产品成为文档阅读器的原因。该类型的历史根源是纯只读查看器，一个没有现代机制的查看器仍然完全属于该类型。

当重心转移——为阅读舒适度重新布局内容、创作或编辑文档内容、整理书籍或论文集合——该产品已偏离到不同的应用程序类型（电子书阅读器、文档编辑器、电子书库、学术论文阅读器）。
leaves.dc:
```text
Document file from an external source
└── Faithful fixed-layout page rendering
    └── Movement through the paginated document
        (paging, jumping, scale adjustment)
```

Three properties. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as a document reader:

- **The externally-obtained document as the unit of reading.** The application opens whole document files of arbitrary provenance and content — invoices, manuals, papers, forms, brochures. It holds no authoring relationship to the content and no collection semantics of its own. Without this, the product is an authoring tool or a content service, not a reader.
- **Faithful fixed-layout page rendering.** Pages are presented as fixed compositions — text, images, and graphics placed at exact positions, with pagination determined by the file itself. The same file looks the same everywhere; the application's obligation is fidelity to the file as authored, not re-presentation for comfort. Without this, the product re-lays-out content (e-book reader) or changes content (editor).
- **Movement through the paginated document.** Because the layout is fixed and does not adapt to the window, reading requires machinery to move: scrolling and paging between pages, jumping to a page or position, and adjusting viewing scale (zoom, fit-to-window/page/width). Without this, the product is a static page image.
leaves.dc_zh:
来自外部源的文档文件
└── 忠实的固定布局页面渲染
    └── 在分页文档中移动
        (翻页、跳转、缩放调整)
leaves.rules:
### Fidelity is the obligation

The reader renders what the file says. It does not re-flow text to fit the window, does not re-typeface for comfort, does not "improve" the layout. Everything that changes presentation rather than scale belongs to other Types. This is the structural contrast with e-book reading, where the presentation is the app's to optimize.

### The text layer is not guaranteed

A PDF's pages may be true text or may be scanned images. When there is no text layer, search, selection, and copy do not work — a failure mode documented in mainstream products' own troubleshooting guides. Text recognition features in some products exist precisely to bridge this gap; the base behavior is: **no text layer, no text interaction**.

### Documents carry permissions; readers enforce them

An author can protect a document: a password to open it, and restrictions on printing or copying content. The reader enforces these — it can refuse to print a restricted document or require a password before text can be copied. The reader never grants rights the file does not carry.

### Markup and form data are changes to a copy

Annotation and form input modify the opened document (or a copy of it). Persistence mechanics differ — some products write back into the file, some require an explicit save-as-copy step — but in all cases unsaved work is transient. A filled form that is not saved is lost.

### The outline is the document's, not the app's

A table of contents exists only if the authoring tool put one in the file. Most documents carry none; the reader must remain fully usable through thumbnails, page numbers, and search alone.

### The file is live

The reader views a file that other programs may change while it is open; products commonly reload the document when the file changes underneath. The reader is a window onto the file, not a container that owns it.

### Reading is not editing

The line the market itself maintains: readers present, mark up, fill, and sign; they do not rewrite the document's content. Products that do both split the capability into a separate editor product or explicitly disclaim editing. Page-level organization (combining, reordering, deleting pages) is the gray zone — offered by some readers as a convenience, owned by editors as a job — and is treated here as optional, never defining.
leaves.rules_zh:
### 保真度是义务

阅读器渲染文件所说的内容。它不重新流动文本以适应窗口，不为舒适度重新排版，不“改进”布局。所有改变呈现而非比例的内容属于其他类型。这与电子书阅读形成结构性对比，在电子书阅读中，呈现是应用程序要优化的。

### 文本层不是保证的

PDF 的页面可能是真正的文本，也可能是扫描图像。当没有文本层时，搜索、选择和复制不起作用——这是主流产品自己的故障排除指南中记录的故障模式。某些产品中的文本识别功能正是为了弥合这一差距；基本行为是：**没有文本层，就没有文本交互**。

### 文档携带权限；阅读器执行它们

作者可以保护文档：打开它的密码，以及对打印或复制内容的限制。阅读器执行这些——它可以拒绝打印受限制的文档，或在复制文本前要求密码。阅读器从不授予文件不携带的权利。

### 标记和表单数据是对副本的更改

注释和表单输入修改打开的文档（或其副本）。持久化机制不同——一些产品写回文件，一些需要显式的另存为副本步骤——但在所有情况下，未保存的工作是暂时的。未保存的已填写表单会丢失。

### 大纲属于文档，不属于应用程序

只有当创作工具在文件中放入目录时，目录才存在。大多数文档没有；阅读器必须仅通过缩略图、页码和搜索保持完全可用。

### 文件是活动的

阅读器查看的文件可能在打开时被其他程序更改；产品通常在文件更改时重新加载文档

leaves.name: Peer Review Platform
leaves.overview:
A **Peer Review Platform** is the organized evaluation exchange: it collects submissions — papers, abstracts, proposals, applications — as identified records, pairs each submission with eligible reviewers drawn from a managed pool, captures each reviewer's evaluation as a structured record, and resolves the reviews into a recorded per-submission outcome (a decision, a ranking, or a certified review report) that the organizing body — a conference, journal, funding agency, or association — acts on.

It solves a coordination problem that email and spreadsheets cannot: an organizing body must simultaneously move dozens to thousands of submissions through evaluation while coordinating participants — reviewers, authors, program committee members — who are mostly external, part-time, and unknown to each other. The platform is the shared place where every submission's evaluation state lives, where reviewer–submission pairing is made under conflict-of-interest rules, and where reviews, discussions, and decisions accumulate as a record.

The boundary of the Type: it is the review exchange itself — not the event a conference review feeds (that is conference management territory), not the journal a review feeds (that is the journal's editorial system), and not a community commentary board where anyone reviews anything.
leaves.overview_zh:
**同行评审平台** 是一个有组织的评估交换系统：它收集投稿——论文、摘要、提案、申请——作为已识别记录，将每篇投稿与来自管理池的合格审稿人配对，将每位审稿人的评估捕获为结构化记录，并将评审解析为记录在案的每篇投稿结果（决定、排名或经认证的评审报告），供组织机构——会议、期刊、资助机构或协会——执行。

它解决了一个电子邮件和电子表格无法解决的协调问题：组织机构必须同时将数十到数千篇投稿推进评估，同时协调参与者——审稿人、作者、项目委员会成员——他们大多是外部的、兼职的，且彼此不认识。该平台是共享场所，每篇投稿的评估状态在此存在，审稿人–投稿配对在利益冲突规则下进行，评审、讨论和决策作为记录积累。

该类型的边界：它就是评审交换本身——不是会议评审所馈入的事件（那是会议管理的领域），不是评审所馈入的期刊（那是期刊的编辑系统），也不是任何人都能评审任何东西的社区评论板。
leaves.dc:
Four properties. Remove any one and the software is no longer a peer review platform:

- **The reviewable submission as the unit of record.** A work enters the platform as a persistent, individually identified record — manuscript or abstract files, metadata, contributor list — created for the purpose of being evaluated. Every later action (assignment, review, discussion, decision) attaches to this record. Without it there is nothing to review.
- **Platform-mediated reviewer–submission pairing.** The platform connects each submission to one or more eligible reviewers from a managed pool. Pairing may be done by direct assignment, by collecting reviewer preferences (bidding) and assigning accordingly, or by computing matches from expertise profiles — but it is always the platform's act, performed under the process's conflict-of-interest rules, not self-selection by reviewers. Without mediated pairing the surface becomes an open commentary board.
- **The review as a first-class record.** Each reviewer's evaluation is captured as a structured record bound to the specific submission–reviewer pair: a written assessment, ratings or scores against defined criteria, and a recommendation. The review has its own lifecycle (draft, submitted, confirmed) and a visibility policy — who may see which reviews at which point. Without it, assignment is just a tracker and evaluation is just a survey.
- **The evaluation outcome loop.** Reviews are aggregated and considered by the operating roles and resolved into a recorded per-submission outcome — accept/reject/revise decisions, a ranking or score summary, or a certified review report — communicated to the submitters and used by the organizing body for its next action (admit to a program, fund, award, publish elsewhere). Without it, reviews accumulate but no process completes.
leaves.dc_zh:
- **可评审的投稿作为记录单元。** 一份作品作为持久的、独立标识的记录进入平台——稿件或摘要文件、元数据、贡献者列表——为评估目的而创建。后续的每个操作（分配、评审、讨论、决定）都附加到这个记录上。没有它，就没有什么可评审的。

- **平台介导的评审者–投稿配对。** 平台将每个投稿与管理池中的一位或多位合格评审者连接起来。配对可以通过直接分配、收集评审者偏好（竞标）并相应分配，或从专业档案中计算匹配来进行——但它始终是平台的行为，在过程的冲突利益规则下执行，而不是评审者的自我选择。没有介导配对，平台就变成了一个开放评论板。

- **评审作为一等记录。** 每位评审者的评估被捕获为绑定到特定投稿–评审者对的结构化记录：书面评估、根据预定标准的评分或分数，以及推荐。评审有其自己的生命周期（草稿、提交、确认）和可见性策略——谁在哪个阶段可以看到哪些评审。没有它，分配只是一个跟踪器，评估只是一个调查。
leaves.rules:
- **Pairing is governed by conflicts.** Conflict-of-interest rules are structural: reviewers declare conflicts (and expertise), the system computes or enforces them, and a review can be invalidated or hidden when a conflict emerges after the fact.
- **Reviews have a visibility policy.** Who sees which review when is a configured property of the process — hidden from authors until decisions, released to authors and reviewers during the process, or published openly. The default posture in most sampled products is confidentiality until decision.
- **The review record is attributed and durable.** Reviews bind to the specific reviewer and submission, persist through the process, and remain part of the submission's evaluation history; operators can typically undo or reset aggregation decisions but the review trail remains.
- **Deadlines are enforced states.** Submission and review windows open and close on configured dates; late reviews require operator intervention; enforceable cutoffs prevent post-deadline evaluation.
- **Authority is tiered.** Reviewers recommend; meta-reviewers, judges, or chairs finalize. The system enforces who may record which outcome, and intermediate layers can override reviewer recommendations.
- **Outcomes are recorded state changes.** A decision changes the submission's state, triggers templated correspondence, and is typically irreversible except through explicit operator action (revert, reopen).
- **Submitters see status, not (by default) the deliberation.** Author portals expose submission state and outcome; the internal review record is exposed only as the visibility policy allows.
leaves.rules_zh:
- **配对由冲突控制。** 利益冲突规则是结构性的：审稿人声明冲突（和专业领域），系统计算或强制执行它们，当冲突事后出现时，评审可能被作废或隐藏。
- **评审具有可见性策略。** 谁在何时看到哪篇评审是流程的配置属性——对作者隐藏直到决定、在流程中向作者和审稿人发布，或公开发布。大多数采样产品中的默认姿态是保密直到决定。
- **评审记录是归因的且持久的。** 评审绑定到特定审稿人和投稿，在流程中持续存在，并作为投稿评估历史的一部分；操作员通常可以撤销或重置汇总决策，但评审轨迹保留。
- **截止日期是强制状态。** 投稿和评审窗口在配置日期开放和关闭；延迟评审需要操作员干预；可强制执行的截止防止截止日期后的评估。
- **权限是分层的。** 审稿人推荐；元审稿人、评委或主席最终确定。系统强制执行谁可以记录哪种结果，中间层可以覆盖审稿人推荐。
- **结果是记录的状态变更。** 决定改变投稿状态，触发模板化通信，通常不可逆，除非通过明确操作员操作（恢复、重新打开）。
- **投稿者看到状态，而不是（默认）审议过程。** 作者门户暴露投稿状态和结果；内部评审记录仅在可见性策略允许时暴露。

leaves.name: Peer-to-peer Fundraising Platform
leaves.overview:
A **Peer-to-peer Fundraising Platform** enables a nonprofit organization to mobilize its supporters as fundraisers: supporters create and own their own fundraising pages inside a context the organization provides — a campaign, an event, or a year-round invitation — solicit their personal networks through those pages, and every gift made through a supporter's page is credited to that supporter while the money settles to the organization.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Organization's fundraising context (campaign / event / standing invitation)
└── Supporter-held fundraising page (own story, own goal, org's branding)
    └── Donor gives through the page
        └── Gift credited to the fundraiser (and team), rolled up to the totals
            └── Money settles to the organization — never to the supporter
```

Everything commonly associated with modern peer-to-peer fundraising — team hierarchies, leaderboards, thermometers, badges, coaching email journeys, registration flows, fitness tracking — is widespread in current products but is not what makes the product a peer-to-peer fundraising platform. The walk-a-thon pledge sheet, where a supporter collects pledges from friends and turns the money in to the charity, already contains the whole defining structure.

When the organization itself runs the fundraising page and asks its own donors, the product is a different Application Type (Nonprofit Crowdfunding Platform or Online Donation Platform). When the supporter keeps the money, it is personal crowdfunding, not this.
leaves.overview_zh:
一个**点对点筹款平台**使非营利组织能够动员其支持者成为筹款人：支持者在组织提供的背景内——活动、事件或全年邀请——创建并拥有自己的筹款页面，通过这些页面向其个人人脉网络募捐，通过支持者页面进行的每一笔捐赠都将记入该支持者名下，同时资金最终汇入组织账户。

其核心结构如下：

```text
组织的筹款背景（活动 / 事件 / 常年邀请）
└── 支持者持有的筹款页面（个人故事、个人目标、组织品牌）
    └── 捐赠者通过该页面捐款
        └── 捐赠记入筹款人（及团队）名下，并汇总至总金额
            └── 资金结算至组织——绝不会至支持者
```

所有通常与现代点对点筹款相关的元素——团队层级、排行榜、温度计、徽章、指导邮件流程、注册流程、健身追踪——在当前产品中普遍存在，但并非使该产品成为点对点筹款平台的关键。步行筹款活动的认捐表，即支持者从朋友处收集认捐并转交给慈善机构，已经包含了整个核心结构。

当组织自身运营筹款页面并直接向其捐赠者募捐时，该产品属于不同的**应用类型**（非营利众筹平台或在线捐赠平台）。当支持者保留资金时，则属于个人众筹，而非此类型。
leaves.dc:
Three structures. If any one is removed, the product stops being a peer-to-peer fundraising platform:

- **The supporter-held fundraising page.** A persistent, individually identified page created and owned by a supporter — an individual or a team — carrying the supporter's own story, goal, photos, and updates. The page is built from a template the organization prepared, so it inherits the organization's branding and donation experience while the supporter supplies the words and the personal material. Without supporter ownership, the page is an organization-run campaign page (crowdfunding territory); without the organization's context and branding, it is a personal crowdfunding page.

- **The attribution-and-roll-up gift flow.** Donors give through a supporter's page. Each gift is recorded against that page — crediting the fundraiser, and the team, who brought the donor in — and rolls up in real time into the team, campaign, and organization totals. The money always settles to the organization's account; the supporter never holds or touches the funds. The attribution record ("who introduced whom") is what lets the organization thank both the donor and the fundraiser and steward the new relationship. Without attribution, the page is just a donation form with a name on it; without settlement to the organization, it is personal crowdfunding.

- **The delegated solicitation role.** The ask is made by the supporter to their own personal network. The platform hands the solicitation job to the supporter and equips it: a personal page link, one-tap sharing across email, SMS, and social channels with the supporter's own message, visibility of the page's donors, and thank-you and update tools. Without this, the organization is simply soliciting its own donors — the dynamic that distinguishes the sibling Types.
leaves.dc_zh:
三个结构。如果任何一个被移除，产品就不再是点对点筹款平台：

- **支持者持有的筹款页面。** 一个持久的、单独标识的页面，由支持者（个人或团队）创建和拥有，包含支持者自己的故事、目标、照片和更新。页面基于组织准备的模板构建，因此继承了组织的品牌和捐赠体验，而支持者提供文字和个人材料。如果缺少支持者所有权，页面就是组织运营的活动页面（众筹领域）；如果缺少组织的上下文和品牌，它就是个人众筹页面。

- **归因和汇总的捐赠流程。** 捐赠者通过支持者的页面进行捐赠。每笔捐赠都记录在该页面上——记录筹款人和团队引入的捐赠者——并实时汇总到团队、活动和组织的总额中。资金总是结算到组织的账户；支持者从不持有或接触资金。归因记录（“谁介绍了谁”）让组织能够感谢捐赠者和筹款人，并管理新关系。如果没有归因，页面只是一个带有名字的捐赠表单；如果没有结算到组织，它就是个人众筹。

- **委托的募捐角色。**
leaves.rules:
### Money always goes to the organization

No matter which page a donor gives through, the funds settle to the organization's account. The supporter is a solicitor and a credit recipient, never a money holder. This is the structural line against personal crowdfunding.

### Every gift carries its fundraiser

Gifts made through a supporter's page are attributed to that supporter (and team) — visible in leaderboards and totals, and commonly written to the donor record as a soft credit. The organization can therefore answer "who introduced whom" — and thank both.

### Totals move together

Personal, team, and campaign totals are computed from the same gift records and update together in real time; there is no reconciliation layer between the supporter's page total and the organization's total.

### Branding is inherited, content is personal

Supporter pages are created from organization-prepared templates: the supporter supplies story, photos, and goal; the design, donation experience, and money handling stay the organization's. Some products let the organization review pages before they go public; others leave them self-serve.

### The supporter's reach drives acquisition

Donors reached through supporter pages are typically new to the organization — reached through personal relationships rather than the org's own channels. This is why the Type is marketed as network expansion, and why the donor record with its fundraiser attribution is treated as the durable asset.

### Offline participation counts

Gifts collected in person by fundraisers (cash, checks) are logged into the same totals and roll-ups, so the public picture reflects everything raised.
leaves.rules_zh:
### 资金始终流向组织

无论捐赠者通过哪个页面捐款，资金都结算至组织账户。支持者是募捐者和记名接收者，但绝不是资金持有者。这是与个人众筹的结构性界限。

### 每笔捐赠都记录其筹款人

通过支持者页面进行的捐赠归属于该支持者（及团队）——在排行榜和总金额中可见，通常也作为软信用写入捐赠者记录。因此，组织可以回答“谁介绍了谁”——并感谢双方。

### 总金额同步变动

个人、团队和活动总金额基于相同的捐赠记录计算并实时同步更新；支持者的页面总金额与组织总金额之间没有核对层。

### 品牌继承，内容个性化

支持者页面基于组织准备的模板创建：支持者提供故事、照片和目标；设计、捐赠体验和资金处理机制属于组织。一些产品允许组织在页面公开前进行审核；另一些则让其自助操作。

### 支持者的影响力驱动捐赠者获取

通过支持者页面触达的捐赠者通常对该组织是新的——通过个人关系而非组织自身渠道触达。这就是为什么该类型被宣传为网络扩张，以及为什么带有筹款人归属信息的捐赠者记录被视为持久资产。

### 线下参与同样有效

筹款人亲自收集的捐赠（现金、支票）计入相同的总金额和汇总数据，因此公开的募捐全景反映了所有筹集的资金。

leaves.name: Peer-to-peer Payment Application
leaves.overview:
A **Peer-to-peer Payment Application** is an application through which individuals send money directly to other individuals. Each party holds a personal account tied to an identified person; the sender addresses the recipient through a personal identifier, names an amount, and the application executes a recorded transfer from money the sender controls to money the recipient can access, tracking it to a completion state and keeping it in a persistent history.

The defining core is small:

```text
Personal account (identified individual)
└── Addressable recipient (another identified individual)
    └── Transfer (amount + direction + funding)
        └── Recorded transfer with a completion state
            └── Persistent transaction history
```

Everything else commonly associated with the category — money requests and bill splitting, stored balances, social feeds, business profiles, issued cards, direct deposit — is widespread market structure layered on that core, not what makes the product a peer-to-peer payment application. The category's products differ sharply in philosophy (standalone balance apps, bank-network services embedded in banking apps, platform-native wallet payments), and the definition above holds across all of them.
leaves.overview_zh:
一个**点对点支付应用**是个人直接向其他个人发送资金的应用程序。各方持有一个与已识别个人绑定的个人账户；发送方通过个人标识符指定接收方，指定金额，应用程序执行从发送方控制的资金到接收方可访问资金的记录转移，将其跟踪至完成状态，并将其保留在持久历史记录中。

其定义核心很小：

```text
个人账户（已识别个人）
└── 可寻址接收方（另一个已识别个人）
     └── 转移（金额 + 方向 + 资金来源）
         └── 具有完成状态的记录转移
             └── 持久交易历史
```

通常与该类别相关联的其他所有内容——资金请求和账单分摊、存储余额、社交动态、商业资料、发行卡片、直接存款——都是叠加在该核心之上的广泛市场结构，而非使该产品成为点对点支付应用的原因。该类别的产品在理念上存在显著差异（独立余额应用、嵌入银行应用的银行网络服务、平台原生钱包支付），上述定义适用于所有这些产品。
leaves.dc:
Four structures. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as a peer-to-peer payment application:

- **Personal account for an identified individual.** Every participant holds an account bound to a real person. Identity is verified to varying depth — from a confirmed email to full government-ID verification — but the account is personal, not organizational.
- **Addressable recipient.** The sender must be able to designate one specific other person. Addressing runs over personal identifiers: phone number, email address, in-app username or handle, a scannable personal QR code, or contacts synced from the device. The recipient is a person the sender selects, not a public audience.
- **Transfer.** The central object: a directed movement of a stated amount from money the sender controls (a linked bank account, a card, or a balance held inside the application) to money the recipient can access (their balance or their own bank account). A transfer may carry an optional note describing what it was for.
- **Recorded transfer with a completion state.** Every transfer is a durable record that moves through states — at minimum initiated → completed, with pending and failed paths — and remains in both parties' histories. The record is what makes the movement a payment rather than an informal promise.
leaves.dc_zh:
四个结构。若移除其中任何一个，该产品将不再能被识别为点对点支付应用：

- **针对已识别个人的账户。** 每个参与者都持有一个与真实个人绑定的账户。身份验证的深度不一——从已确认的电子邮件到全面的政府ID验证——但该账户是个人的，而非组织的。
- **可寻址的收款方。** 发送方必须能够指定一个具体的另一个人。寻址通过个人标识符进行：电话号码、电子邮件地址、应用内用户名或个人标签、可扫描的个人二维码，或从设备同步的通讯录。收款方是发送方选择的一个具体个人，而非公开受众。
- **转账。** 核心对象：一笔从发送方控制的资金（关联的银行卡、信用卡或应用内余额）向收款方可访问的资金（其余额或其自身银行账户）进行的、金额明确的定向转移。转账可以附带一个可选的备注，说明用途。
- **带有完成状态的转账记录。** 每一笔转账都是一条持久记录，其状态至少经历“已发起 → 已完成”，并可能存在“待处理”和“失败”的路径，并保留在双方的交易历史中。正是这条记录，使得该资金转移成为一次支付，而非一个非正式的承诺。
leaves.rules:
- **Completed transfers are effectively irrevocable.** Across the researched sample, a completed transfer cannot be unilaterally reversed by the sender. Recovery paths are the recipient returning the money or support intervention. This irreversibility shapes everything: confirmation screens re-display the recipient's name, and scam-prevention warnings are prominent.
- **Pending is a real state, not an error.** Transfers can sit pending because the recipient has not yet enrolled or verified their identifier, or because a bank is still processing. Some pending states let the sender take the payment back; others only allow waiting.
- **Verification gates capability.** Holding a balance, raising limits, or using all features typically requires identity verification; unverified recipients can hold payments in pending.
- **Limits exist and are often dynamic.** Per-transaction, daily, or rolling-period limits apply; at least one model determines the applicable limit per transaction based on factors including the recipient.
- **Fees depend on funding method, not on the act of paying a person.** Bank-account and balance funding is commonly free; card funding and accelerated transfers commonly cost more, disclosed at review time.
- **Transaction visibility is a privacy surface.** Where a social layer exists, each payment carries a privacy setting (public / friends / private), with defaults resolving to the more restrictive choice between the two parties. Products without a social layer keep transfers private by construction.
- **Business use is a boundary, not a given.** Some products welcome small-business payments and business profiles; at least one major product explicitly prohibits business use of its person-to-person service. The person-to-person job is the Type's center; commercial acceptance is a governed extension.
leaves.rules_zh:
- **已完成的转移实际上是不可撤销的。** 在研究的样本中，已完成的转移不能由发送方单方面撤销。恢复途径是接收方退回资金或支持介入。这种不可逆性塑造了一切：确认屏幕重新显示接收方姓名，且防诈骗警告很突出。
- **待定是一个真实状态，而非错误。** 转移可能处于待定状态，因为接收方尚未注册或验证其标识符，或因为银行仍在处理。某些待定状态允许发送方取回付款；其他状态仅允许等待。
- **验证限制功能。** 持有余额、提高限额或使用所有功能通常需要身份验证；未验证的接收方可使付款处于待定状态。
- **限额存在且通常是动态的。** 适用每笔交易、每日或滚动周期限额；至少一种模式根据包括接收方在内的因素确定每笔交易的适用限额。
- **费用取决于资金方式，而非向个人付款的行为。** 银行账户和余额资金通常免费；卡片资金和加速转移通常成本更高，在审查时披露。
- **交易可见性是隐私界面。** 在存在社交层的情况下，每笔付款携带隐私设置（公开 / 朋友 / 私密），默认值解析为双方之间更严格的选择。没有社交层的产品在结构上保持转移私密。
- **商业用途是边界，而非既定事实。** 某些产品欢迎小企业付款和商业资料；至少一个主要产品明确禁止其个人对个人的服务用于商业用途。个人对个人的工作是该类型的中心；共

leaves.name: Penetration Testing Management
leaves.overview:
A **Penetration Testing Management** application is the system of record for offensive security testing organized as managed engagements. It exists to make a penetration test — an authorized, simulated attack against defined systems, carried out by identified testers within bounded rules — into a managed piece of work: scoped and scheduled before it runs, recorded while it runs, and tracked through remediation after it runs.

The problem it solves is specific. A penetration test involves parties who must coordinate but not fully trust each other: the asset owner who authorizes the test, the testers who execute it, and the stakeholders who must fix what is found. Without a shared system, the engagement lives in contracts, spreadsheets, chat threads, and word-processor reports; findings get lost between test and fix, retests are ad hoc, and nobody can show what was tested, what was found, and what was done about it. A PTM application gives the engagement a record, gives its findings a lifecycle, and gives both sides one place to meet.

The defining core is small:

```text
Engagement (scoped, authorized, staffed test undertaking)
└── Findings (evidenced vulnerability records produced by the test)
    └── Lifecycle through remediation verification
        (planned → executed → reported → fixed-and-retested or accepted-risk → closed)
```

Everything else commonly associated with the category — tester marketplaces, continuous testing programs, compliance attestation letters, scanner integrations, AI-assisted report writing — is widespread but not what makes the product a PTM system.
leaves.overview_zh:
一个**渗透测试管理**应用程序是记录有组织进行的攻击性安全测试的系统。它存在的目的是将渗透测试——一种针对已定义系统、由已识别测试员在限定规则内进行的授权模拟攻击——转变为一项管理工作：在执行前进行范围界定和计划安排，在执行过程中记录，并在执行后跟踪直至修复。

它解决的问题是具体的。渗透测试涉及必须协调但不能完全互信的多方：授权测试的资产所有者、执行测试的测试员，以及必须修复发现问题的利益相关者。如果没有共享系统，项目会散落在合同、电子表格、聊天记录和文字处理报告中；发现在测试和修复之间丢失，复测是临时性的，且无人能展示测试了什么、发现了什么以及采取了什么措施。一个 PTM 应用程序为项目提供记录，为发现提供生命周期，并为双方提供一个共同协作的平台。

其定义的核心结构如下：

```text
项目（已界定范围、已授权、已配备人员的测试任务）
└── 发现（测试产生的有证据支持的漏洞记录）
    └── 经历修复验证的生命周期
        （计划 → 执行 → 报告 → 修复并复测 或 接受风险 → 关闭）
```

通常与该类别相关的其他一切——测试员市场、持续测试计划、合规性证明信、扫描器集成、AI辅助报告撰写——都很常见，但并非使该产品成为 PTM 系统的关键。
leaves.dc:
**The engagement.** The unit of record is the engagement — one offensive-security test undertaking. It is persistent and individually identified, and it carries the structures that make an attack test legitimate:

- **Scope** — the targets to be tested (assets such as a web application, API, network range, or cloud environment) and, just as importantly, what is out of scope.
- **Test window** — the bounded period during which testing may occur.
- **Authorization context** — who may test what, under which rules: permitted techniques, knowledge level given to testers, exclusions, and emergency contacts.
- **Assigned testers** — the identified people executing the test, with a lead responsible for the team and the deliverable.

Remove the engagement record and the product becomes a findings tracker or a scheduling tool — there is no test undertaking to manage.

**Findings.** The engagement's security output is the finding: a structured record of one discovered vulnerability, bound to the engagement and to the affected target. A finding carries what was found, where, the evidence that proves it (screenshots, request fragments, proof-of-concept steps), a severity, and remediation guidance. Findings are reviewed before they reach the client — triage and quality review are part of the record, not an afterthought. Remove findings and the product is authorization paperwork with no security result.

**The lifecycle through remediation verification.** The engagement advances through recognizable states — planned, in execution, reported — and its findings are tracked to resolution. A finding is closed in one of two ways: it is fixed and a retest confirms the fix (the retest is recorded against the same finding), or the organization formally accepts the risk. The engagement closes when its findings reach one of those ends. This loop is what turns a one-shot report into management. Remove it and the product is a report generator.
leaves.dc_zh:
**测试任务（Engagement）。** 记录单元是测试任务——一个攻击性安全测试任务。它是持久的且独立标识的，并携带使攻击测试合法化的结构：
- **范围** — 要测试的目标（如Web应用程序、API、网络范围或云环境等资产），同样重要的是，哪些不在范围内。
- **测试窗口** — 测试可能发生的有限期间。
- **授权上下文** — 谁可以在什么规则下测试什么：允许的技术、提供给测试人员的知识级别、排除项和紧急联系人。
- **指派的测试人员** — 执行测试的已识别人员，有一个负责人对团队和交付物负责。

移除测试任务记录，产品就变成发现跟踪器或调度工具——没有测试任务可管理。

**发现。** 测试任务的安全输出是发现：一个已发现漏洞的结构化记录，绑定到测试任务和受影响目标。发现携带了发现的内容、位置、证明它的证据（截图、请求片段、概念验证步骤）、严重性和修复指导。发现在到达客户之前会被审查——分诊和质量审查是记录的一部分，而不是事后想法。移除发现，产品就变成授权文书，没有安全输出。
leaves.rules:
### Authorization bounds the test

Testing happens only against scoped targets within the test window, under the agreed rules. Findings discovered outside scope are flagged as out of scope rather than silently absorbed. Some rules are explicit safety rules: certain destructive techniques (such as denial-of-service testing) are commonly excluded from standard engagements, and testing against third-party services is limited to the integration points, not the third party's own systems.

### Findings are reviewed before they count

A discovered vulnerability typically enters a triage state where it is validated and severity is assigned before it becomes a client-visible finding. Invalid reports are declined, duplicates merged. This review gate is part of the record, protecting both sides from noise and from premature escalation.

### The retest closes the loop

A fix is not "done" until a retest confirms it; a failed retest returns the finding to remediation. Accepting a risk is a formal, recorded alternative to fixing. The engagement stays open until every finding reaches one of these ends.

### Findings are sensitive by nature

A findings corpus is a map of an organization's weaknesses. Access is scoped per engagement and per organization; evidence and reports are handled as confidential data. This is why delivery models that keep data entirely on the buyer's infrastructure exist as a first-class variant, not an edge case.

### Severity is a model, not a measurement

Severity is assigned through a defined rating approach — CVSS-family scoring or impact-and-likelihood rating — applied consistently across testers. Shared findings libraries and review workflows exist precisely so that the same finding gets the same rating regardless of who found it.

### The report is a deliverable with standing

Reports serve audiences beyond the testing team: management, auditors, regulators, customers. Attestation-style deliverables exist because third parties need evidence that independent testing occurred, not just a list of bugs.
leaves.rules_zh:
### 授权限定测试范围

测试仅在时间窗口内针对已界定范围的目标进行，并遵守协商一致的规则。在范围外发现的发现会被标记为超出范围，而不是被悄悄吸收。一些规则是明确的安全规则：某些破坏性技术（如拒绝服务测试）通常在标准项目中被排除，针对第三方服务的测试仅限于集成点，而非第三方自身的系统。

### 发现需经审核后才被计入

一个被发现的漏洞通常会进入一个分类状态，在成为客户可见的发现之前，需要进行验证并分配严重性等级。无效的报告被拒绝，重复的报告被合并。这个审核关卡是记录的一部分，保护双方免受噪音干扰和过早升级。

### 复测闭合回路

修复直到复测确认才算“完成”；复测失败则将发现返回修复阶段。接受风险是修复的正式、已记录的替代方案。项目在每个发现都达到这些终态之一之前保持开放。

### 发现本质上是敏感的

发现集合是一个组织弱点的地图。访问权限按项目和组织限定；证据和报告被视为机密数据处理。这就是为什么数据完全存储在买方基础设施上的交付模式作为一类首选变体存在，而不是边缘情况。

### 严重性是一种模型，而非测量

严重性通过一个定义的评级方法（CVSS系列评分或影响与可能性评级）分配，并在测试员之间保持一致应用。共享的发现库和审核工作流存在的目的，正是为了让同一个发现无论由谁发现都获得相同的评级。

leaves.name: Pension Administration Platform
leaves.overview:
A **Pension Administration Platform** is the system of record and operating system for pension schemes: it maintains a registry of scheme members whose entitlements are governed by the scheme's rules, tracks each member's long-horizon accrual (service and/or contribution history), calculates the benefit due at life events under those rules, and administers the payment of those benefits — recurring retirement income and one-off settlements such as lump sums, transfers, and death benefits.

The defining core is deliberately small:

```text
Scheme (governing rule container)
└── Member (identified person, scheme-governed participation)
    └── Accrual record (service / contribution history → entitlement)
        └── Benefit calculation at life events (under scheme rules)
            └── Benefit payment (recurring income and/or one-off settlement)
```

Everything else commonly associated with these products — member portals, case management, pension payroll machinery, indexation processing, statements, employer portals, regulatory reporting — is standard capability that makes the administration practical, not what makes the product a pension administration platform. Older mainframe-era systems and differently positioned regional products fit the same core without any of the modern surfaces.

The platform's horizon is measured in decades: a member's record typically begins at joining the scheme and remains active through employment, leaving, retirement, and death. This long horizon — and the fact that the entitlement is defined by scheme rules rather than by a commercial contract or an investment account alone — is what separates this Type from its neighbors.
leaves.overview_zh:
**养老金管理平台**是养老金计划的记录系统和操作系统：它维护一个养老金计划成员的注册表，其权益受计划规则管辖，跟踪每个成员的长期积累（服务和/或缴费历史），根据这些规则计算生活事件中应得的福利，并管理这些福利的支付——包括定期退休收入和一次性结算，如一次性支付、转移和死亡福利。

其定义性核心刻意保持小巧：

```text
计划（管理规则容器）
└── 成员（已识别人员，计划管辖的参与）
    └── 积累记录（服务/缴费历史 → 权益）
        └── 生活事件中的福利计算（根据计划规则）
            └── 福利支付（定期收入和/或一次性结算）
```

其他通常与这些产品相关的一切——会员门户、案例管理、养老金工资处理机制、指数化处理、对账单、雇主门户、监管报告——是使管理变得实用的标准能力，而非使产品成为养老金管理平台的核心。较旧的大型机时代系统和不同定位的地区性产品也符合相同的核心，而没有任何现代界面。

该平台的时间跨度以几十年计：成员的记录通常从加入计划开始，并在就业、离职、退休和死亡期间保持活跃。这种长期跨度——以及权益由计划规则而非商业合同或投资账户单独定义的事实——是将此类型与其相邻类型区分开来的关键。
leaves.dc:
Four structures. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as pension administration:

- **Scheme-governed member registry** — members are identified people whose participation is defined by the rules of one or more pension schemes or plans. The scheme — a trust-based occupational scheme, a statutory public plan, a recordkeeping plan — is the governing container: it defines eligibility, accrual, vesting, indexation, survivor benefits, and available payment forms. One platform commonly administers multiple schemes, and one scheme commonly spans multiple sponsoring employers.
- **Long-horizon accrual record** — per member, the history from which entitlement derives: service history and pensionable salary (in defined-benefit schemes), contribution history (in defined-contribution schemes), and the derived entitlement. Records span decades, survive changes of employment, and must be correctable retroactively with effective dates.
- **Rule-based benefit calculation** — computing what a member is entitled to, now or at a future date, from their accrual record under the scheme's rules. In defined-benefit schemes this is formula-based (service, accrual rate, salary, revaluation); in defined-contribution schemes it is the accumulated account value. The rules are the scheme's own — the platform encodes them as configuration, not as fixed behavior.
- **Benefit payment administration** — putting the benefit in the member's hands: recurring retirement-income payments (a pension payroll with gross calculation, tax treatment, bank payment files, and payment advices) and one-off settlements (lump sums, transfers to other schemes, death benefits).
leaves.dc_zh:
四大核心结构。若移除任何一个，该产品将不再被识别为养老金管理平台：

- **方案治理的成员登记册**——成员是已被识别的个人，其参与资格由一项或多项养老金方案或计划的规则所定义。方案——无论是基于信托的职业计划、法定公共计划还是记录保存计划——是治理容器：它定义了资格归属、累积、归属权、指数化调整、遗属福利以及可选支付形式。一个平台通常管理多个方案，而一个方案通常跨越多个参保雇主。

- **长期累积记录**——每位成员的权益源于此记录历史：包括服务年限和养老金薪酬（在待遇确定型计划中）、缴费历史（在缴费确定型计划中），以及由此推导出的权益。记录跨越数十年，不受就业变动影响，且必须支持带有生效日期的追溯更正。

- **基于规则的福利计算**——根据方案规则，从成员的累积记录中计算其当前或未来某个时间点应享有的权益。在待遇确定型计划中，此计算基于公式（服务年限、累积率、薪酬、再估值）；在缴费确定型计划中，则为累积账户价值。规则是方案自身的——平台将其编码为配置项，而非固定行为。

- **福利支付安排**——
leaves.rules:
### Scheme rules are the supreme law

Everything the platform computes is derived from the scheme's own rules — eligibility, accrual, vesting, indexation, survivor benefits, payment forms. The platform encodes these as configuration; two schemes on the same platform can behave differently in every respect except the core model.

### Effective dating and retro-calculation

Records span decades. Rule changes and data corrections carry effective dates, and affected history is recomputed. A backdated salary change or a retroactive scheme-rule amendment must flow through every calculation that depends on it.

### Payment accuracy and overpayment recovery

The recurring payment run is the platform's most sensitive operation. Overpayments create recoverable debts; underpayments create complaints and regulatory exposure. Detection, correction, and recovery of incorrect payments are standing behaviors, not edge cases.

### Tax treatment is mandatory and jurisdiction-specific

Pension payments are taxed according to the regime of the scheme's jurisdiction. The payment run applies this treatment as part of gross-to-net calculation; the platform cannot treat it as optional.

### Long retention and full audit

Records must persist for the member's lifetime and beyond (survivor benefits), with a complete audit trail of changes. Member data protection obligations apply throughout, and outlive the employment relationship.

### Death changes the record's owner, not its existence

On a member's death, the record does not close: dependants' survivor benefits are calculated and paid, sometimes for decades. Dependant records are first-class, not notes on the member record.

### Transfers are guarded movements of entitlement

Moving entitlement between schemes requires value calculation and coordination with the receiving scheme under regime-specific safeguards; platforms treat transfers as controlled cases rather than simple transactions.
leaves.rules_zh:
### 计划规则是最高法律

平台计算的一切都源于计划自身的规则——资格、积累、归属、指数化、幸存者福利、支付形式。平台将这些编码为配置；同一平台上的两个计划可以在除核心模型外的所有方面表现不同。

### 生效日期和追溯计算

记录跨越数十年。规则变更和数据更正带有生效日期，并重新计算受影响的历史。追溯工资变更或追溯计划规则修订必须流经依赖它的每个计算。

### 支付准确性和多付回收

定期支付运行是平台最敏感的操作。多付产生可追回的债务；少付导致投诉和监管风险。检测、更正和回收不正确支付是持续行为，而非边缘案例。

### 税务处理是强制性和司法管辖区特定的

养老金支付根据计划所在司法管辖区的制度征税。支付运行将此处理作为总到净计算的一部分；平台不能将其视为可选。

### 长期保留和完整审计

记录必须在成员的一生中及之后（幸存者福利）持续存在，并具有完整的变更审计跟踪。成员数据保护义务在整个期间适用，并在雇佣关系结束后继续存在。

### 死亡改变记录的所有者，而非其存在

成员死亡时，记录不会关闭：计算并支付受抚养人的幸存者福利，有时长达数十年。受抚养人记录是一等记录，而非成员记录的备注。

leaves.name: People Analytics Platform
leaves.overview:
A **People Analytics Platform** integrates an organization's workforce data from its various source systems into one governed analytical model, and answers workforce questions — about composition, movement, cost, diversity, and outcomes — through metrics, trends, segments, and insights.

The defining core is small:

```text
Integrated workforce data layer (people records + their history)
└── Governed workforce metrics (consistent definitions)
    └── Analytical question → answer loop
        (filter by segment, trend over time, compare, drill)
```

Everything else commonly associated with the category — prebuilt connector libraries, out-of-the-box dashboards, benchmarks, attrition prediction, AI assistants, self-serve distribution to managers — is widespread in mature products but is not what makes the product a people analytics platform. Older warehouse-era HR analytics deployments and suite-embedded analytics modules also satisfy the core without any of those specifics.

The platform is analytical, not operational: it does not process hires, run payroll, or record performance. It reads the records those systems produce and turns them into workforce understanding. When the primary job shifts to running HR transactions, the product is an HRIS/HCM; when it shifts to forward-looking supply/demand planning, it is drifting toward Workforce Planning.
leaves.overview_zh:
一个**人员分析平台**将组织来自其各种源系统的工作人力数据整合到一个受管控的分析模型中，并通过指标、趋势、细分和洞察来回答关于构成、流动、成本、多元化和结果的工作人力问题。

其定义核心很小：

```text
整合的工作人力数据层（人员记录 + 他们的历史）
└── 受管控的工作人力指标（一致的定义）
    └── 分析问题 → 答案循环
        （按细分筛选、随时间趋势、比较、钻取）
```

通常与此类别相关的其他一切——预构建连接器库、开箱即用的仪表板、基准、流失率预测、AI助手、向管理者的自助分发——在成熟产品中普遍存在，但它们并不是该产品成为人员分析平台的核心要素。较旧的仓库时代HR分析部署和套件内嵌分析模块也满足了这些核心定义，而无需具备那些具体功能。

该平台是分析性的，而非运营性的：它不处理招聘、运行工资单或记录绩效。它读取这些系统产生的记录，并将其转化为对工作人力的理解。当主要工作转向运行HR事务时，该产品就是HRIS/HCM；当主要工作转向前瞻性的供需规划时，它就向工作人力规划（Workforce Planning）偏移。
leaves.dc:
**Workforce data layer.** The platform's world is built on the organization's people records: identified employees carrying attributes (role, job, location, manager, demographics, compensation), plus the dated events that happen to them — hires, exits, promotions, transfers, pay changes. Records are integrated from one or more source systems (HRIS, payroll, applicant tracking, engagement surveys, performance, finance) into a single model that preserves history. History is essential: workforce questions are almost always asked about a point in time ("how many people did we have in Engineering last June?"), and people's attributes change as they move.

**Governed workforce metrics.** On top of the data layer sit quantified measures — headcount, hires, exits, turnover rate, internal mobility, span of control, compensation measures, and similar. What makes them analytics rather than spreadsheets is governance: each metric has a managed, shared definition, so that HR and Finance (for example) answer "what is our headcount?" with the same number. Mature products expose these definitions as inspectable, versioned objects rather than buried formulas.

**Segments.** Every workforce question is asked about a slice of the organization: by department, location, manager, tenure band, demographic group, or any attribute in the data layer. Segments are first-class — the same metric is computed for the whole company and for any subgroup.

**Time.** Metrics are computed over time: current state, trends across months and years, and comparisons between periods. The platform's ability to reconstruct the workforce "as of" a past date is a direct consequence of the historical data layer.

**Analytical answer surfaces.** The loop closes in surfaces that present answers: dashboards and storyboards, guided insight views organized around workforce questions, and increasingly conversational answers generated from the governed data.

```text
Source systems (HRIS · payroll · ATS · surveys · performance · finance)
        ↓  integrate
Workforce data layer (people records + events + history)
        ↓  compute
Governed metrics  ×  Segments  ×  Time
        ↓  present
Dashboards · guided insights · conversational answers
        → consumed by leaders, HRBPs, managers
```

leaves.rules:
### Access control is structural, not an add-on

People data is among the most sensitive data an organization holds. Access control in this Type is therefore part of the product's structure: permissions are defined over the data, over analytical content, and over consumption channels. In the most developed implementations, permissions reach row and column level, and access is dynamic — it updates automatically as people move, so a manager's view follows their current team, and compensation or performance data stays protected even as self-serve access expands.

### Metric definitions are governed

The platform's authority rests on one version of the numbers. Definitions of metrics like headcount or turnover are managed objects: changing one is a deliberate, versioned act, not a hidden edit. This is what lets HR and Finance share the same answer.

### Point-in-time semantics

Workforce questions are asked about moments in time. The platform preserves history so that today's report and last year's report both remain answerable, and reorganizations do not silently rewrite the past. Some products compute figures only as of a completed period; others deliver continuously updating data — the cadence varies, the point-in-time requirement does not.

### Data quality gates the answers

Analytics is only as good as the underlying records. Missing or wrong employment dates make turnover uncomputable; hierarchy gaps break manager-level views. Mature products expose data-health tooling and, in some cases, withhold or flag metrics whose inputs are incomplete rather than present misleading numbers.

### Small groups are statistically protected

Workforce analysis routinely slices into small groups, where individuals become identifiable and random variation dominates. Products commonly apply safeguards: minimum group sizes before group-level results are shown, statistical tests before a group is flagged as unusual, and confidentiality protections inherited from survey data. Exact thresholds are product-specific and configurable.

### The platform reads; it does not transact

The platform does not change employment records, approve anything, or execute HR processes. Its outputs are understanding — and, in some products, hand-offs toward planning or action in adjacent systems.
leaves.rules_zh:
### 访问控制是结构性的，而非附加功能

人员数据是组织所持有的最敏感数据之一。因此，此类型中的访问控制是产品结构的一部分：权限被定义在数据之上、分析内容之上以及消费渠道之上。在最成熟的实现中，权限可达行级和列级，且访问是动态的——它随人员变动自动更新，因此管理者的视图会跟随其当前团队，而薪酬或绩效数据即使在自助访问扩展时也能保持受保护。

### 指标定义是受管控的

平台的权威性建立在数字的单一版本之上。像员工总数或流失率这样的指标定义是受管理的对象：更改定义是一个深思熟虑的、带版本的操作，而非隐式编辑。这就是为什么人力资源和财务部门可以共享相同答案的原因。

### 特定时间点语义

工作人力问题是关于特定时间点提出的。平台保留历史，以便今天的报告和去年的报告都可以回答，并且重组不会悄悄改写过去。一些产品仅在完整周期结束后计算数据；其他产品提供持续更新的数据——节奏不同，但特定时间点的要求不变。

### 数据质量决定答案

分析质量取决于底层记录的好坏。缺失或错误的雇佣日期使得流失率无法计算；层级缺口会破坏按经理级别的视图。成熟产品提供数据健康工具，并且在某些情况下，会隐瞒或标记输入不完整的指标，而不是呈现误导性数字。

### 小型群体受到统计保护

leaves.name: Performance & Attribution Platform
leaves.overview:
A **Performance & Attribution Platform** is the investment industry's measurement and explanation system for realized portfolio results. It maintains a population of measured portfolios, computes their returns period by period from holdings, valuations and cash flows, evaluates those returns against defined references (benchmarks, targets or peer structures), decomposes the difference into named and quantified effects — such as allocation, security selection, currency and factor effects — and packages the results as reports and data extracts for stakeholders.

It answers two questions that portfolio record-keeping alone cannot: **how did the portfolio actually perform**, and **why did it perform the way it did** — which decisions, segments or exposures produced the result relative to the reference.

The defining core is small: measured portfolios, periodic return measurement, a comparison reference, attribution decomposition, and results delivered for consumption. Everything else commonly associated with the category — composite management, GIPS support, factor and fixed-income attribution models, risk measures, managed-service delivery — is mature structure that makes the platform practical, not what makes it a performance & attribution platform.
leaves.overview_zh:
**绩效与归因平台**是投资行业对已实现投资组合结果的衡量和解释系统。它维护一组被衡量的投资组合，根据持仓、估值和现金流逐期计算其回报率，将这些回报率与定义的参考基准（基准、目标或同行结构）进行评估，将差异分解为已命名和量化的效应——例如资产配置、证券选择、货币和因子效应——并将结果打包为报告和数据摘录供利益相关者使用。

它回答了仅靠投资组合记录保存无法解决的两个问题：**投资组合的实际表现如何**，以及**为什么表现如此**——相对于参考基准，哪些决策、细分或敞口产生了结果。

定义核心很小：被衡量的投资组合、定期回报衡量、比较参考基准、归因分解和交付使用的结果。与该类别通常关联的其他所有内容——组合管理、GIPS支持、因子和固定收益归因模型、风险管理措施、托管服务交付——都是使平台实用的成熟结构，而非使其成为绩效与归因平台的因素。
leaves.dc: - **Results surfaced for stakeholder consumption** — computed results reach their audience as reports, dashboards or data extracts. Without this, the calculations never fulfill the Type's purpose.
leaves.dc_zh: - **为利益相关者消费而呈现的结果** — 计算出的结果通过报告、仪表板或数据提取的形式到达其受众。如果没有这一点，计算就永远无法实现该类型的目的。
leaves.rules:
### Results inherit the quality of upstream data

The platform measures data produced elsewhere. Validation, reconciliation and audit trails are structural, not cosmetic: a performance number published on bad data is a professional liability, and mature products treat data quality control as a first-class workflow.

### Comparisons must be computed on a consistent basis

Portfolio and reference returns must be produced with the same period boundaries, currency treatment and cash-flow handling. Products maintain this consistency as a core discipline; blended and custom benchmarks exist precisely to keep the comparison meaningful.

### Attribution effects reconcile to the difference

The decomposition is expected to add back up to the excess return being explained. Where effects do not reconcile (for example, around currency, trading or pricing effects in fixed income), products split out or isolate those effects explicitly.

### Structures drive everything

Hierarchies, composites and benchmark assignments are configuration, not per-run choices. Changing a structure changes what every subsequent result means — which is why structure management is an administrative surface with controlled access.

### The process is controlled and auditable

Performance results feed client reporting, marketing claims and oversight decisions. Mature products therefore run the measurement process with roles, permissions, approval-style review and audit trails, and support standards-driven presentation (GIPS-style composites) where the market requires it.

### Restatement is part of the loop

When input data is corrected or a reference changes, results can be recomputed and republished; the audited history of what was produced and when is part of the record.
leaves.rules_zh:
### 结果继承上游数据的质量

平台衡量在其他地方产生的数据。验证、协调和审计跟踪是结构性的，而非装饰性的：基于糟糕数据发布的绩效数字是专业责任，成熟产品将数据质量控制视为一流工作流程。

### 比较必须在一致的基础上计算

投资组合和参考基准回报率必须在相同期间边界、货币处理和现金流处理下产生。产品将此一致性作为核心纪律；混合和自定义基准正是为了保持比较有意义。

### 归因效应与差异协调一致

分解预期加回正在解释的超额回报率。当效应不协调时（例如，在固定收益的货币、交易或定价效应周围），产品明确分离或隔离这些效应。

### 结构驱动一切

层次结构、复合和基准分配是配置，而非每次运行的选择。更改结构会更改每个后续结果的含义——这就是为什么结构管理是一个具有受控访问权限的管理界面。

### 过程受控且可审计

绩效结果馈送客户报告、营销声明和监督决策。因此，成熟产品使用角色、权限、审批式审查和审计跟踪来运行衡量过程，并在市场需要时支持标准驱动的展示（GIPS风格的复合）。

### 重述是循环的一部分

当输入数据被更正或参考基准更改时，结果可以重新计算和重新发布；经审计的生成历史和时间记录是记录的一部分。

leaves.name: Performance Management Platform
leaves.overview:
A **Performance Management Platform** is an HR application an organization uses to run structured assessments of its employees' performance. It operates on the organization's roster of employees, organizes assessments into defined occasions (review cycles), has identified evaluators — the employee's manager, the employee, selected peers, direct reports — complete a structured evaluation record for each person being reviewed, and carries each record through a controlled lifecycle to a released, acknowledged, and durably kept outcome.

The defining structure is deliberately small:

```text
Organization-defined employee population
└── Assessment occasion (review cycle)
    └── Structured evaluation record per employee
        └── Attributed evaluators in roles relative to the employee
            (self / manager / peer / direct report)
            └── Tracked lifecycle to a completed, released, durable outcome
```

Everything else commonly associated with the category — rating scales, competency libraries, calibration sessions and 9-box matrices, goal and OKR linkage, continuous check-ins and feedback, AI-drafted reviews, compensation handoffs — is widely supported by mature products but is not what makes the platform what it is. Older appraisal processes (paper forms, appraisals embedded in HR systems) fit the same defining structure without any of those features.

When the core shifts to setting and aligning goals without evaluating people, the product becomes an OKR / Goal Management Platform; when it measures populations anonymously rather than evaluating identified individuals, it becomes an Employee Engagement or Survey Platform.
leaves.overview_zh:
一个**绩效管理平台**是组织用于对员工绩效进行结构化评估的人力资源应用程序。它基于组织的员工名册运作，将评估组织到特定的场合（评审周期）中，指定评估者——员工的经理、员工本人、选定的同事、直接下属——为每位被评审者完成一份结构化的评估记录，并通过一个受控的生命周期，将每份记录推进到最终发布、确认并永久保存的结果。

其核心定义性结构是刻意保持精简的：

```text
组织定义的员工群体
└── 评估场合（评审周期）
    └── 每位员工的结构化评估记录
        └── 相对于员工的不同角色的评估者
            （自我 / 经理 / 同事 / 直接下属）
            └── 跟踪至完成、发布、持久保存结果的生命周期
```

其他通常与该类别相关联的一切——评分量表、胜任力库、校准会议和九宫格矩阵、目标与OKR关联、持续签到与反馈、AI草拟的评审意见、薪酬数据传递——成熟的产品普遍支持这些功能，但它们并非定义该平台本质的要素。早期的评估流程（纸质表格、嵌入HR系统的评估）同样符合此定义性结构，即使不具备这些功能。

当核心重点从评估人员转向设定和对齐目标时，该产品就变成了OKR / 目标管理平台；当它以匿名方式测量群体而非评估特定个体时，它就变成了员工敬业度或调研平台。
leaves.dc:
**Employee population.** The platform operates on the organization's identified employees as the population being assessed. It is organization-scoped: who is in scope, who reports to whom, and who joined or left are facts the platform inherits from the organization, normally via HRIS or org-structure integration.

**Review cycle.** The assessment occasion is the central unit of work. A cycle defines who is being reviewed, the timeline, which evaluation directions are in play, which template applies, and how results will be released. Cycles are created and administered by HR administrators; many products also support automated or scheduled cycles (for example, triggered by tenure milestones) and smaller occasions outside the main cadence (project-based reviews, new-hire assessments).

**Evaluation record.** For each reviewee in a cycle, the platform holds a structured record: a set of questions or criteria — typically narrative prompts, competency ratings, or both — answered on a template the organization configures. This record is the durable artifact of the assessment.

**Attributed evaluators.** Every evaluation response is written by an identified person standing in a defined role relative to the reviewee:

- **self** — the employee assesses their own performance;
- **downward / manager** — the manager assesses the direct report;
- **peer** — colleagues assess the employee, usually through a nomination-and-approval step;
- **upward** — direct reports assess their manager.

The reviewer graph is derived from the organization's reporting structure plus peer selection; a person's role relative to the reviewee determines what they are asked and what they may see. This attribution — named people accountable for judgments about named people — is what separates this type from anonymous survey tools.

**Tracked lifecycle to a released outcome.** Evaluations are not free-floating documents. The platform tracks each one from assignment through drafting and submission, monitors completion across the cycle, and only then releases results — an explicit act under administrator or manager control — after which the record is finalized, typically acknowledged by the reviewee, and kept as part of the person's performance history.

Remove any one of these five and the product is no longer a performance management platform: without the population it is a survey tool; without the occasion, a feedback tool; without the structured record, a meeting-notes tool; without attributed evaluators, an analytics dashboard; without the lifecycle, a form builder.
leaves.dc_zh:
**员工群体。** 平台以组织内已识别的员工为评估对象。其范围与组织绑定：平台继承组织的结构事实（如人员归属、汇报关系、入职离职），通常通过人力资源信息系统或组织结构集成实现。

**评估周期。** 评估活动是核心工作单元。一个周期定义评估对象、时间安排、评估维度、适用模板及结果发布方式。周期由人力资源管理员创建管理；多数产品还支持自动化/定时周期（如基于司龄触发）以及主节奏外的小型评估（项目评估、新员工评估）。

**评估记录。** 平台为周期内的每位被评估者保存结构化记录：基于组织配置的模板，包含一组叙事性提示、胜任力评级或两者兼有的问题/标准。此记录是评估的持久化成果。

**归责评估者。** 每份评估回复由与被评估者存在明确角色关系的实名人员撰写：
- **自评** — 员工自我评估；
- **向下评估/管理者评估** — 管理者评估直属下属；
- **同级评估** — 同事互评；
leaves.rules:
### Results are withheld until explicitly released

Across the researched sample, review content is not visible to the reviewee (or broadly to the organization) until an authorized person shares it. Release is a distinct, logged act — followed by acknowledgment and finalization. This is one of the most characteristic behaviors of the type: the platform is designed around confidentiality of in-progress judgments.

### Role determines reach

A manager sees and acts on their direct reports' reviews; not on others'. Broader visibility (HR, executives, skip-level managers, designated "review viewers") exists but is granted explicitly. Exports and reports are similarly role-restricted. The reporting structure is therefore both the source of the reviewer graph and the access-control boundary.

### Peer feedback is mediated

Peer reviews pass through a nomination-and-approval workflow before anyone writes them, and the person sharing final results typically controls which peer answers are included and in what form. Peer review content is treated as sensitive input to the manager's summary, not as an automatically published document.

### The reviewer graph is fixed for the duration of a cycle

Once a cycle is created (in some products, at creation; in others, at launch), the set of people being reviewed and who reviews whom is stabilized, so that assessments are comparable and complete. Mid-cycle changes are possible but are administrator operations with traceable effects — not silent reassignments.

### Submission is a state change with consequences

A submitted evaluation typically stops being freely editable; edits afterwards require reopening mechanisms (employee request → manager/admin approval, or administrator action), and finalized results are locked further. Cycles themselves can be extended, locked, and (in some products) audited end to end.

### Calibration adjusts, it does not replace

Where calibration is used, the calibrated rating — not the original submitted one — becomes the rating of record for onward use. The adjustment is itself recorded.
leaves.rules_zh:
### 在明确发布前结果保密

在所研究的样本中，评审内容对被评审者（或对组织内其他成员）不可见，直到授权人员将其共享。发布是一个独立且被记录的操作——随后是确认和定稿。这是该类型最典型的特征之一：平台的设计围绕进行中评审的保密性展开。

### 角色决定可见范围

经理可以查看和处理其直接下属的评审；不能处理他人的。更广泛的可见性（HR、高管、越级经理、指定的“评审查看者”）存在，但需被明确授予。导出和报表同样受角色限制。因此，汇报结构既是评审者关系图的来源，也是访问控制的边界。

### 同事反馈经过中介流程

同事评审在任何人撰写之前，会经过提名和审批工作流，而最终结果共享者通常控制哪些同事的回答被包含以及以何种形式包含。同事评审内容被视为经理总结性评审的敏感输入，而非自动发布的文档。

### 评审者关系图在周期内固定

一旦周期创建完成（在某些产品中是创建时，另一些是启动时），被评审者的集合以及谁评审谁的关系就稳定下来，以确保评估具有可比性和完整性。周期中期的变更是可能的，但属于会产生可追溯影响的管理员操作——而非静默的重新分配。

### 提交会引发状态变更并产生后续影响

提交的评估通常会停止自由编辑；后续的编辑需要重新打开机制（员工申请 → 经理/管理员批准，或管理员操作），而定稿的结果会被进一步锁定。周期内的评审内容

leaves.name: Performance Testing Application
leaves.overview:
A **Performance Testing Application** is the software a team uses to learn how its own system behaves under controlled, simulated demand — the tooling of the performance-testing discipline: evaluating a system's speed, stability, and scalability under workload, before real users depend on it.

The discipline is practiced through a family of workload-shaped test types — load, stress, soak (endurance), spike, volume/scalability, and breakpoint (capacity) testing — but every one of them is the same underlying act: run a modeled population of simulated users against a target system, shape that population over time, and measure how the system responds. The products built for this purpose are marketed under both the "performance testing" and "load testing" names — vendor sites routinely pair the terms in product titles and menus — because they form one product category: the discipline name and the method name for the same tooling.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Load scenario of record      (what each simulated user does)
+ Controlled simulated population   (how much demand, shaped over time)
+ Measured execution against the target   (how the system responds under load)
= performance result sets that can be analyzed, compared, and judged
```

The canonical boundary: the target is the team's own system in a test or staging context, and the load is deliberately heavy enough to be informative — sometimes destructive. When the surface becomes single-user journey verdicts, it is end-to-end testing; when it becomes minimal-load scheduled probes of production, it is synthetic monitoring; when it observes the running application from inside its own process, it is APM or profiling.
leaves.overview_zh:
一个**性能测试应用**是团队用来了解其自身系统在受控模拟需求下如何运行的软件——性能测试学科的工具：在真实用户依赖系统之前，评估系统在负载下的速度、稳定性和可扩展性。

该学科通过一系列负载形状的测试类型来实践——负载测试、压力测试、耐力测试（持久性）、尖峰测试、容量/可扩展性测试和断点（容量）测试——但它们都是同一个基本行为：针对目标系统运行模拟用户的建模群体，随时间塑造该群体，并测量系统的响应方式。为此目的构建的产品以“性能测试”和“负载测试”两个名称进行营销——供应商网站通常在产品标题和菜单中配对这些术语——因为它们形成一个产品类别：相同工具的学科名称和方法名称。

其定义结构较小：

```text
记录的负载场景      (每个模拟用户所做的操作)
+ 受控模拟群体   (需求量，随时间调整)
+ 针对目标的度量执行   (系统在负载下的响应方式)
= 可分析、比较和评判的性能结果集
```

典型边界：目标是团队自身在测试或预发布环境中的系统，负载被故意设置得足够重以提供信息——有时具有破坏性。当表面成为单用户旅程评判时，它是端到端测试；当表面成为对生产环境的最小负载定时探测时，它是合成监控；当从运行应用程序的内部过程观察时，它是APM或分析。
leaves.dc:
| Test type | Population shape | Question it answers |
|---|---|---|
| Smoke | minimal load, short | does the scenario work and the system respond correctly at all? |
| Load (average) | expected production level, sustained | does the system maintain performance under normal use? |
| Stress | above average | how does the system manage as load exceeds the expected average? |
| Soak / endurance | average level, hours-long | does the system degrade, leak, or destabilize over time? |
| Spike | sudden very high bursts | does the system survive and recover from sudden peaks? |
| Breakpoint / capacity | gradually increased until failure | where are the system's actual limits? |

Vendor documentation is candid that the names of these types are not standardized and that the boundaries are relative to each system's use case — a stress test for one system is an average-load test for another. The types are a shared vocabulary for shaping the population, not separate product capabilities.
leaves.dc_zh:
| 测试类型 | 负载模式 | 回答的问题 |
|---|---|---|
| 冒烟测试 | 最小负载，短时间 | 该场景是否工作，系统是否正确响应？ |
| 负载测试（平均） | 预期生产水平，持续 | 系统在正常使用下是否保持性能？ |
| 压力测试 | 高于平均 | 当负载超过预期平均时，系统如何管理？ |
| 耐久性测试 | 平均水平，长时间 | 系统是否随时间退化、泄漏或不稳定？ |
| 峰值测试 | 突然的高峰 | 系统是否能从突然的峰值中存活并恢复？ |
| 断点测试 | 逐渐增加直到失败 | 系统的实际极限在哪里？ |
leaves.rules:
- **Results are only valid if the load was actually delivered.** A failed or under-provisioned load generator means the target never experienced the intended pressure — the run is invalid and must be re-run. Monitoring the generators themselves is part of the discipline.
- **The run is destructive by design.** Heavy runs can crash the target; limit-finding runs are *meant* to find the failure point. This is why the target should be a test/staging environment, why elasticity may need to be disabled when hunting limits, and why small validation runs come first.
- **The population model changes the meaning of a run.** In a closed model, a fixed user population iterates — if the system slows, the offered load drops. In an open model, arrivals continue at the defined rate regardless — slowdowns pile up. The two answer different questions; products expose both.
- **Functional failure feeds the performance verdict.** Non-2xx responses and failed assertions count into the error rate; a performance pass with a broken system is not a pass.
- **Verdicts are codified expectations.** Thresholds, SLAs, and baselines turn measurements into pass/fail decisions; without them, judgment is manual. The concept is universal in modern products; the specific mechanisms vary.
- **Test types are relative, not absolute.** The same population shape is a stress test for one system and an average-load test for another; the names are a shared vocabulary, not standardized categories.
leaves.rules_zh:
- **只有当负载实际交付时，结果才有效。** 失败或供应不足的负载生成器意味着目标从未经历预期的压力——该运行无效，必须重新运行。监控生成器本身是该学科的一部分。
- **运行是破坏性的设计。** 重负载运行可能使目标崩溃；限制查找运行旨在找到故障点。这就是为什么目标应该是测试/预发布环境，为什么在查找限制时可能需要禁用弹性，以及为什么小验证运行先行。
- **群体模型改变运行的含义。** 在封闭模型中，固定用户群体迭代——如果系统变慢，提供的负载就下降。在开放模型中，到达率无论是否减速都按定义速率继续——减速会堆积。两者回答不同的问题；产品都提供。
- **功能失败影响性能评判。** 非2xx响应和失败断言计入错误率；一个系统损坏但性能通过的评判不是通过。
- **评判是编码的期望。** 阈值、SLA和基线将测量转化为通过/失败决策；没有它们，评判是手动的。这个概念在现代产品中是通用的；具体机制有所不同。
- **测试类型是相对的，而不是绝对的。** 相同的群体形状对一个系统是压力测试，对另一个系统是平均负载测试；名称是共享词汇，而不是标准化类别。

leaves.name: Performing Arts Organization Management
leaves.overview:
A **Performing Arts Organization Management** application is an arts organization's audience-and-revenue system of record. It holds one unified database of the organization's patrons, sells admission to the organization's own performances and events through its own channels (box office and online), and runs the ongoing relationship loop — fundraising, memberships, and targeted communication — over the transaction history those sales and donations create.

The defining structure is the combination of three things in one system:

```text
Unified patron record
└── Ticketing for the organization's own events (box office + online)
    └── Recorded transactions feeding the relationship loop
        └── Fundraising / membership / marketing over the patron base
```

Remove the unified patron relationship and the product becomes a ticketing platform; remove ticketing and it becomes a donor CRM; remove the relationship loop and it becomes a bare box office terminal. The Type is defined by holding all three together for the organization's own audience.
leaves.overview_zh:
一个**表演艺术组织管理**应用是艺术组织用于管理观众与收入的官方系统。它维护着一个统一的组织赞助人数据库，通过自有渠道（售票处和在线）销售其自身演出和活动的入场券，并基于这些销售与捐赠产生的交易历史，持续运营关系维护循环——包括筹款、会员管理和定向沟通。

其核心定义在于将以下三者融合于一个系统中：

```text
统一的赞助人记录
└── 为组织自有活动售票（售票处 + 在线）
    └── 记录的交易驱动关系维护循环
        └── 基于赞助人基础进行筹款/会员/营销活动
```

移除统一的赞助人关系，该产品就变成了一个票务平台；移除售票功能，它就变成了一个捐赠者CRM；移除关系维护循环，它就变成了一个简易的售票终端。该类型的定义在于为组织自有观众将这三者完整地结合在一起。
leaves.dc: One persistent record per audience member sits at the center. Everything the person does with the organization attaches to it: ticket purchases, donations, memberships, subscriptions, communications received, contact preferences. The record is the join point between departments — the box office, the development office, and marketing all see (their permitted view of) the same person. Mature products provide customer lists, tags, and segmentation built on this record.
leaves.dc_zh: 每个观众成员都有一个持久记录位于中心。此人与组织的所有互动都附加到记录上：票务购买、捐赠、会员资格、订阅、接收的通信、联系偏好。该记录是部门之间的连接点——票房、发展办公室和市场部门都看到同一个人的（他们被允许查看的）视图。成熟的产品基于此记录提供客户列表、标签和细分。
leaves.rules:
- **One person, one record.** The system's value depends on purchases, gifts, and communications resolving to the same patron; duplicate handling and record merging are structural concerns.
- **The patron history is the asset.** Ticketing history is deliberately retained and reused for fundraising and marketing; the system is not a pass-through seller.
- **Contact preferences are enforced.** Patron communication choices (opt-ins/opt-outs) govern what marketing may be sent — a structural rule, not an afterthought.
- **Sales channels share one inventory and one record.** Box office and online sales draw on the same event configuration and write to the same patron database.
- **Exchanges and returns are normal operations**, not exceptions — subscription holders routinely swap performance dates.
- Exact numeric limits, fee structures, and tax handling (e.g., charitable-gift tax relief) vary by product and jurisdiction and are not standardized across the Type.
leaves.rules_zh:
- **一人一记录。** 系统的价值取决于购买、捐赠和沟通能否解析到同一个赞助人；重复项处理和记录合并是结构性考量。
- **赞助人历史是核心资产。** 票务历史被有意识地保留并用于筹款和营销；该系统不是一个简单的销售过账工具。
- **联系偏好必须强制执行。** 赞助人的沟通选择（同意/拒绝接收）决定了可以发送何种营销信息——这是一项结构性规则，而非事后补充。
- **销售渠道共享同一库存和同一记录。** 售票处和在线销售基于同一活动配置进行，并写入同一赞助人数据库。
- **换票和退票是常规操作**，而非异常情况——订阅者通常会更换演出日期。
- 确切的数字限制、费用结构和税务处理（例如，慈善捐赠税收减免）因产品和司法管辖区而异，在该类型内并非标准化。

leaves.name: Performing Rights Management
leaves.overview:
A **Performing Rights Management** application is the collective-administration system of a performing rights organization — the society (PRO/CMO) that stands between music users and rights holders. It keeps the registry of the works or recordings the society represents, attributes observed and reported public performances to the rights holders behind them, and runs the loop that licenses music users, collects licence fees, and distributes them as royalties under published rules.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Rights holders (writers / publishers / artists / owners)
└── Represented repertoire of record
    │     (works or recordings, with shares — administered, not owned)
    ├── Usage-to-rights-holder attribution chain
    │     (census or sample evidence → matched to the registry → attributed per shares)
    └── Collective licensing-and-distribution loop
          (license music users → collect fees → deduct costs → distribute royalties)
```

Everything else commonly associated with societies — member portals, licensee portals, fingerprinting monitoring, cue sheets, setlist programs, international reciprocity, public repertory search — is standard equipment of mature implementations, not what makes the system a performing rights management system. A century-old society running on paper membership cards, broadcaster cue sheets, sample logbooks, and clerk-calculated distributions satisfies the same definition.

When the subject narrows to one rights owner's own catalog and contracts, the product is a different Application Type (Music Publishing Management). When the money loop disappears and only the data remains, it is a registry or a monitoring service, not this Type.
leaves.overview_zh:
一个**表演权管理**应用程序是表演权组织的集体管理系统——该组织是介于音乐用户和权利持有人之间的协会（PRO/CMO）。它维护协会所代表作品或录音的登记册，将观察和报告的公共表演归于其背后的权利持有人，并运行一个循环：为音乐用户发放许可证、收取许可证费用，并根据已发布的规则将这些费用作为版税进行分配。

核心结构很简单：

```text
权利持有人（作者/出版商/艺术家/所有者）
└── 代表的曲库登记
    │     （作品或录音，包含份额——是管理的，而非拥有的）
    ├── 使用情况到权利持有人的归属链
    │     （普查或样本证据 → 与登记册匹配 → 按份额归属）
    └── 集体许可与分配循环
          （为音乐用户发放许可证 → 收取费用 → 扣除成本 → 分配版税）
```

通常与协会相关的其他所有内容——成员门户、被许可方门户、指纹识别监控、提示表、曲目单计划、国际互惠、公开曲库搜索——是成熟实现的标配，而非定义该系统为表演权管理系统的要素。一个依靠纸质会员卡、广播提示表、样本日志和人工计算分配运营了百年的协会，同样符合这个定义。

当主题缩小到单个权利持有人自己的目录和合同时，产品是另一个应用类型（音乐出版管理）。当资金循环消失而只有数据保留时，它就是一个登记册或监控服务，而非此类型。
leaves.dc:
